On Mount Nārada, he performed penance, intent on meditation upon Hari,
beholding Śrī Kṛṣṇa seated within the lotus of his heart as a sphere of light.
He constantly beheld the charming [Kṛṣṇa] together with Rādhā within his meditation;
however, once during the night, while he was in the midst of meditation, Kṛṣṇa had not arrived.
Having practiced meditation again and again, the great sage became weary;
rising from his meditation, that sage was yearning for a vision of Kṛṣṇa.
The sage went to the hermitage of Nārāyaṇa, adorned with groves of Badarī trees;
however, he did not see there the divine Hari, the sage Nara-Nārāyaṇa.
Then, greatly amazed, the brahmin went to the Lokāloka mountain;
however, he did not see the thousand-headed god there at all.
There he asked his attendants, "Where has the Blessed One gone from here?
and when they replied, "We do not know," the sage was then dejected in mind. (35)
He went to the divine Śvetadvīpa, adorned by the Ocean of Milk;
yet even there, upon the couch of Śeṣa, he did not see Hari again.
Then the sage, with a dejected mind yet his face bristling with joy from love, asked the attendants there, "Where has the Blessed One gone from here? (37)
"O sir, we do not know; the sage has been told [of our arrival] and is now absorbed in thought.
What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can I obtain a sight of him? (38)
Speaking thus, he who travels by mind then reached Vaikuṇṭha;
however, he did not see the Lord of Gods there, nor Ramā, the resident of Vaikuṇṭha.
O King, he was not seen there among the devotees by the sage Asuri;
thereafter, that lord of sages and lord of yogis departed for Goloka.
In Vṛndāvana and even in the groves, the sage did not see the Supreme Being; then, distressed by separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he became dejected in mind.
He asked his attendants there, "Where has the Blessed One gone from here?
The attendants replied to him, "The cowherds [have gone] to the beautiful egg of Vāmana."
"Where Pṛśnigarbha was born, there the Blessed One himself [is present].
Having been told this, Āsuri arrived at that very egg. || 43 ||
Not seeing Hari, the sage set forth and reached Kailāsa;
there he found Mahādeva stationed, entirely absorbed in meditation upon Kṛṣṇa.
Having bowed, the great sage, his mind distressed that night, questioned him;
Āsuri said:
"O Blessed One, the entire universe has been seen by me here and there."
Wandering from Goloka as far as Vaikuṇṭha,
desiring a sight of Him, I did not obtain a vision of the God of gods anywhere.
Śrī Mahādeva said: O Brahmin among the Asuras, you are blessed; you are a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, free from worldly motives.
O great sage, I know that you have undergone this exertion out of a desire to see [Him]. (47)
Just as the organs of action [perceive] tastes and so forth,
so too do sages possessed of desire experience that pleasure which people expect only slightly.
It is hidden, supreme, and characterized by the absence of qualities (nirguṇa). || 48 ||
He who went in haste from all sides to liberate the swan-like sage fallen into suffering within the great ocean—
by him, this very day in the forest of Vṛndāvana, along with his companions, [the swan has been rescued].
The Lord of Rasikas himself performs the rāsa dance. || 49 ||
O Sage, the night has been made six months long today by the best of gods through his own power;
I shall go there to see that very thing.
Go yourself quickly, according to your desire.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Narrative of Āsuri," within the Rāsa-krīḍā section of the Vṛndāvana-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā.
Śrī Nārada said: Having reflected thus in his mind, Śiva, together with Āsuri,
both went to the region of Vraja for the purpose of beholding Kṛṣṇa.
Beholding that divine land, adorned with clusters of arbors formed by celestial trees, creepers, and shrubs, the two of them went near the Kālindī.
The women residing in Goloka, who were gatekeepers stationed on the path, possessed great strength and held canes in their hands; standing there, they forcibly forbade him from proceeding.
They both said, "We have arrived, longing for a sight of Kṛṣṇa.
O tiger among kings, the female gatekeepers standing on the path spoke to them. (4)
The female gatekeepers said:
"O twice-born ones, we are stationed here by Kṛṣṇa in numbers of millions upon millions to form a protective circle on all sides, constantly guarding the rāsa dance."
There is one person, Kṛṣṇa, in the secluded circle of the Rāsa dance;
no other ever enters the private assembly of the cowherd girls anywhere except him.
If you two desire to see his bathing in the Mānasa lake,
then go there quickly, O sages, having assumed the state of cowherd women.
Śrī Nārada said:
Having been addressed thus, the sage and Śiva bathed in Lake Mānasa,
and suddenly assuming the form of cowherd girls, they went to the circle of the Rāsa dance.
In that beautiful and auspicious place, the ground was inlaid with gold and rubies,
and it was covered by clusters of mādhavī creepers and kadamba trees.
It was illuminated by the moonlight of the spring season, perfected in every artistry,
and resplendent with jeweled staircases and balconies along the Yamunā.
It resounded with the warbling of peacocks, swans, gallinules, and cuckoos,
and was beautified by the sprouts of trees swaying in the cool breezes from the Yamunā.
It was surrounded by the corridors of the assembly hall, rows of pillars in the courtyards,
and golden jars with divine luster from which banners were fluttering.
The area was filled with clusters of white and reddish flowers, with pathways leading to the Flower Temple,
pervaded by the humming of bees, and resonant with the sweet sounds of musical instruments.
It was made fragrant on all sides by a cool, most meritorious breeze that moved slowly over the thousand-petaled lotuses.
In that bower, Śrī Kṛṣṇa was adorned by Rādhā, who possessed the luster of ten million moons, who was like a lotus, and who moved with the grace of a swan.
He is eternally surrounded by jewels among women, standing in the center of the circle of the dance (rāsa-maṇḍala),
possessing the beauty of ten million Cupids, with a dark and handsome form.
Holding a flute, clad in yellow garments, with a cane in his hand, he is enchanting;
marked with the Śrīvatsa, adorned with the Kaustubha gem, and resplendent with a forest garland.
Adorned with tinkling anklets, bracelets, and a girdle, as well as necklaces, bangles, and a pair of earrings bright as the rising sun; || 18 ||
He wore a crown resembling ten million moons; he was the delighter of Nandana, and with his side-long glances, he was skilled at stealing the hearts of women.
O King, O best of monarchs, while all the cowherd folk looked on, the two demonesses were seen from afar with their palms joined in reverence.
Having bowed at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the two, overwhelmed with joy, spoke. They both said:
"O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa! O Great Yogin, God of gods, Lord of the universe! (21)
O lotus-eyed one, O Govinda, O you whose banner bears Garuḍa, salutations to you!
O Janārdana, O Lord of the World, O Padmanābha, O Trivikrama, O Dāmodara, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Vāsudeva, let there be salutation to you! 22.
O Lord, this very day may You become manifest as the Supreme Perfection for the welfare of the virtuous and to remove the heavy burden of the earth;
for having made Your own entire realm completely empty, You have arrived at the house of Nanda, You who are beyond the beyond.

Endowed with parts, sub-parts, and minute portions that are delightful through their intense and full abundance of ecstatic immersion, you, the most perfect Supreme Being yourself, sustain the entire universe, adorn the essence of aesthetic flavor, and grace Vṛndāvana. 24.
O Lord of Goloka, Sovereign of the King of Mountains, Supreme Lord, Master of Vṛndāvana, whose divine pastimes are eternally performed;
O Consort of Rādhā, whose fame is sung by the women of Vraja!
O Govinda, O Lord of Gokula, may victory indeed be yours! || 25 ||
O glorious one, you are the springtime of the vine of Nikuñja; you are the ornament for the heart and neck of Śrī Rādhikā;
you are the lord of the circle of the Śrī Rāsa dance and the sovereign of the realm of Vraja.
You are the protector of the earth within the sphere of the cosmic egg. || 26 ||
Śrī Nārada said: Then the blessed Lord Hari, accompanied by Rādhā, being pleased,
spoke to the sage with a gentle smile and in a voice as deep as a thundercloud.
For sixty thousand years you two performed penance; by that, a vision of me has been attained by you both, who are entirely free from worldly desire.
"He who is without possessions, who is peaceful, and whose enemy is unborn—he is my friend.
Therefore, let the desired boon be chosen by you both in your minds. (29)
Śiva and Asurī said:
"O Infinite One, let there be obeisance to your lotus feet, which always dwell in the midst of Vṛndāvana.
No other thought pleases us; we offer obeisance to you both, Hari and Rādhikā. (30)
Śrī Nārada said:
Having spoken thus, O King, the Blessed One [resided] in the enchanting forest of Vṛndāvana,
near the Yamunā, adorned with the circle of the Rāsa dance.
Near the bower, on the sandy bank close to the bamboo grove,
Śiva, the sage who is the enemy of the Asuras, made his eternal dwelling.
Then Kṛṣṇa performed the Rāsa-līlā in the forest of Padmākara,
which was filled with bees and possessed fragrant pollen falling from the flowers, accompanied by the gopīs.
In this way, O King of Mithilā, Kṛṣṇa made the night six months long during the rāsa-līlā of the gopīs.
It passed away as happily as a single moment. || 34 ||
At the time of sunrise, O King, all the women of Vraja, their desires fulfilled, went to their own homes in groups.
The son of Nanda went directly to the illustrious abode of Nanda;
meanwhile, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu quickly proceeded to the city of Vṛṣabhānu.
Thus, this enchanting narrative of Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra’s Rāsa dance is meritorious, removing all sins, granting desires, and a source of auspiciousness. (37)
I have described before you that which bestows the three goals of life upon people, and grants perfect liberation to those seeking release.
What more do you wish to hear? || 38 ||
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Hymn by Śiva and Āsuri," within the Rāsakrīḍā section of the Vṛndāvana-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā.
Śrī Bahulāśva said: The light of Aghāsura and the other Daityas entered into Kṛṣṇa;
why, then, did that of Śaṅkhacūḍa become merged into Śrīdāman? || 1 ||
Tell me this, O one of great intelligence, you who are the best among those who know both the higher and the lower!
Oh, how most wonderful is the life-story of Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra! || 2 ||
O high-minded King, listen to the account of Goloka heard of old from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa; it is meritorious and removes all sins. (3)
Rādhā, Śrī, and Virajā were the three wives of Hari;
among them, Rādhā was exceedingly dear to the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
O King, once the Lord sported in a secluded grove with Rādhikā’s companion Virajā, who possessed the splendor of ten million moons.
Hearing from the mouth of her friend that Kṛṣṇa was accompanied by his co-wives, Rādhā became exceedingly dejected, distressed by the happiness of her rival wives.
It was a hundred yojanas in width and rose a hundred yojanas upward;
it was joined by tens of millions of horses and possessed a splendor equal to ten million suns.
The chariot was adorned with hanging garlands of gold and pearls of various colors,
and embellished by tens of millions of banners and golden jars.
Having ascended with her companions, whose hands held ten billion canes,
Śrī Rādhā, the beloved of the Lord, went quickly to see Hari.
Having observed the mighty Śrīdāmā, who had been stationed as the gatekeeper in that bower by Hari, he rebuked him along with his circle of friends.
Having suddenly struck them with canes, she prepared to go to the door;
hearing the clamor of her friends, Hari vanished from sight.
Out of fear of Rādhā, the river Virajā then suddenly became a stream ten million yojanas in length and flowed toward Goloka.
Suddenly coiling itself up, it shone like the ocean encircling the earth;
its body was variegated with jewel-like flowers, appearing as if sealed with the uṣṇīṣa mark.
Knowing that Hari had departed and seeing that the river had likewise become a stream,
Rādhikā looked upon that bower and went to her own bower.
Then, O lord of kings, by means of his boon, Kṛṣṇa quickly caused Virajā— who had become a river— to assume a physical form, clad in stainless garments.
Furthermore, Hari himself performed the rāsa dance together with Virajā in the forest of Virajā-tīrajā, amidst the groves and thickets of the Nikuñja-vṛnda forest.
Seven sons were born to Virajā through the power of Kṛṣṇa;
indeed, those children adorned the grove with their childhood play.
Once, a quarrel arose among them; the eldest was struck by them, and fleeing in fear, he went into his mother's lap.
Having consoled her son, the virtuous woman began to fondle him;
at that very moment, the Blessed Lord vanished right there before her eyes.
Afflicted by separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa, she cursed her son in anger:
"O evil-minded one, you who have caused the separation from Kṛṣṇa, become water! (20)
"O mortals, never shall you drink water at any time!
Thus he cursed the Jyeṣṭhās, saying, "Go to the earth, you instigators of strife! (21)
"Having the nature of water, you shall travel separately and not remain together;
your meeting shall occur only occasionally, at the time of dissolution."
Śrī Nārada said: Thus,
by the curse of their mother, they indeed came to the earth and settled within the moats formed by the wheels of Priyavrata’s chariot.
O King, those seven oceans—of salt water, sugarcane juice, wine, clarified butter, curd, milk, and fresh water—came into being; they were unshakeable and difficult to cross.
Difficult to fathom and profound, they extend for a hundred thousand yojanas;
on each individual island, their depth is successively doubled.
Then, after her sons had departed, Kṛṣṇa approached his beloved wife, who was overwhelmed by grief for her children and separated from them, and granted her a boon.
O timid one, when shall there be no separation between you and me?
You shall always provide protection for your sons through your own splendor.
Then, O King of Videha, having learned that Rādhā was suffering in separation, Kṛṣṇa Hari himself went to her bower accompanied by Śrīdāmā.
Seeing her beloved, who was dearer than life itself, arrived at the entrance of the bower with his companions, Rādhā became indignant and spoke these words to Hari: || 29 ||
Go to that very place where your new affection for Hari arose;
for Virajā has indeed become a river, and you ought to become a stream.
"Make your dwelling in that grove; what need have you of me?
Śrī Nārada said:
Having heard this, the Blessed One then went to that grove.
Śrīdāmā, the friend of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, spoke these words in anger to Rādhā:
"Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the most perfect Supreme Lord Himself. (32)
The Lord of countless universes shines resplendent in the Golokas;
the Supreme beyond the supreme is capable of creating millions of powers such as yourself.
"You are censuring him, O Rādhā;
do not be proud, do not be proud!
Rādhā said:
O fool, having praised your father,
you revile your mother, me.
"O evil-minded one, become a Rākṣasa and depart from Goloka!
Śrīdāmā said: "O auspicious lady, this pride of yours has arisen because of Kṛṣṇa’s compliance. (35)
Therefore, O Lord, your separation from Kṛṣṇa, who is the Supreme on earth and the most perfect one, will last for a hundred years; of this there is no doubt.
Śrī Nārada said:
While the two of them were thus terrified by the mutual curse they had incurred and were陷入 deep anxiety, the Lord himself appeared before them. (37)
The Blessed Lord said:
O Rādhā, I am indeed capable of setting aside my own scriptural injunctions,
but I am not capable of setting aside the words of my devotees.
"Do not grieve, O auspicious Rādhikā; hear my boon:
at the end of every month's separation, you shall have a vision of me. (39)
"In the kalpa known as Vārāha, for the sake of relieving the earth's burden, I shall go with you to grant an audience to my devotees. (40)
O Śrīdamana, listen to my words: become an asura by a portion of yourself;
in the Vaivasvata interval, you shall commit an offense against me during the rāsa dance.
And by my hand your death shall come, of this there is no doubt;
furthermore, you shall again experience separation from me as before, by virtue of my boon.
Śrī Nārada said: Thus, O King, by that curse, Śrīdāmā, who was of great austerity, formerly took birth in the house of Sudhana in the abode of the Puṇyajanas.
Known as Śaṅkhacūḍa, he became an attendant of the Giver of Wealth (Kubera).
From him, that light merged into Śrīdāman, O King of Videha.
Delighting in his own self, that Great Soul, the Lord of all and the form of all, being non-dual, performs every action through his own play within his own abode.
I do not consider this to be wonderful; I bow to that Kṛṣṇa. || 45 ||
O Vaideha, I have thus narrated to you this captivating section concerning Vṛndāvana;
the excellent man who hears this account [attains the highest goal].
He goes to the supreme state, which is most meritorious. || 46 ||
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Narrative of Śaṅkhacūḍa," in the Vṛndāvana-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā.
This Vṛndāvana-khaṇḍa is completed.
Bahulāśva said:
How did the Blessed One uphold the excellent Govardhana mountain?
Just as a child playfully [picks up] an *ucchilīndhra* flower with a single hand. || 1 ||
O best of sages, tell this divine and wonderful life-story of this great-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is most perfectly complete.
Śrī Nārada said:
At the end of the rainy season, all the cowherds and farmers gave their annual tribute to the king, just as they used to give it to Śakra.
Once, seeing the collection of materials for the great sacrifice to Mahendra, Hari questioned Nanda in the assembly while his beloved wives listened.
The Blessed One said: "What indeed is the fruit of this worship of Śakra?
Do they say it is worldly, or rather, is it pertaining to the next world?"
Śrīnanda said:
This worship of Śakra is indeed supreme for bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
without it, a man is never happy anywhere on earth.
The Blessed One said: Śakra and the hosts of gods, who enjoy the happiness of heaven on all sides by virtue of their own karmas;
They enter the mortal state upon the exhaustion of their merit;
know that such service is not the cause of liberation.
Since even fear would arise for the Supreme Lord (Parameṣṭhin), what indeed could be said of those whose very selves are made of that [fear]? Therefore, time is indeed supreme and infinite.
The wise know that everything else is surpassed by the most powerful.
Then, relying upon that [wisdom], one should worship Hari— the Lord of Sacrifice and Sovereign of the Gods— with excellent deeds,
having mentally renounced all fruits of action.
He shall attain supreme liberation, and not otherwise.
Cows, Brahmins, virtuous men, fire, gods, the Vedas, and likewise Dharma— these are the manifestations of the Lord of Sacrifice;
and those who worship Hari within these sacred abodes [attain Him].
They always go to happiness both here and in the hereafter. || 10 ||
This mountain named Govardhana, the sovereign king of the lords of mountains, has arisen from the chest of Hari;
for it has arrived here through the power of Pulastya, and by the sight of it, rebirth no longer exists.
Having worshipped the cows, Brahmins, and gods with great zeal, this supreme gift must indeed be given this very day;
for this King of Sacrifices is truly dear to me.
If it is not so, then do as you wish; go, O Vraja.
Śrī Nārada said: Then, in their midst, the aged cowherd Sannanda,
who was highly proficient in ethics and exceedingly gracious, spoke to Śrī Kṛṣṇa while Nanda listened.
Sananda said:
O son of Nanda, O dear one, you are the manifest treasure-house of knowledge;
by what ritual procedure should the worship of the mountain be performed? Tell me that according to the truth.
The Blessed Lord said: Having smeared the ground at the foot of the king of mountains with cow dung,
and having gathered all the necessary materials, one who is endowed with devotion and has conquered the senses [should proceed].
He should also cause the mountain to be bathed with the waters of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, along with the twice-born, while reciting the Sahasraśīrṣā mantra.
Then, having bathed the mountain with streams of white cow’s milk, with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), and again with fragrant flowers and black water; || 17 ||
Having offered divine garments, food offerings, and a seat superior in every respect, as well as a multitude of garlands and ornaments, and a supreme row of lamps; 18.
Then one should perform a circumambulation and thereafter offer salutations;
having joined the palms in reverence, one should utter this as follows: || 19 ||
Salutations to you who bear Vṛndāvana as your mark, the crown of Goloka;
salutations to Govardhana, the parasol of the perfect Brahman.
Then one should offer a handful of flowers, and after that,
perform the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) accompanied by sweet-sounding musical instruments such as bells, cymbals, and mṛdaṅga drums.
"I know this"—with this mantra, one should perform the rite with rain-like parched grains;
and endowed with faith, one should prepare a heap of food near that [image]. || 22 ||
It consisted of sixty-four bowls arranged in five rows, filled with the waters of the Śrī Gaṅgā and Yamunā mixed with Tulasī leaves. || 23 ||
With a concentrated mind, one should perform the service with fifty-six parts;
then, having honored the fires, the Brahmins, the cows, and the gods with perfumes and flowers. (24)
Having fed the best of the twice-born with fragrant and sweet foods,
he should also give excellent food to others, even to those who cook for horses.
One should have the cows perform a dance accompanied by groups of cowherds and cowherdesses;
with auspicious sounds and shouts of "Victory!", one should celebrate the Govardhana festival.
Listen now to the procedure for worship where the Govardhana mountain is not present:
one should fashion a representation of it out of cow dung, making its form exceedingly high. (27)
Adorned with arrays of flowers, networks of creepers, and blades of grass, Mount Govardhana on earth is always to be worshipped by mortals. (28)
Having cast gold equal in weight to a stone upon a mountain, one should take that stone away;
he who takes it without the gold shall go to the Mahāraurava hell.
One should always cause the service of the deity Śālagrāma to be performed;
indeed, sin shall not touch him, just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf.
That best of the twice-born who performs service to the rock of the king of mountains obtains the fruit of bathing in all the sacred fords of the earth consisting of seven continents. || 31 ||
He who performs the great worship of the King of Mountains every year,
having enjoyed all happiness in this world, attains liberation in the hereafter.

Thus ends the first chapter, titled "Description of the Ritual for the Worship of Śrī Girirāja," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Śrī Girirāja-khaṇḍa of the glorious Śrī Garga Saṃhitā. || 1 ||
Hari Oṃ! May this be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is Tat-Sat.
Śrī Nārada said:

Having heard the words of the son of Nanda, the lords of Vraja—the excellent Nanda, Sunanda, and others—were directly filled with great wonder; abandoning their previous activities, they performed the worship of the illustrious King of Mountains (Giri-rāja). || 1 ||
O King of Mithilā, having led away Bali and brought his two sons, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, King Nanda, together with Yaśodā,
went for the purpose of worshipping Śrīgiri.
Gārgya, full of zeal and serene, [spoke]. || 2 ||
Quickly mounting a very tall elephant of variegated color adorned with golden chains,
he proceeded toward the edge of Govardhana accompanied by herds of cows.
Like Śakra accompanied by his beloved amidst the autumn clouds. || 3 ||
Nanda and Upananda, along with the Vṛṣabhānus,
together with their sons, grandsons, and wives,
arrived at the side of the illustrious King of Mountains.
And having gathered together the entire burden of the sacrifice.

Mounting a palanquin whose radiance flashed like a thousand rising suns, Rādhā, adorned with divine garments and jewels along with her circles of friends, shone like Śacī; she was surrounded by women resembling cakorī birds and female bees.
O King, when the two supreme companions, Lalitā and Viśākhā— well-adorned, surrounded by millions of friends, and radiant— had arrived at his side, [he spoke].
O moon-faced one, who wields beautiful chowries! || 6 ||
Thus, O King, there were Ramā, Virajā, Mādhavī, Māyā, Kṛṣṇā, and Jahnu’s daughter;
indeed, they numbered thirty-two, eight, and sixteen.
And it is said that a troop of their female friends arrived there.
Indeed, [this applies] to the illustrious Maithilas, as well as the Kosalas, and likewise to the personified Vedas in the form of sages,
and similarly to the inhabitants of the city of Ayodhyā.
Of those who dwell in the forest of Śrīyajñasītā. || 8 ||
Of those residing in Vaikuṇṭha beginning with Ramā, likewise of those residing in the Upper Vaikuṇṭha,
and of those residing in the most brilliantly radiant islands.
[This refers to] those who dwell on the mountains of the worlds beginning with Dhruva. || 9 ||

Of the three divine qualities born from the ocean and others, of the non-divine medicinal herbs produced in celestial chariots, and of those belonging to Jālandharī—namely the daughters of the Ocean, Barhiṣmatī, and Jā, who reside in the subterranean realm (rasātala). || 10 ||
Likewise, the apsarases, all the daughters of the serpent-chiefs, and those dwelling in herds and flocks,
arrived at the side of the King of Mountains, beautifully adorned and carrying offerings for the palms and lamps.
The cowherds— old men, children, and youths—
were adorned with yellow garments, turbans, and peacock feathers,
and graced by necklaces of lotus seeds, *guñjā* berries, and forest garlands.
They shone together with their new bamboo staffs.

Having heard from my mouth of the festival of the best of mountains, the Bearer of Ganga—his matted locks bound in a circle, bearing a skull, smeared with ashes produced from bones, and adorned with bracelets of coiled garlands of serpents—[arrived]. || 13 ||
Intoxicated by the drinking of dhattūra, bhaṅgā, and poison, accompanied by the daughter of the Himālaya mountain and surrounded by his attendants,
he mounted Nandīśvara, the primordial vehicle.
He arrived at the region of the illustrious King of Mountains.
Royal sages, brahmin-sages, and celestial sages, as well as the lords of the Siddhas, the masters of yoga, and the foremost among the Haṃsas,
all came from afar for the purpose of beholding the mountain.
Thousands of groups of brahmins assembled. || 15 ||
O King, Govardhana, composed of jeweled stones, shone with golden peaks gleaming on all sides;
with intoxicated bees and beautiful waterfalls, it appeared like a woman with uplifted arms through its mountain caves. 16.
At that very moment, it is said, the mountains Meru, Himācala, and others, having taken on embodied forms and bearing auspicious offerings in their hands, bowed down to that mountain.
The lords of mountains [worship] Govardhana, who assumes a physical form. || 17 ||

And having performed the worship of the deity Govardhana with the twice-born, and having honored and bestowed upon them great wealth and abundant riches as instructed by Acyuta for the sake of the brahmins, the fire, and the cattle-wealth;
The Lord of Vraja offered an oblation to Śrīgiri.
Accompanied by Nanda and Upananda, by the Vṛṣabhānus, and by throngs of cowherd women and cowherds who were filled with great joy,
Kṛṣṇa performed the circumambulation of the excellent mountain while they sang and were intent upon dancing and playing musical instruments.
While the gods showered a rain of flowers and the people showered heaps of parched grain,
Govardhana— the king of kings among mountains— shone like a great monarch at a sacrifice amidst the throngs of men.

Kṛṣṇa, too, having assumed another exceedingly long form from within the midst of the Vraja mountain, and proclaiming, "I am the mountain; [swallow] the worlds," swallowed the entire heap of food that had been prepared.
The leaders of the groups of cowherds and cowherdesses,
having personally witnessed the power of the mountain,
spoke to Him as He was prepared there to grant a boon.
They were greatly amazed, their minds filled with joy. || 22 ||
"You are known by the cowherds; the Lord of the King of Mountains has been revealed directly by the son of Nanda.
Indeed, neither our cattle nor our excellent kinsmen [are here]."
May it attain increase day by day in the Kaurava land. || 23 ||
Having said, "So be it," Govardhana, the king of mountain kings, assumed a divine form,
his body made beautiful by a crown and armlets.
In an instant, he vanished from that place.
Nanda and Upananda, the Vṛṣabhānus, Bala, Sucandra, King Vṛṣabhānu,
the illustrious King Nanda, Hari, and the cowherds.
And all the cowherd women, along with their own herds of cows. || 25 ||
Then the twice-born, the hosts of Siddhas who are masters of yoga, Śiva and others, and all other people,
having bowed and worshipped the Mountain, were filled with joy.
And they went to their respective homes with reluctance. || 26 ||
I have related before you this wonderful account of the supreme life of Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra and the great festival of the king of mountains.
It is purifying and removes the great sins of men. || 27 ||

Thus ends the second chapter, titled "The Description of the Great Festival of Girirāja," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Śrī Girirāja-khaṇḍa of the glorious Śrī Garga Saṃhitā. || 2 ||
Hari Om. May this be offered to the True Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Tat Sat. Śrī Kṛṣṇārpaṇam astu.
Śrī Nārada said:
Then, having heard from my mouth that his own sacrifice had been destroyed and that the Govardhana festival had taken place, Purandara became enraged.
Indra swiftly dispatched the host named Sāṃvartaka, which is released from its bonds at the time of universal dissolution, for the destruction of Vraja.
Then the masses of clouds, roaring and variegated in color, became enraged;
some were black-hued, some yellow-hued, and others possessed a green luster.
Some clouds resemble the indragopa insect, some possess a luster like camphor, and there are various other clouds with the beautiful radiance of blue lotuses.
Intoxicated with pride, they rained down drops of water equal to elephants,
and those who were flickering discharged streams resembling the trunks of elephants.
Millions of stones, resembling mountain peaks, fell violently;
and fierce winds blew, uprooting trees and houses.
O Lord of Mithilā, there arose upon the earth a terrifying and great roar from the Pracaṇḍas, who bring an end to the thunderbolts and the clouds.
By that roar, the cosmic egg along with the seven worlds and their subterranean cavities resounded;
the elephants of the quarters trembled, and the stars indeed fell toward the circle of the earth.
Terrified and desiring victory, the leaders of the cowherds, accompanied by their families and placing their respective children in front, went to Nanda’s residence.
Having bowed down to the Supreme Lord, the delighter of Śrī, who is accompanied by Balarāma,
all the inhabitants of Vraja, afflicted by fear, spoke while having sought refuge in him.
The cowherds said:
O Rāma, Rāma, O mighty-armed one! O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Vraja! Protect, protect your own people from this great calamity sent by Indra!
Having destroyed the sacrifice to Indra at your word, the festival of Govardhana was performed;
now that Śakra is enraged, tell us quickly what must be done.
Śrī Nārada said:
Seeing Gokula agitated and crowded with cowherds and cowherdesses,
as well as the cattle along with their calves, he, remaining unperturbed, spoke to the cowherds.
The Blessed Lord said:
"Do not fear; go to the mountain slope along with all your attendants.
He by whom your worship was offered will provide protection for you."
Śrī Nārada said:
Having spoken thus, Hari, together with his kinsmen, went to Govardhana;
lifting it up, he held the mountain effortlessly with a single hand.
Just as a young elephant effortlessly holds Mount Śilīndhra with its trunk,
so did the joy of King Vraja shine forth, holding Mount Puṣkara with his own lotus-like hand.
He is the source of compassion, the Lord consisting of mercy. || 16 ||

Then he said to the cowherds: "O father, O mother, O beloved of the cowherd settlement, O lords! With all our wealth, including the utensils and the cows, let us enter the mountain cave; here there is no fear at all from Śakra."
Having thus heard the words of Hari, the cowherds, together with their wealth of cattle,
their families, and their household goods, entered the foothills of Śrīgiri.
O King, all the young companions, commanded by Kṛṣṇa,
took up their respective clubs— which were as sturdy as mountain peaks— and prepared themselves along with Balarāma.
Seeing Sudarśana and Śeṣa approaching on a flood of water at the foot of that mountain, the Blessed One gave them his command by means of his mind.
O King of Mithilā, the Sudarśana discus, possessing the radiance of ten million suns,
drank up the downpour of rain from above the mountain, just as Agastya drank the ocean.
Remaining coiled like a serpent below that mountain,
Śeṣa blocked that vast expanse of water, just as the shoreline restrains the great ocean.
Hari, the upholder of Govardhana, remained perfectly steady for seven days;
they stood gazing at Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra like cakora birds.
Mounting his intoxicated elephant Airāvata, Purandara,
accompanied by his army and filled with wrath, arrived at the circle of the cowherd settlement.
From afar, he hurled his own thunderbolt with the intent to destroy Nanda’s cow-pen;
Mādhava paralyzed Śakra’s arm together with the thunderbolt.
Then Śakra, terrified, fled suddenly along with the hosts of Sāṃvartaka clouds and the gods, like an elephant struck by a lion. || 26 ||
At that very moment, O King, sunrise occurred; the clouds dispersed in all directions, the winds immediately ceased, and the rivers became shallow with little water.
The surface of the earth became free from mire, and the sky became stainless;
the four-footed animals and the birds found happiness here and there.
Then, as Hari had instructed them, the cowherds emerged from the mountain cave,
slowly taking with them each their own wealth and their cattle.
Having lifted Govardhana, he presented it and spoke to his companions;
they said to him, "Go forth; we shall hold up this mountain by our own strength."
To the cowherds who were thus intent on their talk, Hari, the upholder of Govardhana,
being high-minded, gave half of that mountain's weight to them.
And by that weight, the weak cowherd boys were cast down.
Raising them up with his hand, Kṛṣṇa effortlessly placed the mountain back in its original position while everyone looked on.
At that very moment, O King, the hosts of cowherd women and the chief cowherds, having worshipped Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda,
with perfumes, unbroken grains, and other offerings such as curds and milk, and recognizing him as the Supreme, all bowed down to him most intensely.
O King, Nanda, Yaśodā, Rohiṇī,
Balarāma, and the elders headed by Sannanda embraced Kṛṣṇa and presented Him with riches.
Afflicted by compassion, they joined together with auspicious blessings. || 35 ||
Having praised him and being intent on singing and instrumental music,
the residents of Vraja danced nearby the joy of the king’s lineage and returned to their own homes.
Placing Hari at their head, they went according to their desire. || 36 ||
At that very moment, the gods, filled with great joy, rained down auspicious flowers born from the beautiful Nandana grove;
they sang the glory of the one who bears the mountain-king Śrī Giri.
The hosts of Siddhas in heaven, along with the chiefs of the Gandharvas. || 37 ||
Thus ends the third chapter, titled "The Lifting of Govardhana," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Śrī Girirāja-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā.
Hari Om. May this be offered to the True Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Om Tat Sat. Śrī Kṛṣṇārpaṇam astu.
Śrī Nārada said:
Then Śakra, together with the hosts of gods, arrived there on the mountain;
his pride gone, he bowed down in secret before Kṛṣṇa.
Indra said:
You are the God of gods, the Supreme Lord, the Sovereign, the Perfect, the Ancient, the Most Excellent among the Supreme Persons;
you are higher than the highest, beyond primordial nature, Hari—protect me, protect me, O Lord of Heaven, O Lord of the Universe! 2.
You alone are the Blessed One who has manifested in ten incarnations out of a desire to protect the cows of the Dharma and the Veda;
today you have been born as the Perfect God.
For the destruction of the lords of the Daityas, such as Kaṃsa and others. || 3 ||
O Lord of Heaven, forgive me, whose mental faculties are deluded by Your māyā, who am arrogant with pride, and who have become an object of Your contempt— just as a father forgives his son.
Be gracious, O Lord of gods, O Abode of the World!
Oṃ, salutations to Govinda, the lifter of Mount Govardhana, the dweller in Gokula,
the cowherd, the lord of the cowherds, the husband of the gopīs, the upholder of the mountain-elephant,
the ocean of compassion, the creator of the world, the auspiciousness of the world, and the abode of the world.

Salutations to You, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the most perfect Supreme Being, the enchantment of the universe, the one who puts even ten million Cupids to shame, the bridegroom of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, the lamp of King Nanda’s royal lineage,
the Lord of the Goloka realm, and the Sovereign of countless universes.
Homage to you, homage to you, to the Self-Existent Blessed One together with his host. || 5 ||
Śrī Nārada said: Whoever, having risen in the morning, recites this hymn composed by Śakra,
shall attain all perfections and shall have no fear of calamities.
Having thus praised the god Hari together with all the hosts of deities,
Purandara, with palms joined in reverence, bowed down before him.
Then, on the beautiful Govardhana mountain, Surabhi, the cow born from the ocean,
bathed the Lord of the Gopas with streams of her own milk.
The intoxicated elephant Airāvata bathed Śrī Kṛṣṇa with four trunk-tusks filled with the waters of the celestial Gaṅgā.
O King, the ṛṣis, all the Śrutis, the gods, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras, being filled with joy and showering flowers, praised Hari.
O King, when Kṛṣṇa’s consecration had taken place, the great Govardhana Hill melted and,
impelled by joy and bliss, carried him here and there.
The Blessed One, being pleased with him, placed his lotus-hand there;
O King, that hand-mark is visible even today on that mountain.
That sacred ford is supreme, a destroyer of the sins of men;
know that very footprint to be that sacred ford, O King of Mithilā. (13)
Such was the footprint of that [cow] right there;
O King of Mithilā, the footprints of Surabhi likewise appeared there.
O King of Mithilā, by the descent of the water of two Gaṅgās and by bathing in Kṛṣṇa,
the mental Gaṅgā was indeed produced there on the mountain, destroying all sins.
O King, from the streams of milk flowing from Surabhi during the bathing of Govinda on the mountain,
Govindakuṇḍa was formed, which is the supreme destroyer of great sins.
Sometimes the sweetness of milk is perceived there;
having bathed in that place, a person shall directly attain the state of Govinda.
Having circumambulated Hari, bowed down,
and offered oblations there, Purandara and the other gods raised shouts of victory and rained down a shower of beautiful flowers.
The gods, filled with happiness, went to heaven.
O King of kings, whoever hears the narrative of Kṛṣṇābhiṣeka obtains a fruit greater than that of the final purificatory bath of ten horse-sacrifices; indeed, he obtains even more.
He goes to the supreme station of the highest Creator.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Coronation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa," in the Girirāja-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā, within the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Oṃ. May this be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is Tat-Sat.
Śrī Nārada said: Once, all the cowherds and cowherd-maidens, having witnessed that wondrous deed of the son of Nanda, spoke to Nanda and Yaśodā.
The cowherds said:
"O King of Cowherds, no one has ever been born in your lineage who could support this mountain.
O Yaśomatī, you are not capable of supporting this stone for seven days."
Where is a seven-year-old boy, and where is the lifting of the king of mountains?
Therefore, no doubt arises in us regarding your mighty son.
Like a lordly elephant bearing a lotus, he held that best of mountains with one hand as easily as a child playfully holds a mushroom.
"O Yaśodā, you are fair-complexioned; O Nanda, you too possess a fair complexion.
Yet this one who has been born is dark-complexioned—this is contrary to the characteristics of this family. (5)
Or rather, let it be that such childishness may belong to Kṣatriyas;
there would be no fault in Balabhadra, who is born of the Lunar dynasty.
"We shall abandon our kinsmen if you do not speak the truth;
tell us of his birth among the cowherds, and if you do, there will be no strife. (7)
Śrī Nārada said:
Having heard the words of the cowherds, Yaśodā was overwhelmed with fear;
then King Nanda spoke to the cowherds who were filled with anger.
Śrī Nanda said: "O cowherds, with a concentrated mind I shall speak the words of Garga,
by which you, the hosts of cowherds, may quickly become free from suffering."
The letter *ka* is the beloved of Kamalā; the letter *ṛ* is Rāma;
and the letter *ṣa* is the Lord of the six qualities, the dweller in Śvetadvīpa.
The letter *ṇa* is this Man-Lion (*Narasiṃha*), and the letter *a* is indeed the imperishable consumer of fire;
likewise, these two *visargas* are the sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

And because the six full [tattvas] are completely dissolved into that Great Self (mahātman) within which all sounds reside, He is directly celebrated as Kṛṣṇa, the Most Perfect One (paripūrṇatama). || 12 ||
His complexion was white, red, and yellow, assumed according to each successive age; at the end of Dvāpara and the beginning of Kali, this boy has turned black.
Therefore, this son of Nanda is renowned by the name Kṛṣṇa;
for the Vasus are indeed the senses, and their deity is the mind alone.
And whoever acts within that [body] is also remembered as Vāsudeva. || 15 ||
Rādhā, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, was born in Kīrtimandira;
he is her manifest husband, and for that reason he is remembered as Rādhāpati.
The most perfect Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself, the master of countless universes, shines resplendent in his abode of Goloka. 17.
Thus, this child has been born to you for the purpose of relieving the burden [of the earth], for the sake of slaying Kaṃsa and others, and for the protection of devotees. (18)
O Bhārata, his names are infinite and secret even to the Vedas; and as they will arise through his divine sports in the performance of his deeds, there should be no wonder at them.
Having heard this regarding my son, I no longer harbor any doubt;
for on this earth, the words of the Vedas and the speech of Brahmanas are indeed the authoritative standard. (20)
The cowherds said:
"If the great sage Garga-ācārya had come to your house at that very moment for the naming ceremony, you would not have failed to invite your kinsmen."
The naming ceremony for the infant was performed by you in your own home;
such is your custom that everything remains secret even within the house. (22)
Śrī Nārada said:
Speaking thus, those cowherds departed from Nanda’s palace and went to Vṛṣabhānu, their bodies filled with rage. (23)
All the hosts of cowherds, filled with pride toward their kinsman, spoke directly to Vṛṣabhānu, the foremost of men and the companion of King Nanda.
The cowherds said:
"O best of the Vṛṣabhānus, you are indeed the chief of our kinsmen and are high-minded;
O lord of the cowherds, O king, abandon King Nanda for the sake of the clan. (25)
The illustrious Vṛṣabhānu said: "What fault is there in King Nanda that I should abandon him?
He is the beloved of the cowherds, the crest-jewel of kinsmen, and dear to me. (26)
The cowherds said: "O King, if you do not abandon him, then we, the residents of Vraja, shall abandon you.
O great sage, this girl has been raised in your house and is now fit for marriage."
"By you, the chief of kinsmen, intoxicated by prosperity, no bride was given to the foremost of suitors; therefore, a stain attaches to you. (28)
Today we consider you, O King, to have fallen from your kin;
therefore, O high-minded one, quickly abandon King Nanda—abandon him! (29)
The illustrious Vṛṣabhānu said:
"O cowherd, with a concentrated mind I shall speak the words of Garga, by which you, the hosts of cowherds, may quickly become free from suffering. (30)
The Lord of Goloka, the master of countless universes, higher than the highest—there is no one superior to Him, who was born as an infant in the house of Nanda. (31)
Requested by Brahmā for the removal of the earth's burden and for the slaying of Kaṃsa and others, Kṛṣṇa appeared upon the surface of the world.
She who is the illustrious principal queen of Kṛṣṇa, known as Rādhikā in Goloka, has also been born in your house; yet you do not recognize her as the Supreme.
"O King, I will not cause a marriage to take place with this woman;
their marriage shall occur at Bhāṇḍīra on the bank of the Yamunā. (34)
And near Vṛndāvana, in a secluded and beautiful place,
Parameṣṭhin will arrive and cause the marriage to be performed.
Therefore, O best of cowherds, know Rādhā to be the half-body of the Supreme Lord himself, the queen in the palace of Goloka, who is the crest-jewel of the worlds. (36)
"All of you cowherds have come to this earth from Goloka;
likewise, the hosts of gopīs and the cows are in Gokula by the will of Rādhikā. (37)
When the great sage Garga Ācārya had spoken thus and departed,
from that day forth I no longer harbor any doubt regarding Rādhā.
"The word of the Vedas is the speech of Brahman and is indeed the authority on this earth;
thus has it been told to you, O cowherds. What more do you wish to hear? (39)
Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Dispute of the Cowherds," in the Śrī Garga Saṃhitā, within the Girirāja-khaṇḍa, in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Om. May this be offered to the True Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Om tat sat. Śrī Kṛṣṇārpaṇam astu.
Śrī Nārada said: Having heard these words of the noble Vṛṣabhānu, the inhabitants of Vraja, having attained peace, were filled with wonder; their doubts dispelled, they spoke again. || 1 ||
The cowherds said:
"O King, the boon was appropriate; for the beloved of Hari chose the son of Rādhā.
By his power, your great majesty is seen upon this earth. (2)
There were thousands of intoxicated elephants and tens of millions of restless horses;
there were chariots resembling the celestial abodes of the gods and tens of millions of auspicious palanquins.
By the tens of millions, by the tens of millions, there were cows enchanting with gold and jewels,
variegated mansions, and various kinds of gems.
All comforts, such as food and the like, are now seen by you;
even Kaṃsa has been subdued upon seeing your wonderful power.
O great hero, you are the direct son-in-law of the Lord of Kānyakubja and of King Bhaṇḍana, and you possess a treasury like that of Kubera.
Nowhere in the palace of King Nanda is there any glory equal to yours;
King Nanda is but a farmer, a cowherd of humble mind.
If the son of Nanda is indeed Hari himself, the most perfect one, then,
O Lord, perform his examination while we all look on.
Śrī Nārada said:
Having then heard their words, the great Vṛṣabhānu performed an examination of King Nanda’s opulence.
O Lord of Maithila, there were necklaces of pearls, each consisting of ten million large pearls,
with every single pearl possessing a radiant luster worth ten million coins.
O King, having placed those [jewels] in vessels, he sent them to Nanda by means of skilled men carrying them, while everyone looked on.
Having gone to King Nanda’s assembly hall, those highly skilled men,
choosing [him], set down their vessels of milk-curd and, bowing before him, spoke to Nanda.
The suitors said:

"Recognizing Rādhā—who possesses eyes like nine lotuses and bears the luster of ten million moons—as one fit for marriage, the chief among them, headed by Vṛṣabhānu, deliberated while searching for an excellent groom. (13)
Having beheld your divine son, who enchants even the god of love, who is preeminent for his arm that lifted Mount Govardhana, and who is saluted by Vṛṣabhānu;
He sent him forth, O Lord of the people, O Master.
First, take a heap of pearls for placing upon the lap of the bridegroom;
and from here, provide enough for the sake of the bride.
For this is indeed the well-known tradition of our family. || 15 ||
Śrī Nārada said: Having seen the object, the supreme Nanda, though already amazed, reflected upon it;
then, taking someone equal to Yaśodā to question her, he went into the inner apartments.
Then Nanda and the illustrious Yaśodā reflected for a long time:
"There is no object in my house equal to this pearl. (17)
In this world, all sense of shame has departed; if wealth were extracted through laughter, what should be done regarding that which occurred during the marriage ceremony of Śrī Kṛṣṇa? 18.
"Therefore, it is improper to take him now; he should be taken later when wealth has been acquired.
While Nanda was thinking thus, Yaśodā [spoke]. 19.
The Blessed One, the destroyer of suffering, arrived there unobserved;
having led a hundred ropes to those outer fields on all sides, he remained there.
And he indeed cast pearl-ornaments one by one with his own hand,
just as a farmer sows seeds of grain in his own fields.
Then Nanda, counting the collection of buds once more,
saw that it was short by one hundred and fell into a state of doubt.
Śrī Nanda said:
"There is nothing equal to what happened before, and even that has now reached a state of deficiency.
Alas! A stain will fall upon all our own kinsmen from every side."
Or perhaps Kṛṣṇa or the child Baladeva took it for the sake of play; with a dejected mind, he asked them both. (24)
Śrī Nārada said:
Having reflected thus, Nanda also questioned Kṛṣṇa with respect;
the Blessed One, the lifter of Govardhana, smilingly spoke to Nanda. (25)
The Blessed Lord said:
"We cowherds are cultivators who cause all seeds to sprout; we have scattered the seeds of pearls upon the field, having yoked our draft animals. (26)
Śrī Nārada said:
Having heard what was spoken by his own son, the Lord of Vraja rebuked him and went to those sacred fields together with him in order to take them away.
There, hundreds of auspicious pearl-bearing trees were seen, possessing long trunks and adorned with green sprouts. (28)
O King, clusters of pearl garlands by the millions upon millions hung down and shone like celestial lights in the expanse of the sky.
Then Nanda, filled with great joy upon realizing that Kṛṣṇa was the Supreme Lord,
[offered] divine pearls as large as small melons.
King Nanda, the lord of Vraja, having loaded ten million bhāras of those [milk products] onto carts, gave them to those who were requesting them. (31)
Having taken all of that, O King, they went to the excellent Vṛṣabhānu and sang of the glory of Nanda while everyone listened.
Then, all the inhabitants of Vraja, filled with great wonder and having realized that the son of Nanda was Hari,
bowed down to the excellent Vṛṣabhānu, their doubts dispelled.
O Lord of Mithilā, from that day forward, it became known to all the people of Vraja that Rādhā was dear to Hari, and Hari was dear to Rādhā. (34)
O King of Mithilā, because pearls were cast there by Hari, the son of Nanda,
that place became a king among holy sites known as Muktāsarovara.
Whoever makes an offering of even a single pearl there obtains the fruit of giving a hundred thousand pearls; of this there is no doubt. (36)
Thus, O King, I have related to you the great festival of the Lord of Mountains, which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation upon men; what more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "The Examination of Hari," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Girirāja-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā.
Hari Om. May this be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is Tat-Sat.
Śrī Bahulāśva said:
"O Great Yogin, you who possess direct divine vision, tell me this: how many principal sacred sites (tīrthas) are there upon the high-souled king of mountains?"
Śrī Nārada said:
O King, the entire Govardhana is remembered as the best of all sacred fords (tīrthas); and Vṛndāvana is the mountain that is the crown jewel of Goloka, most highly honored.
He who bestows protection upon the cowherds, their wives, and the cattle; he who is the great beloved of Kṛṣṇa;
he whose parasol is the perfect Brahman—who else could be the most excellent of sacred fords? (3)
Having completely set aside the sacrifice to Indra,
the Blessed Lord, the Sovereign of the World, commenced his worship together with all his own people.
He is the most perfectly complete, the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself in person;
the master of countless universes, the Lord of Goloka, higher than the highest.
O King of Mithilā, even the Four-faced One [Brahmā] is not capable of describing the majesty of that place where he always dwells and sports with children.
There indeed is the mental Gaṅgā, which destroys the flood of great sins;
there is the pure and auspicious Govindakuṇḍa and the Candrasarovara lake.
Rādhākuṇḍa, Kṛṣṇakuṇḍa, and Lalitākuṇḍa,
as well as Gopālakuṇḍa and Kusumākara, are located right there.
Through contact with the crest of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s head, the stone became marked by his crown;
merely by the sight of it, a person shall become like the crown of a god.
On that rock where various figures were drawn by Kṛṣṇa,
even today it remains sacred and is known as Citraśilā on the mountain.
That stone which Kṛṣṇa, delighting in play, used to strike while playing with the children—
by being struck, that stone became the destroyer of a multitude of great sins.
O King of Mithilā, that field where Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra played with the cowherds at ball is known as Kaṇḍuka.
Having seen it, one goes to the station of Śakra; having bowed to it, one reaches that station of Brahmā;
and by rolling in its dust, one would go directly to the station of Viṣṇu.
There, Mādhava stole the turbans of the cowherds;
that sacred site on the mountain is named Auṣṇiṣa, which destroys great sins.
Once, a group of cowherd women set out to sell curds;
hearing the sound of tinkling anklets nearby, they blocked the path, infatuated by the god of love.
Vaṃśīdhara, preceded by the cowherds and holding his excellent staff,
placed his foot before them; for me, he gave a gift for the sake of collecting taxes from their hands.
He spoke to the cowherd women on the path, saying, "Give [me]! (16)
The gopīs said:
You alone are crooked, having set out upon the path with the cowherd boys, being excessively greedy for dairy products.
Together with your mother and father, we shall indeed force you into the bonds of Kaṃsa.
The Blessed Lord said: "I shall slay Kaṃsa, who wields a most terrible rod of punishment, along with his kinsmen; this is my solemn oath for the sake of the cows.
I shall do this by force in the city of Yadu, and I shall always lead [you] from the land of the king of mountains."
Śrī Nārada said:
Having spoken thus, the son of Nanda joyfully took the vessels of curd from the children one by one and dashed them against the surface of the earth. (19)
"Oh, this son of Nanda is exceedingly bold and fearless!
This hero may be spoken to without restraint in the forest, but he would be powerless in the city. (20)
"Let us tell this to Yaśodā and Nanda today," they said;
speaking thus, those cowherd women went to their homes with smiles upon their faces.
Having prepared droṇas of nīpa and pālāśa leaves, Mādhava,
together with the boys, ate them along with the thick curds.
Then the leaves of the trees took on the shape of a *droṇa* measure;
and that most meritorious field, O lord of kings, became known by the name Droṇa. (23)
Having made a gift of curd there, and having drunk the curd held in a leaf-cup, a man should offer salutation; for him, there shall be no falling from Goloka.
Where Mādhava, having covered his eyes, became absorbed along with the children, there a worldly holy site (tīrtha) was born that destroys all sins. || 25 ||
And there is the Kadambakhaṇḍa Tīrtha, which is always associated with the pastimes of Hari;
by the mere sight of it, a man becomes Nārāyaṇa.
O King of Mithilā, on that very spot of Govardhana where Rādhā performed her amorous dalliance during the rāsa dance, there arose a circle of erotic splendor.
O King, that very form in which Kṛṣṇa held up Mount Govardhana exists there as the Śṛṅgāramaṇḍala.
At the beginning of the Kali age, four thousand and eight hundred years have passed there in the sacred field of Śṛṅgāramaṇḍala.
O King, while everyone looks on, that form of Hari, which is self-perfected, will manifest from within the cave of the king of mountains.
O King, virtuous people will call that Śrīnātha the "Tamer of Gods," for he always performs his divine play upon Mount Govardhana.
O Lord of Mithilā, those people in the Kali age who behold that form with their own eyes shall become fulfilled in their purpose.
Jagannātha, Raṅganātha, Dvārakānātha,
and Badrīnātha are located at the four corners on the mountain of Bhārata as well.
O King, this Lord also resides in the center of Govardhana;
in the sacred land of Bhārata-varṣa, there are five Lords who are the masters of the gods.
They are pillars for the pavilion of the True Dharma, devoted to the protection of those in distress;
by beholding them, a man becomes like Nārāyaṇa. (35)
A wise man who performs the pilgrimage to the four Lords on earth, yet does not visit Devadamana, shall not obtain the fruit of that pilgrimage. || 36 ||
One should behold Śrīnātha, the subduer of gods, on Govardhana Hill;
one shall obtain the fruit of the pilgrimage to the four Lords on earth.
O King of Mithilā, wherever there are the footprints of Airāvata and Surabhi, even a sinful man who bows there goes to Vaikuṇṭha.
Having seen and bowed to the handprints and footprints of the great-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa, any man shall go directly to the abode of Kṛṣṇa. (39)
O King, these sacred fords, ponds, and sanctuaries are the very limbs of the king of mountains; what more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Sacred Tīrtha of Girirāja," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Girirāja-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā.
Hari Om. May this be offered to the True Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Om Tat Sat. Śrī Kṛṣṇārpaṇam astu.
Śrī Bahulāśva said: In which various limbs of his body are which sacred sites (tīrthas) situated?
Speak, O God, O Mahādeva, for you are the supreme knower of all that is high and low. ||1||
Śrī Nārada said:
Whichever limb in which a particular [divine] manifestation is well-known, that they know to be the supreme limb.
O King of Mithilā, there is no accumulation of parts in the king of mountains as he proceeds [in his dissolution]. ||2||
Just as Brahman is omnipresent, so indeed are all its limbs.
O giver of honor, I shall likewise speak eternally of manifestation according to its actual state.
Below the Śṛṅgāra-maṇḍala is the face of Govardhana.
Where the Blessed One had a mountain of food prepared by the residents of Vraja.
The eyes are indeed the celestial Gaṅgā, and the nose is the lake of the moon.
Govindakuṇḍa is indeed the lower lip, and Kṛṣṇakuṇḍaka is the chin. ||5||
Rādhākuṇḍa is his tongue, and the Lalitāsaras lake is his two cheeks.
Gopālakuṇḍa, Karṇa, Karṇānta, and Kusumākara. ||6||
O Maithila, know that his forehead is marked with the sign of a crest-lock.
His head was the Citraśilā stone, and his neck was indeed the Vādanī stone.
The *kāṇḍuka*, the side region (*pārśvadeśa*), and the *auṣṇiṣa* are said to be the waist (*kaṭi*).
Droṇatīrtha is said to be in the region of the back, and Laukika in the belly. ||8||
The Kadamba grove is her breast, and the circle of lovers is her life-force.
The mind of that great-souled one was fixed upon the footprints of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ||9||
Likewise, the hand-sign, the intellect, the footprint of Airāvata, and the sacred site.
On the footprints of Surabhi were the two wings of that great-souled one.
Likewise, the tail is remembered as being in the Puccha-kuṇḍa, and the strength in the Vatsa-kuṇḍa.
Likewise, one should meditate on Krodha at Rudrakuṇḍa and Kāma at Śakrasarovara.
At Kuberatīrtha, he displayed exertion; at Brahmatīrtha, serenity.
For those who know the ancient lore say that at Yamatīrtha, one indeed speaks of the ego (ahaṃkāra). ||12||
In this manner, O King of Mithilā, all the limbs of the king of mountains are present everywhere.
And I have related to you those which remove all sins. ||13||
And that best of men who hears of the splendor of the king of mountains.
He shall go to the supreme abode, Goloka, which is difficult even for yogis to attain. ||14||
That mountain named Govardhana, the king of kings among mountains, rose up from the chest of Hari.
For Pulastya has arrived here by his own splendor; by the sight of him, rebirth no longer exists. (15)
Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Glories of Girirāja," in the Śrī Garga Saṃhitā, within the Girirāja-khaṇḍa, in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Oṃ! May this be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is Tat-Sat.
Śrī Bahulāśva said:
Oh, Govardhana is truly the king of mountains, beloved by Hari!
Indeed, no sacred site equal to it exists upon the earth or in heaven.
When did this lord of mountains come to rest upon the chest of Śrī Kṛṣṇa?
Tell me this, O one of great intelligence, for you are the very mind of Hari himself.
Śrī Nārada said: O high-minded King, listen to the account of the origin of Goloka,
which bestows the four goals of human life upon men and is endowed with the primordial pastimes.
The self is beginningless, the person, devoid of qualities, and beyond primordial nature;
he is the most perfect, the manifest Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Blessed Lord, the Master.
The inward abode, self-luminous, rejoicing eternally,
wherein Time— the lord of those who reckon time— resides for those who perceive it as a mere attribute of the Abode.
O King, neither illusion nor even the Great Quality (mahat) can prevail;
they do not enter anywhere, O King, for the mind, consciousness, intellect, and the ego are [mere constructs].
In his own abode, he fashioned by his will Brahmā in embodied form;
first there appeared Śeṣa, white as a lotus stalk and of vast body.
In its lap is the great realm of Goloka, honored by the worlds;
having attained it, one endowed with devotion never returns again.
Furthermore, the Gaṅgā, who flows through the three paths, was born from the lotus feet of the Lord, the master of Goloka and the sovereign of countless Brahmāṇḍas.
Furthermore, O King, from his left shoulder there arose Kṛṣṇā, the best of rivers;
she shone with the flowers of her amorous charms, appearing like a woman adorned with uśīra paste.
The divine Śrī Rāsa-maṇḍala, endowed with gold and jewels and filled with various decorative splendors, [rests] upon the two ankles of the Lord, the illustrious Hari. 11.
Surrounded by the assembly halls, courtyards, and pathways,
it possessed the sweetness of spring and was filled with the warbling of cuckoos.
Filled with peacocks and bees and attended by lakes, a grove was produced from the two shanks of the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa. || 13 ||
O King, Vṛndāvana, the best of all forests, appeared from his knees, and Līlāsarovara appeared directly from the thighs of the Supreme Soul. (14)
From the region of her waist issued the golden earth, radiant and inlaid with divine jewels;
and upon her abdomen was the line of hair, like the spreading creepers of the spring.
Filled with flocks of various birds and adorned by humming bees,
they were bent down by the weight of excellent flowers and fruits, like those born of noble lineage.
From that glorious navel-lotus of his, thousands of lotuses shone here and there in the lakes of the realm of Hari.
From the region of Tribali, a very cool breeze blew gently;
from the area of the collarbone, the auspicious cities of Mathurā and Dvārakā were born. (18)
From the two arms of Śrī Hari were born the eight primary attendants (pārṣadas) headed by Śrīdāma;
from the two wrists came the Nandas, and from the tips of the hands, the Upanandas.
O King, all the Vṛṣabhānus indeed arose from the two armpits of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
and all the hosts of cowherds were born from the hairs of Kṛṣṇa.
O Lord of Mithilā, the cows were the minds of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the bulls were those who bear the burden of dharma, and the clumps of grass were the intellects. (21)
From his left shoulder arose a fair radiance of shimmering splendor;
from that were born Līlā, Śrī, Bhū, and Virajā, the beloved consorts of Hari.
Līlāvatī is his beloved, whom others know as Rādhā;
from the two arms of Śrī Rādhā came the two friends Viśākhā and Lalitā. (23)
O King, likewise the cowherd girls, who were born from the hair-pores of Rādhā, became his companions;
in this manner Madhusūdana fashioned the layout of Goloka.
O King, having thus arranged His entire own realm, the Supreme Self, the Lord of countless world-eggs, shone there together with Śrī Rādhā.
The Supreme, the Lord of the supreme, the perfectly full God. || 25 ||

Once, in that beautiful assembly circle of the Rāsa dance, which was filled with the resonant sound of shimmering anklets, and whose courtyard was resplendent with large drops of perspiration flowing down the bodies of those covered by fine parasols and strings of pearls; (26)
In that place, fragrant with the naturally flowing, excellent nectar from the clusters of beautiful Malati flowers,
and resounding with the sounds of mridanga drums, cymbals, and flutes;
To the Supreme One, who is enchanting with a beautiful voice, song, and other such qualities.
In the delightful nectar of the Śrīsundarī-rāsa, standing in the midst of it— more enchanting than ten million Cupids—
he spoke to the Lord of Rādhā with powerful words.
Having cast a sidelong glance, she displayed her skill in bestowing aesthetic flavor (rasa).
Rādhā said:
"O Lord of the Universe, if you are pleased with me because of my love during the Rāsa dance, then I shall make before you this prayer that resides in my heart. (29)
The Blessed Lord said: "Choose a boon, O lady of beautiful thighs, whatever dwells in your mind.
Even if there is something that ought not to be given, I shall give it out of love, my dear."
Rādhā said:
"In Vṛndāvana, beside the divine groves on the bank of the Kṛṣṇā, there is a place suitable for the rasa-dance."
O God of gods, make this secluded place beautiful; this is my heart's desire.
Śrī Nārada said:
Having said, "So be it," the Blessed One reflected upon that which is appropriate for solitude and beheld his own heart with his lotus-like eyes.
At that very moment, as the multitude of gopīs looked on, a watery radiance emerged from Kṛṣṇa’s heart like a sprout of his own passion.
Having fallen upon the surface of the earth, it grew into the form of a mountain;
divine, composed of jewels and minerals, and surrounded by beautiful waterfalls and caves.
It was enchanting with its network of *kadaṃba*, *bakula*, and *aśoka* creepers, abounding in clusters of *mandāra* and *kunda* flowers, and teeming with flocks of beautiful birds. || 35 ||
O Vaideha, in a mere moment,
it extended for a hundred million yojanas and was further suspended like Śeṣa over a distance of ten million yojanas.
It rose upwards to a height of fifty koṭis of yojanas;
it stood eternally like a lordly elephant, extending fifty koṭis [in width]. || 37 ||
O King of Mithilā, it was like a palace with hundreds of peaks flashing with limbs ten million yojanas long, and adorned with lofty golden finials.
Some call it Govardhana, while others call it Śataśṛṅga;
yet even such as it was, it grew further, its mind filled with longing.
When that tumult arose and Goloka was overwhelmed with fear,
Hari, seeing this, rose up and immediately struck him with his hand.
"Why do you grow, O Lord, standing here covering the severed world?
Or why do these [beings] not dwell there? To this, Hari brought about peace. (41)
Having gazed upon that best of mountains, the beloved of the Blessed One became serene;
O King, she shone together with Hari in that secluded place.
This very best of mountains was personally impelled by Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
it consists of all sacred fords, is dark-complexioned like a rain-cloud, and is dear to the gods.
To the west of Bhārata, from the midst of Śālmalīdvīpa,
Govardhana took birth from the wife of Droṇācala.
O King of Videha, Pulastya brought him to the region of Vraja in Bhārata; his arrival has already been described by me to you. (45)
Reflecting on the curse, the Supreme Lord considered how this [earth] might once again become eager to expand, or how it might become a covering for the world, just as it was before.
He gave it for the sake of destruction to the son of Droṇa. || 46 ||

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Origin of the King of Mountains," in the Girirāja-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā, within the dialogue between the glorious Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Oṃ. May this be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is Tat-Sat.
Śrī Nārada said: In this very context, they cite this ancient history,
by the mere hearing of which great sin is destroyed.
A certain Brāhmaṇa named Vijaya, who resided on the banks of the Gautamī,
came to Mathurā, the destroyer of sins, in order to collect his own debt.
Having finished his business and returning home, he went to the slope of Govardhana;
there, O King of Mithilā, he picked up a single round stone.
Gradually departing from the district of Vraja toward the forest region,
he beheld before him an approaching Rākṣasa of terrifying form.
He whose face was on his chest, who had three feet and six arms,
three hands, thick lips, and a nose as high as his hand.
Seven cubits tall, with a lolling tongue and body hair like thorns,
they had long, reddish eyes and curved, terrifying teeth.
O King, making a gurgling sound and being hungry, the Rākṣasa came before the Brāhmaṇa who was standing there.
He struck him with a stone produced from the king of mountains;
by the touch of that mountain-king’s rock, he abandoned his demonic body.
With eyes as broad as lotus petals and a dark, beautiful form, he wears a forest garland and yellow garments; he is crowned and adorned with earrings.
Holding a flute and a staff in his hand, like another god of love,
he stood with palms joined in reverence and bowed repeatedly to the brāhmaṇa.
The Siddha said:
"Blessed are you, O best of Brahmins, who are devoted to the protection of others;
by you, O high-minded one, I have indeed been liberated from the state of a Rākṣasa."
By the mere touch of the stone, my welfare was indeed restored;
for no one at all is capable of liberating me except you.
The illustrious Brāhmaṇa said:
"I am amazed by your words; I am not capable of releasing you.
I do not know the fruit of touching a stone; tell me, O observer of noble vows. (13)
The Siddha said:
The glorious Govardhana mountain is the form of Hari, the king of mountains;
by the mere sight of it, a person attains the fulfillment of their purpose.
Whatever fruit a person obtains on a pilgrimage to Gandhamādana,
ten million times that merit is gained by the sight of the King of Mountains.
O Brahmin, the fruit of the penance performed for five thousand years at Kedāra, a man obtains that very same fruit in an instant at Govardhana.
Whatever fruit there is from giving a load of gold on the Malaya mountain,
ten million times that merit is gained by staying for a month on the King of Mountains (Girirāja).
He who gives gold as a sacrificial fee on Mount Maṅgalaprastha attains the same form as Viṣṇu, even if he is burdened with hundreds of sins.
Indeed, by the sight of the King of Mountains, a man attains that supreme state;
there exists no other sacred ford (tīrtha) equal in merit to the King of Mountains. (19)
A man who gives ten million cows adorned with golden horns at Mount Ṛṣabha, Mount Kūṭaka, and likewise at Mount Kolaka; || 20 ||
Even he who diligently honors Brahmins would obtain great merit;
however, O twice-born one, on Mount Govardhana, the merit is a hundred thousand times greater than that.
Furthermore, during the pilgrimage to Ṛṣyamūka, Sahya, and Devagiri,
one obtains the merit and the fruit of traveling across the entire earth.
The fruit of that pilgrimage to the King of Mountains is ten million times greater;
there has never been, nor will there ever be, a holy place equal to the King of Mountains.
On Śrīśaila, at the Vidyādhara pool, the virtuous man who performs an ablution for ten years shall obtain the fruit of a hundred sacrifices.
A person who performs a bath for even a single day at Pucchakuṇḍa on Govardhana directly attains the merit of ten million sacrifices; of this there is no doubt.
By performing the horse sacrifice (Aśvamedha) on Mount Veṅkaṭa, at Vāridhāra, on Mahendra, or on the Vindhya mountain, a man shall indeed become a lord of heaven.
He who, having performed a sacrifice on this Govardhana and having given excellent sacrificial fees,
secures a place in heaven, shall attain the abode of Viṣṇu.

O best of the twice-born, [he was born] at Citrakūṭa on the full-moon day of the month of Pauṣa; on the ninth day of the month of Āśvina by the Payasvinī river; and on the third day of Vaiśākha at Pāriyātra.
On the full moon day at Kukkurādri, on the twelfth day at Nīlādri, and on the seventh day at Indrakīla, bathing, giving gifts, and the performance of austerities [yield great fruit]. (29)
All that becomes multiplied ten millionfold in Bhārata;
but on Govardhana, O twice-born one, all that becomes infinite.
At the Godāvarī when Jupiter is in Leo, at Māyāpurī when Jupiter is in Aquarius,
at Puṣkara under the Puṣya asterism, and at Kurukṣetra during a solar eclipse— 31.
During a lunar eclipse at Kāśī, likewise at Naimiṣa in the month of Phālguna;
on the eleventh day at Śūkara, and on the full moon of Kārtika at Gaṇamuktida.
On the eighth day of the month of Madhu in the city, on the twelfth day at Khāṇḍava, and on the full moon of Kārtika at the great banyan tree of Vaṭeśvara; || 33 ||
At Prayāga during the month of Makara, at Barhiṣmatī during the Vaidhṛti yoga,
on the banks of the Sarayū in Ayodhyā on the day of Śrī Rāmanavamī.
Thus, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight dedicated to Śiva, in the auspicious forest of Vaijanātha;
likewise, on the new moon day falling on a Monday, at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean.
On the tenth day at Setubandha, and on the seventh day at Śrīraṅga—at these places, charity, austerity, bathing, recitation, and the worship of gods and brahmins [yield great fruit]. (36)
O best of the twice-born, all that becomes multiplied ten millionfold here;
one obtains merit equal to that on the excellent Govardhana mountain. (37)
O Lord of Mithilā, he who bathes in the pure Govindakuṇḍa with his mind fixed on Kṛṣṇa attains the same form as Kṛṣṇa; of this there is no doubt.
Thousands of horse-sacrifices and hundreds of Rājasūya sacrifices do not equal the Mānasī Gaṅgā here on our mountain.
O Brahmin, you have personally beheld the King of Mountains and touched him; thereafter you bathed there. There is no one on earth superior even to you.
If you do not believe me, look at this supreme sinner who has attained a form identical to Kṛṣṇa through the touch of the Govardhana stone. (41)
Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Greatness of Girirāja," in the Śrī Garga Saṃhitā, within the Girirāja-khaṇḍa, in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Om. May this be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is Tat-Sat.
Śrī Nārada said:
O King, having heard these words of the Siddha, the Brāhmaṇa was filled with wonder;
he, who was already conversant with the power of the king of mountains, questioned him again.
The Brāhmaṇa said:
Who were you, O sir, in your previous birth? What sin was committed by you?
Tell me everything, O highly fortunate one, for you are truly one of divine vision.
The Siddha said:
"In a previous birth, I was a wealthy Vaiśya, the son of a great Vaiśya; from my very childhood, I was devoted to gambling and skilled in the assemblies of libertines. (3)
"O twice-born one, devoted to courtesans, treading a wicked path, and overwhelmed by the intoxication of wine, I was constantly rebuked by my mother, my father, and even my wife. (4)
Once, O Brahmin, my parents were killed by me through the administration of poison, and likewise my wife was killed with a sword on the road.
Having seized all that wealth, the wicked man, who was utterly merciless and engaged in the deeds of a bandit, departed for the southern direction accompanied by the courtesan.
Once, indeed, I threw a prostitute into a blind well;
for as a robber, I have killed men by the hundreds with nooses.
O Brahmin, out of greed for wealth, you have committed a hundred killings of Brahmins,
as well as thousands of killings of Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras.
Once, having gone to the forest to kill deer in order to bring meat, I was bitten by a serpent that had been stepped upon; thus, struck down by that wicked [creature], I met my death.
Having struck me with terrible mallets, the fearsome messengers of Yama bound me, a wicked man of great sin, and led me to hell.
Having fallen into the great hell Kumbhīpāka for a Manvantara,
that wicked man experienced extreme suffering for one Kalpa in the Taptasūrmi hell.
I fell into each of the eighty-four hundred thousand hells one by one, and I emerged from them at the will of Yama.
Then, in the land of Bhārata, I encountered the latent impressions of my karma;
ten times I was a boar, and I was a tiger for a hundred births.
For a hundred births I was a camel, for a hundred births a buffalo, and for a thousand births I was a serpent, killed by wicked men. (14)
Thus, O twice-born one, at the end of ten thousand years in that waterless forest,
such a Rākṣasa was born— a deformed and great villain.
Having indeed mounted the body of a certain Śūdra,
he went to Vraja from the auspicious vicinity of the Yamunā near Vṛndāvana.
Dark-complexioned black attendants arose with staffs in their hands;
beaten and overpowered by them, I fled from the land of Vraja. (17)
"O Sage, having been hungry for many days, I came here intending to devour you; however, I was struck by you with a stone from the king of mountains."
"By the grace of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, true auspiciousness has indeed come to me.
Śrī Nārada said: While he was speaking thus, from Goloka, a great chariot [arrived].
Resembling a thousand suns and accompanied by ten thousand horses.
O King, he bore the sound of a thousand wheels, was adorned by a circle of a hundred thousand attendants,
and was most enchanting with a network of anklets and tiny bells.
