"Eat [the fruit] as a result of the sin of theft; let my word not be false."
Worship the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; He will grant you liberation.
Having spoken thus, O King, when the great sage, the god Trita, had departed, ||7||
Kakṣīvān, assuming the form of a conch shell, fell into the lake.
Proclaiming "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa," he remained thus for a hundred years. ||8||
The most perfectly complete one, the Lord in person, who is affectionate toward his devotees.
Having arrived at the shore of the lake, he granted them fearlessness, saying, "Do not be afraid."
Having heard that voice, deep as the roar of a cloud, the aquatic creature—
He cried out, "Save me! Save me! O God of gods, Lord of the World!"
The Lord, the Master, [embraced her] with an arm that shone with the luster of the coils of the king of serpents.
Devoted to compassion, he lifted up Śaṅkha, who was devoted [to him], like an elephant.
At that very moment, having abandoned his form as Śaṅkha, he assumed a divine form.
And when he, having bowed with palms joined in reverence, offered praise to Hari; ||12||
Kakṣīvān said:
O Vāsudeva, salutations to you; O Govinda, Supreme Person!
O you who are compassionate toward the wretched, O Lord of the wretched, O Lord of Dvārakā, O Supreme Sovereign!
To the one who is eternal, the bestower of the eternal state, and the remover of Prahlāda’s suffering.
Salutations to you, the deliverer of the elephant; salutations to you, the one who knows strength and who subdues Bala. || 14 ||
Salutations to Hari, who protected the garment of Draupadī.
To the one who assisted the Pāṇḍavas during their residence in the poison-chamber, the fire, and the forest; ||15||
And to the protector of the Yadavas, and to the guardian of the cowherds against Indra.
And salutations again and again to the teacher, the mother, and the twice-born, as well as to the giver of a son. ||16||
To the one who effects the liberation of kings afflicted by the confinement of Jarāsaṃdha.
To the one who directly rescued Nṛga, and to the remover of Sudāman’s distress.
Salutation to Vāsudeva Kṛṣṇa and to Saṃkarṣaṇa.
Salutations to you, the fourfold manifestation, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. ||18||
You alone are my mother and you alone are my father;
you alone are my kinsman and you alone are my friend.
You alone are knowledge, you alone are wealth; you alone are everything to me, O God of gods. (19)
The venerable Nārada said:
Having thus praised Hari, O King, Kakṣīvān was filled with love.
Having ascended the excellent celestial chariot while the Yādavas looked on.
Illuminating the ten directions, he possessed a radiance equal to a hundred suns.
He went to the realm of Viṣṇu, which is free from all afflictions.
O Lord of Mithilā, it was there that the lifting of the Śaṅkha mountain was performed by Hari.
Therefore, that highly meritorious holy site became renowned as Śaṅkhoddhāra.
That best of men who hears this narrative of Śaṅkhoddhāra,
One certainly obtains the fruit of the Śaṅkhoddhāra bath; of this there is no doubt. || 23 ||
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Resurrection of Śaṅkha," in the dialogue between Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Śrīdvārakākhaṇḍa of the glorious Gārgasaṃhitā. || 12 ||
The illustrious Nārada said:
O King of great intelligence, listen also to the majesty of Prabhāsa.
It removes all sins, is meritorious, and is the supreme increaser of splendors. || 1 ||
When Jupiter is in Leo in the Godāvarī, and Saturn is in Aquarius in the field of Hara (Kāśī).
Likewise, at Kurukṣetra during a solar eclipse, and at Kāśī during a lunar eclipse.
O King, whatever merit a person obtains from bathing and giving gifts—
Therefore, at Prabhāsa, there is merit a hundred times greater day after day.
Having bathed there, the Lord of the Stars (the Moon), who had been seized by consumption due to Dakṣa’s curse,
was instantly freed from that affliction and once again attained the rise of his digits.
O King, that place where the Sarasvatī is visible is most supremely meritorious.
Having bathed in it, even a sinful man becomes manifestly composed of Brahman. ||5||
O King, on its bank stands a tree known by the name Bodhapippala.
Wherein the auspicious Bhāgavata was given by Kṛṣṇa to Uddhava.
Having bowed to and worshipped that Śrībodhapippala tree according to the prescribed rite, and having touched it;
Whoever hears this Bhāgavata Purāṇa, which is equal to the Veda; ||7||
Whether it be a verse, half a verse, or a quarter-verse, he should remain silent with his mind restrained.
O King, the supreme station of Viṣṇu shall reside in his hand.
On the full moon day of the month of Proṣṭhapada, [one should offer] together with a golden lion.
He who gives [this] to a devotee of the Lord goes to the supreme goal. ||9||
By those who have never heard the Śrīmad Bhāgavata Purāṇa anywhere, [the truth remains unknown].
The birth of those men who dwell upon the earth has passed in vain.
Those by whom the Bhāgavata Purāṇa has not been heard, and those by whom the Ancient Person (Puruṣa) has not been worshipped;
The oblation was not offered into the mouths of those gods on earth; thus, the birth of those men has gone in vain. (11)
In Dvārāvatī is the king of holy places, the confluence of the Gomatī and the Sindhu.
Having bathed there, a person goes to Vaikuṇṭha, the stainless abode.
The merit born of a hundred horse-sacrifices is found at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean.
Therefore, at the confluence of the Gomatī and the Sindhu, it is a thousand times greater.
In this very context, they cite this ancient history.
By the mere hearing of which, one is liberated from the torment of sin. ||14||
In Hastināpura, there was a preeminent Vaiśya who was the master of the royal highway.
Endowed with great reverence, he was like Dhanada, the lord of treasures. ||15||
He was devoted to the company of courtesans and skilled in the assemblies of parasites.
Addicted to gambling and play, he was possessed by greed, delusion, and pride. ||16||
He was a speaker of falsehoods, exceedingly wicked, and always devoted to evil deeds.
He gave wealth neither to the Brahmins, nor to the ancestors, nor to the gods.
Upon seeing the discourse of Hari from afar, he indeed departed quickly to a great distance.
He did not even serve his parents, nor did he give wealth to his sons. || 18 ||
Having abandoned his wife, that wealthy, evil-minded, and wicked man became divided.
Due to his attachment to a courtesan, even half of his wealth went to ruin. || 9 ||
Half was taken away by thieves, and a small portion fell of its own accord upon the earth.
Prosperity increases through merit; it certainly diminishes through sin.
Thus that great rogue became impoverished and addicted to courtesans.
In that beautiful city of Gajāhvaya, he indeed committed acts of theft.
Having bound him with ropes, the king [restrained] him as he was committing the act of theft.
Śantanu, the lord of kings, banished him from the country.
Even though he lived in the forest, he indeed committed violence against living beings.
When the twelve thousand-year period of the nine-year rain-cloud has passed, it is equal [to the duration of the others]. || 23 ||
But a Vaiśya, afflicted by famine, went toward the western direction.
He too was killed in the forest by a lion with a blow of its paw.
At that very moment, the messengers of Yama bound him with nooses and held him face downwards.
Beating them with lashes of whips, they led them along the path of Yama.
Then a certain large vulture [saw] the flesh of that arm.
Having seized it, he immediately flew into the sky, devouring it with the tip of his beak.
Other birds, free from desire for flesh, flew away distressed, seeking their own prey.
Thus, when a great clamor arose, it was produced by Śaṅkhacihna and the others. ||27||
He did not abandon the flesh from his mouth; he went toward the western direction.
Even from being struck by a vulture of equal size but with a sharp beak, [he was saved]. || 28 ||
Flesh falling from his mouth at the confluence of the Gomatī and the Sindhu.
When his flesh has been washed at a sacred bathing place, this great sinner shall indeed become a Vaiśya. ||29||
Having himself cut those nooses and become a four-armed deity, he [acted].
While the messengers of Yama were looking on, he ascended the celestial chariot.
Illuminating all directions, he went to the supreme abode of Hari.
A person who hears the greatness of the confluence of the Gomatī and the Sindhu, [attains great merit].
Completely liberated from all sins, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu. ||32||

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Confluence of the Prabhāsa, Sarasvatī, Bodha, Pippala, Gomatī, and Sindhu," in the Śrīdvārakākhaṇḍa of the illustrious Gargasahitā, within the dialogue between Nārada and Bahulāśva. || 13 ||
Śrī Nārada said:
O giver of honor, listen to the majesty of the ocean at Dvārāvatī;
it is remembered as holy, removing all sins, and bestowing the fruit of bathing there. || 1 ||

On the full moon day of the month of Mādhava, the observer of the vow who, having bathed in the lord of rivers, bows down and worships according to the prescribed rites, and he who makes a gift of jewels; || 2 ||
O lord of the earth, three gods dwell within his body;
by the mere sight of him, a man attains the fulfillment of his purpose.
By the mere touch of his body, one is instantly liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin;
wherever he goes, the earth there becomes auspicious.
Indeed, even a sinful person who has killed the world, upon seeing him,
dies and cuts through the mass of his sins, for he attains supreme liberation.
Now listen, O giver of honor, to the majesty of Mount Raivata,
which removes all sins, is meritorious, and bestows both liberation and worldly enjoyment.
The wise son of Gautama, a Vaiṣṇava named Medhāvī,
performed penance on the Vindhya mountain for ten million years.
The sage Apāntaratamas himself came to see him;
yet even that wise one, fierce in his asceticism, did not rise from his seat.
Filled with rage, he cursed Apāntaratamas, saying:
"O non-devotee of the virtuous, O evil-souled one, you who are arrogant because of the power of your own asceticism! (9)
"Your stability here shall be like that of a mountain; therefore, O evil-minded one, become a mountain!
Having spoken thus, the sage Apāntaratama himself then departed.
The wise one attained the state of a mountain and became the son of Śrīśaila;
possessing great intellect and remembering his former births, this was due to the power of his devotion to Viṣṇu. || 11 ||
Once, having heard from my mouth the greatness of the city of Dvārakā, he said to the king: "Go quickly to Raivata."
Speak my request, O you who are compassionate toward the greatly distressed;
may this king of great power become gracious. (13)
"By him I shall be led to dwell in the city of Hari"—
having heard this, I, who bring peace to the devotees of Viṣṇu, [acted accordingly].
When Raivata had thus spoken and the supreme word was uttered, he, being pleased, said: "O King, there is no mountain here at all."
"I shall establish it there, having uprooted it by the strength of my arms and raised it high";
thus he made this vow at Dvārakā. (16)
O King, when that best of monarchs had set out to steal it,
I arrived from my former place in the city of Śrīśaila.
Even though I am fond of strife, I related the entire account, including the king's theft, to the high-souled Śrīśaila.
Śrīśaila, rebuking him out of affection for his son, said: "Where indeed are you going—to Sumeru, the king of mountains, or to Himavat, the lord of peaks? (19)
The righteous Śrīśaila, overwhelmed with affection for his son, said:
"This one was given to me by fate; I have no other sons, nor many."
When the exceedingly powerful King Raivata arrived to seize him,
my son went abroad because of that high-souled king.
Overcome by affection for my son, I have come to you for refuge;
having quickly conquered that Raivata, you ought to give me back my son. (22)
And due to their birth, those two— Sumeru and Himācala—
surrounded by hundreds of thousands of mountains, quickly arrived to fight.
Then, having uprooted that mountain with his two arms like Hanumān,
and having lifted it upward by force, the king set his mind on departing.
And at that very moment, seeing the mountains approaching, bearing weapons and missiles,
he let out a loud, boisterous laugh like a flash of lightning falling upon himself.
By that roar, the entire universe, along with the seven worlds and their subterranean realms, resounded;
at that very moment, the weapons fell of their own accord from their hands.
When those mountains were rendered weaponless, though they repeatedly let out loud roars,
they struck him on the path with their fists and knees as he proceeded along with his mountain.
Just as in the past he had followed the mighty Hanumān,
even though struck by them, the king did not let go of the mountain from the tips of his hands.

Having heard from my mouth about the mountain's exertion against the king, the Blessed Lord Śrī Hari, who is affectionate toward His devotees, immediately [set out] for the sake of assisting His devotee. (29)
Having arrived even by way of the sky and bestowed his supreme splendor,
he granted fearlessness, saying "Do not fear," and quickly vanished.
When Lord Hari had departed, [the demon], endowed with the power of the Blessed One,
held a mountain on one hand with a fist that struck like a thunderbolt.
Like a most powerful wielder of the thunderbolt, he swiftly struck Mount Sumeru;
by the blow of his fist, Meru was thrown into a state of agitation.
Having cast Himavat to the surface of the earth by the force of his arms,
he who was intoxicated with the pride of battle crushed others, such as Vindhya and the rest, with his feet.
And all those [mountains], including the Vindhya and others, were crushed by the blow of his foot;
terrified with fear, they abandoned the battlefield and fled in the ten directions.
Having thus conquered that host of mountains, Raivata— who himself resembled a mountain—
caused that mountain to fall among the Ānartas with shouts of victory.
O King, that mountain named Raivata became known as Raivataka;
devoted to Hari, this preeminent mountain shines resplendent at Dvārāvatī.
By the mere sight of it, one is liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin;
by touching it, a person obtains the fruit of a hundred sacrifices. || 37 ||
Having undertaken a pilgrimage and having circumambulated it with a bowed face, one who gives food to a Brāhmaṇa goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. || 38 ||

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Jewel-Mine and Mount Raivataka," in the Dvārakākhaṇḍa of the glorious Garga Saṃhitā, within the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Śrī Nārada said: On that mountain, a sacrificial site (yajñatīrtha) was established by Raivata in ancient times;
having performed a single sacrifice there, one obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices.
O King, on Mount Raivataka there is a sacred ford named Kapiṭaṅka, which originated from the leap of a monkey and destroys all sins.
There, the wicked monkey named Dvivida, a friend of the demon Bhauma,
was slain by Rāma with a fist-strike that fell like a thunderbolt.
Even he who had treated the virtuous with contempt attained immediate liberation;
O lord of men, the gods always come there to bathe.
The merit obtained from the gift of ten million cows during the pilgrimage to Kalaviṅka is doubled at the auspicious forest named Daṇḍaka. (5)
Therefore, a human being obtains fourfold merit in the great forest named Saindhava,
and fivefold merit at Jambumārga.
Therefore, ten times that merit is remembered for the forest named Puṣkara; ten times that merit is obtained by the pilgrimage to Utpalāvarta.
Therefore, O King of Videha, it is remembered that the merit in the Naimiṣa forest is tenfold;
the merit in Kapiṭaṅka is a hundredfold greater than that.
In Dvārakā, there is the Nṛgakūpa, the most excellent of all holy places (tīrthas);
by the mere sight of it, O Brahmins, one is liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Out of ignorance, he gave a cow to a Brāhmaṇa who was also a Brāhmaṇa;
by that sin, he indeed assumed the body of a chameleon in a well.
Nṛga, the best among givers, then fell for the duration of four yugas;
Śrī Kṛṣṇa brought about his deliverance while the virtuous looked on.
O Lord of the Earth, from that day forth Nṛga’s well became a sacred pilgrimage site;
one should perform a ritual bath there on the full moon day of the month of Kārtika.
A man who performs even a single gift of a cow there according to the prescribed rite is liberated from the sins committed over ten million births; of this there is no doubt. (13)
He indeed obtains the merit born of giving ten million cows; of this there is no doubt.
Now hear the supreme, sin-destroying majesty of Gopībhūmi.
Merely by hearing of it, one is liberated from the bondage of karma;
because the cowherd women (gopīs) dwelt there, it is known as Gopībhuva.
The supreme Gopīcandana is produced from the body-unguent of the Gopīs;
one whose limbs are smeared with Gopīcandana obtains the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā.
The merit that one gains from bathing in great rivers day after day is attained by him who is always marked with the seals of Gopīcandana.

Thousands of horse-sacrifices, hundreds of Rājasūya sacrifices, all the gifts at sacred fords, and likewise all religious vows—these have indeed been performed by him constantly; he has attained his life's purpose, without a doubt. (18)
The dust of Citrakūṭa is said to possess twice the merit of the Gaṅgā;
the dust arising from Pañcavaṭī possesses ten times the merit of that.
Therefore, the dust of Gopīcandana possesses a hundredfold merit;
know that Gopīcandana is equal to the dust of Vṛndāvana.
If one whose limbs are smeared with Gopīcandana is joined even by hundreds of sins, Yama is not able to take him away; how much less so his messengers?
The sinner who constantly wears gopīcandana goes to the abode of Hari, Goloka, which is beyond primordial nature (prakṛti). || 22 ||
There was a king of the Sindhudeśa known as Dīrghabāhu;
he was unrighteous in conduct, evil-minded, and always devoted to the company of courtesans.
Indeed, in that land of Bhārata-varṣa, a hundred killings of Brahmins were committed by him; ten killings of pregnant women were also committed by that evil-minded one.
While out hunting, he killed a tawny cow with a multitude of arrows;
desiring to hunt, he had gone forth mounted upon a horse from the Sindhu region. (25)
Once, out of greed for the kingdom, the minister, filled with rage,
slew that great villain in a forest region with a sharp-edged sword.
Seeing him fallen upon the earth and overtaken by death, the followers of Yama bound him and led him to the city of Yama, exulting among themselves.
Seeing the sinner standing before him, the powerful King Yama quickly said to Citragupta: "What indeed is the appropriate torment for this man?"
Citragupta said:
"O Great King, let him be cast into the eighty-four lakhs of hells without doubt, for as long as the moon and sun endure."
In this land of Bhārata-varṣa, he did not perform even a moment’s virtuous deed;
rather, he committed the murder of a woman ten months pregnant and the slaughter of a tawny cow.
Likewise, having committed thousands of killings of forest deer, he is therefore a great sinner who reviles the gods and the twice-born. (31)
Śrī Nārada said: Then, by the command of Yama, the messengers led that man, who was the very embodiment of sin,
to a great pit filled with boiling oil extending for a thousand yojanas.
They cast them into the Kumbhīpāka hell, where the foam surged and splashed;
yet the fire, equal to the conflagration at the end of an aeon, instantly became cool.
O Vaideha, because of that falling and the hurling of Prahlāda,
the messengers of Yama immediately reported the marvel to the Great-Souled One.
"By this man, no good deed was ever performed on earth, even for a moment," Dharmarāja constantly reflected thus while Citragupta stood by.
Having duly honored Vyāsa upon his arrival in the assembly hall, O King, the righteous and high-minded Dharmarāja bowed to him and questioned him. (36)
Yama said:
"By this sinner, no meritorious deed was ever performed in the past;
he shall now fall into the great abyss of Kumbhīpāka, where the boiling liquid overflows with froth like leaping fire. (37)
"By his hurling [it], the fire has instantly become cool;
my mind is distressed by this doubt, of this there is no uncertainty. (38)
Śrī Vyāsa said:
O great king, the subtle course of both sin and merit is known by the wise who are the best among those learned in all the scriptures, as is the course of Brahman. (39)
By the power of destiny, he has indeed acquired merit of his own accord;
listen, O high-minded one, to that merit by which he has become purified. (40)
Wherever the clay of Dvārakā fell from someone's hand, right there this sinful man died and became purified by its power. || 41 ||
A man whose limbs are smeared with gopīcandana becomes Nārāyaṇa himself;
by the mere sight of him, one is immediately liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Śrī Nārada said:
Having heard this, Dharmarāja specifically brought him there,
placed him upon a celestial chariot that moves at will, and sent him to Vaikuṇṭha, which transcends primordial nature (prakṛti).
He, whose fame rests upon Gopīcandana, suddenly dispatched it.
Thus, O King, has the glory of Gopīcandana been recounted to you. (44)
That best of men who hears the greatness of Gopīcandana goes to the supreme abode of the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa. || 45 ||

Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "The Greatness of Kapiṭaṅka, Nṛgakūpa, and the Land of the Gopīs," in the Dvārakākhaṇḍa of the glorious Garga Saṃhitā, within the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Śrī Nārada said:
O high-minded King, listen to the majesty of Siddhāśrama, by the mere remembrance of which one is liberated from all sins. (1)
Those who know the ancient lore declare that this place, named Siddhāśrama, is such that by touching it, one shall never again be separated from Hari anywhere.
By seeing it, one attains *sālokya*; likewise, by touching it, *sāmīpya*;
by bathing there, *sārūpya*; and by dwelling there, one attains *sāyujya*.
Having heard the greatness of that sacred ford from the mouth of Candrānanā, Rādhā, overwhelmed by her longing for Kṛṣṇa, resolved to bathe there.
During the solar eclipse in the month of Mādhava, on her journey to Śrīsiddhāśrama,
Rādhā rose from the grove of plantain trees and set her mind upon bathing.
Together with a hundred groups of gopīs and all the hosts of cowherds,
a hundred years passed due to the cause of Śrīdāman’s curse.
The virtuous Śrī Rādhā, mounted upon a palanquin and fanned with chowries and a parasol,
went to Siddhāśrama, a great sacred site among the Ānartas.
O King, right there the Blessed One, surrounded by the Yādavas and sixteen thousand women, arrived for the purpose of the procession.
And those cowherds who were most powerful, numbering in the millions and bearing weapons in their hands,
guarded Siddhāśrama on all sides by the command of Rādhikā.
Likewise, the hundredfold groups of cowherd women, mighty and holding canes in their hands,
attended upon Rādhā as she was bathing according to the prescribed rites at Siddhāśrama.
As those residents of Dvārakā stood there desiring to bathe,
the wives of the Blessed One entered while they were being struck with weapons and canes.
They asked, "Who is this woman bathing?"— she whose power was truly extraordinary,
out of respect for whom all the best of the Yādavas here trembled.
"Aha! To whom is she dear, what is her name, and where does she dwell?
For you, O Blessed One, son of Devakī, are omniscient; please tell us. (13)
The Blessed Lord said:
She is the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, Rādhā herself, the delighter of Kīrti;
she is the Queen of Vraja, my beloved, the supreme sovereign of the gopīs.
Having arrived at Siddhāśrama with the groups of cowherd girls to bathe, she possesses a wondrous majesty because of whose weight these [mountains] tremble as they move. 15.
Having heard the words of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the beautiful Satyabhāmā,
who was proud of her own beauty and youth, then spoke softly to her co-wives.
Is Rādhā truly beautiful, or am I not beautiful?
She was previously sought after by many, honored for her qualities of beauty and magnanimity. (17)
"O friends, it was because of my form that Śatadhanvan died;
formerly, both Akrūra and Kṛtavarman fled. (18)
Day after day, he spontaneously produces eight bhāras of gold;
[he destroys] famine, calamities from enemies, and all inauspicious mental and physical afflictions.
There are no sorcerers where that jewel remains worshipped;
it was given by my father as part of his dowry—the very Syamantaka itself.
Because of that, all wonderful prosperity has been born even in my house;
through supreme love, she [the Goddess] travels upon the back of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s Garuḍa.
I witnessed the great battle with the Bhauma Asura and the city of Prāgjyotiṣa; by my grace, you have also come from that city.
All of them have undoubtedly attained the status of being wives of Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
moreover, out of respect for me, he indeed gave the umbrella to Śakra.
The two earrings were indeed given to the goddess Aditi out of a desire for my pleasure;
likewise, the elephants born of Airāvata and the riches of the Bhauma Asura.
Bringer by my will by the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Hari has, for my sake, waged great enmity even against Indra. (25)
The lord of trees, the Pārijātaka, dwells eternally at my door;
yet it is by my devotion as a faithful wife alone that this Śrī Kṛṣṇa has been brought under my influence.
Equipped with all necessary furnishings, it was offered to Nārada;
for who else could possess dignity and splendor equal to mine? (27)
To whom would the magnificence of Rādhā’s form not belong? How can it even be described, since Caidya and others fought against her in battle on account of that very form? 28.
"O fair-browed one, how is it that you, Rukmiṇī, are not beautiful?
She is but a cowherd's daughter, while you, my friends, are indeed princesses; you are all blessed and worthy of honor, the best among proud women. (29)
While Satyabhāmā was speaking thus, O Lord of Mithilā,
all the excellent women, headed by Rukmiṇī, became filled with indignation.
Proud of their noble lineage, skill, virtue, wealth, beauty, and youth,
the eight principal queens spoke to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the bestower of honor.
The queens said:
"We have previously heard from your mouth that the supreme form of Rādhā has been remembered—that she in whom you are always enamored, and who is always enamored of you. (32)
We wish to see that Rādhā, your beloved who dwells in Vraja;
she is exhausted by separation from you and has come here to bathe. (33)
Śrī Nārada said: Having said, "So be it," Śrī Kṛṣṇa, surrounded by his principal queens and accompanied by sixteen thousand women, went to see Rādhā.
In the beautiful camp of the illustrious Hema, adorned with flags and banners, rich with the splendor of the lunar orb, auspicious and covered with canopies; || 35 ||
Where there was a curtain of pearls and an auspicious covering of cloths,
rich with jasmine and its nectar, and filled everywhere with fragrance.
Because of that, Śṛṅgāvalī raised a great and sweet clamor;
there, Rādhā, the crowned queen whose mind was captivated by Śrī Kṛṣṇa, [was present].
There she was fanned by her female companions with divine fans made of swan-feathers,
while they moved here and there carrying umbrellas and swings.
Wearing earrings like the rising sun, enchanting with a garland of lightning, she resembles ten million moons; she is slender, with a delicate form. (39)
With their own beautiful fingertips, they slowly and gently supported her most delicate lotus-feet upon the lovely flower-strewn ground.
O great king, seeing Rādhikā from afar, the thousands of Kṛṣṇa’s wives fainted, utterly bewildered by her beauty.
Their luster eclipsed by his splendor, like the hosts of stars before the sun, they all, their pride in their beauty vanished, spoke to one another: || 42 ||
Oh, such a form as this is indeed a marvel not seen even in the three worlds!
Just as it was heard of, so too has it been seen—peerless and captivating.
While he was speaking thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s attendants arrived and embraced the eyes of the gopīs and the princesses. (44)
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, titled "The Vision of Rādhā’s Form," in the Dvārakā-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā, within the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Śrī Nārada said:
Seeing Śrī Kṛṣṇa arrived accompanied by his principal queen, the gopīs, filled with great joy, then raised a cry of "Victory! Victory! (Jaya Jaya).
Suddenly, Rādhā circumambulated Śrī Hari with palms joined in reverence,
shedding tears of bliss from her two lotus-like eyes.
Its feet were inlaid with syamantaka gems, its surface was set with cintāmaṇi jewels,
its center shone with rubies, and it was as circular as the orb of the moon.
Its surface was inlaid with *kaustubha* gems, it was adorned with a circle of *kumbha* jewels, enriched with *pārijātaka* flowers, and possessed a parasol dripping with nectar.
Having offered him the lion-throne, she spoke with a smiling face:
"Today my birth has become fruitful; today my ascetic penance has become fruitful."
"O Hari, now that you have come, my dharma has become fruitful today.
Blessed is the bath at Siddhāśrama; it has become wonderfully successful.
Yet, even by me, no devotion was offered to you, who assist your devotees."
O Lord, you have created many allies for me on this earth,
by whom even Kaṃsa, the conqueror of the world, was struck with fear.
O Hari, Śaṅkhacūḍa was slain by you at my word;
yet, O Lord, out of love for me, you displayed your divine majesty in Vraja.
O Lord, you have forcibly brought about the shattering of Śakra’s pride as well,
by holding up Mount Govardhana while protecting Vraja for my sake.
O Lord, that you were embraced at will by the gopīs during the rāsa dance and brought under their influence—
this deed of yours is a mockery of the world of men.
Speaking thus, Rādhā, acting swiftly at the command of the moon-faced one,
respectfully looked upon the wives of Hari and paid them due honor.
Having met with Bhaiṣmī, Jāmbavatī, Bhāmā, Satyā, Bhadrā, Lakṣmaṇā,
Kālindī, and Mitravindā, they all gathered together with one another.
And she, filled with joy, embraced with her arms the sixteen thousand women and Rohiṇī herself, who were composed of the bliss of love.
Rādhā said: Just as the moon is one, yet there are many cakora birds;
just as the sun is one, yet there may be many eyes.
The Blessed Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra is thus alone, while we, his sisters, are many devotees.
Just as a bee [discerns] the power of a lotus,
or as one who examines [a gem] discerns the power of a jewel, or as a wise man discerns the power of knowledge;
And the power of poetry, as the lord of poets [described]. || 15 ||
For just as a connoisseur among thousands of people truly perceives the power of flavor, so too do the daughters of the king.
A devotee of Kṛṣṇa [perceives] the power of Kṛṣṇa upon the earth. || 16 ||
Śrī Nārada said: Having then heard those words of Rādhā, Rukmiṇī, the daughter of Bhīṣmaka,
together with her co-wives, spoke to the lotus-eyed Rādhā.
Rukmiṇī said:
"O Rādhā, daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, you are blessed;
for by the power of your devotion, He has been brought under your control."
He of whom the three worlds speak in abundance— he alone speaks of your news.
Just as we have heard of your characteristics of being a monkey, so indeed they are seen; it is not at all surprising.
Go quickly now to our camps where we are.
They have come here respectfully to lead you away. || 19 ||
Śrī Nārada said:
Having spoken thus, the high-souled Bhīṣma’s daughter respectfully brought Rādhā, the daughter of Kīrti, to her own quarters.
In a pavilion auspicious on all sides, perfumed with the filaments of lotuses, he lay upon a golden couch,
soft as a śirīṣa flower, provided with a pillow.
Having worshipped according to the prescribed rites during the night, the virtuous lady, together with her co-wives, comfortably dressed herself in garments, garlands, ornaments, and other finery.
Having honored each of the hundred groups of gopīs individually and engaged in various kinds of conversation with those beloved of Kṛṣṇa,
they then joyfully returned to their respective camps.
Having gone to Kṛṣṇa’s side and seeing that he was awake, Bhaiṣmī said to Kṛṣṇa, "O Lord, why do you not lie down? (24)
The Blessed Lord said:
"O Queen of Vraja, O fair-browed one, by your welcoming advances, your outpourings of affection, and your consolation, she has indeed been honored by you; thus, she has become supremely pleased."
She indeed always drinks auspicious milk at the beginning of her sleep and other times;
however, it is said that today, O fair-browed one, she has not drunk any milk.
Therefore, O high-minded one, sleep did not come to her eyes;
for that reason, O daughter of Bhīṣmaka, sleep has not come to me either. (27)
Śrī Nārada said:
Having heard this, the daughter of Bhīṣma, accompanied by her co-wives,
took the milk and approached him with the utmost reverence.
The daughter of Bhīṣmaka, with great affection, had Rādhā drink warm milk mixed with sugar, which had been placed in a golden vessel during the winter season.
Having thus worshipped according to the prescribed rites and offered a roll of betel leaves,
she remained constantly accompanied by her co-wives, such as Satyabhāmā and others.
Having approached the presence of Kṛṣṇa and speaking of her own virtuous deeds,
the auspicious Śrī Rukmiṇī directly took refuge at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Constantly caressing [Kṛṣṇa's] feet with her tender sprout-like hands,
she became filled with wonder upon seeing the calluses on the soles of Kṛṣṇa’s feet.
"O Lord, how did these eruptions appear on the soles of your feet?
They have appeared this very day, O Blessed One, for I do not know the cause of it. (33)
While sixteen thousand women were listening, Hari himself,
being pleased, spoke to Rukmiṇī for the purpose of revealing the devotion to Rādhā.
The Blessed Lord said: Indeed, my lotus-foot shines within the lotus-heart of Śrī Rādhikā.
Bound day and night by the noose of humility, he does not waver even for a moment or half a moment. || 35 ||
"Those splashes from the first warm milk-offering are overflowing upon my feet!
Indeed, you did not give him merely lukewarm [water], but gave him hot milk. (36)
Śrī Nārada said:
O King, having heard the words of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Rukmiṇī and the other excellent women then wiped His feet with love and were filled with wonder on all sides.
Śrī Rādhā’s supreme love for Mādhava, the slayer of Madhu, is equal to nothing else; it is unique and without peer upon this earth. (38)

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of Rādhā’s Love," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Dvārakā-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga Saṃhitā, concerning the meeting of Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa at Siddhāśrama. || 17 ||
Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Śrī Nārada said:
Having perceived the supreme love of Śrī Rādhā and the assembly of gopīs,
the princesses, eager to witness the rāsa dance, spoke to Hari.
Blessed indeed are those gopīs, your devotees endowed with the characteristic of divine love, who attained you on the stage of the rāsa dance; how can their austerity even be described?
O Mādhava, O Lord, if you so deem it fit, we wish to see that ritual by which the Rāsa dance was performed in Vṛndāvana.
And you, O Lord of Gods, as well as Rādhā, all the cowherd girls, and the women of Vraja—all of us are right here; thus, the Rāsa dance would be appropriate in this very place.
O Lord of our lives, fulfill this desire of ours;
no other desire has been made by us, O Hari, except for the Rāsa dance.
Having heard these words of theirs, the Blessed One, as if smiling and filled with affection,
spoke to them in words that seemed to enchant them.
The Blessed Lord said:
"O women, if the mind of Rādhā, the Queen of the Rāsa, desires to sport, then the Rāsa dance shall take place here; let it be asked by you."
Having heard his words, Rukmiṇī and the other daughters of kings approached Rādhā with supreme love and, with smiling faces, spoke to her.
The queens said: O lady with thighs like plantain stalks, moon-faced one, sovereign of the beauties of Vraja, mistress of the rāsa dance, dearest friend, whose character and form are sublime!
O Rādhā, you who bring fame to the lineage of Sukīrti and possess auspicious limbs, we have all come here to question you. || 9 ||
Indeed, Rāseśvara is the bestower of rasa here,
and you are Rāseśvarī, as are the excellent cowherd women;
thus we all exist for the sake of rasa in every way.
Perform the rāsa dance, O most beloved one, and likewise do what is dear to us.
Śrī Rādhā said:
O compassionate one toward the virtuous, if the mind of the Supreme Lord of the Rāsa-dance should desire to sport, then let the Rāsa take place here.
By means of supreme service and the highest devotion, worship him and indeed bring him under your control, O beloved ones. (11)
Śrī Nārada said:
Having heard the words of Rādhā, Śrī Kṛṣṇa spoke accordingly;
and having said, "So be it," that great-minded Rādhā became pleased.
On the auspicious full moon day of the month of Mādhava, at the beautiful Siddhāśrama,
the commencement of the Rāsa dance took place during the evening twilight, radiant as the moon.
Accompanied by the Queen of the Rāsa for the sake of the Rāsa dance,
the Lord of the Rāsa shone in the Rāsa as a connoisseur of aesthetic delight, like the Lord of Rati with Rati.
Assuming as many forms as there were all the cowherd women and as many as there were the princesses, the single Kṛṣṇa shone, appearing by the side of each and every pair.
A great, blended sound arose from the cymbals, flutes, and drums, mingled with the sweet voices of the female companions and the lovely tinkling of their anklets and waist-bands.
Possessing the beauty of ten million Cupids, wearing a garland and adorned with earrings,
O King, he was clad in yellow garments and decked with a crown, bracelets, and armlets.
O King, the Lord of the Rāsa himself sang together with the Mistress of the Rāsa in the midst of the Rāsa dance,
accompanied by throngs of women, just as the moon is surrounded by clusters of stars.
Thus, O King, the entire night passed like a single moment in the circle of the assembly;
it was auspicious and filled with great bliss, O Great Monarch.
Having beheld the glorious Rāsa-maṇḍala, the excellent women, headed by Rukmiṇī, all attained supreme bliss, their desires completely fulfilled. || 20 ||
At the conclusion of the rāsa dance, the queens, headed by Rukmiṇī and devoted to love, spoke directly to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, who is most perfectly complete.
The queens said:
Having beheld the sweetness of Your form on the enchanting stage of the rāsa dance,
our minds have gone to supreme bliss, just as a sage attains the bliss of Brahman.
Even such a rāsa dance as this has never occurred before, nor will it ever happen again;
for here, O Mādhava, there are hundreds of groups of gopīs. (23)
"We sixteen thousand wives, together with our female companions,
and here the eight great queens along with ten million friends—
even in Vṛndāvana, O Lord of Mādhava, there has never been anyone like this. (24)
Śrī Nārada said:
Thus, laughing at the queens who were full of such pride, Hari spoke these words to them as they questioned one another regarding Rādhā: "25"
Satyabhāmā and all the others questioned that enchanting woman;
smiling slightly within her mind, Rādhā spoke these supreme words.
Śrī Rādhā said: "Indeed, this rāsa here, crowded with a multitude of many women,
cannot be equal to the previous rāsa that took place in Vṛndāvana."
And where indeed is this Vṛndāvana forest, filled with divine trees and creepers, its ground bowed down by the weight of love, and its bees intoxicated by honey? (28)
Where indeed is the auspicious river Yamunā here, which carries arrays of flowers, is marked with the uṣṇih meter, and is strewn with swans and lotuses? 29.
Where are the other *mādhavī* creepers here, bowed down by the weight of their blossoms?
And where are the birds, devoted to love, singing with such sweet voices? (30)
Where are the bowers filled with swarms of restless bees, and where are the forest thickets that are like divine mansions?
And where is the cool, gentle breeze blowing, carrying away the pollen of the lotuses? (31)
The Govardhana mountain, with its lofty and enchanting peaks, rich everywhere with fruits and flowers, appears like an elephant with its caverns. (32)
On the delightful bank of the Kālindī, where the sands were stirred by the wind,
he stood holding his flute and staff, resplendent with his ornaments and garments.
And where here is Kṛṣṇa’s adornment, adorned with a forest garland, amidst the dark, stainless, curved faces that bear fragrance? (34)
What movement or mutual play could there be here between the two earrings upon the beautiful cheeks of the illustrious face of the moon-like Kṛṣṇa? (35)
Where is that sight, touch, and joy born of love, [now] joined by swarms of bees wandering about out of greed for the fragrance of the leaf-ornaments? (36)

Where is the passion born from the side-glances of eyes with sharp corners directed toward sensual pleasures, and where is the drawing in [of others] by both hands, followed by the releasing of them from hand to hand? (37)
Melting away in the groves, appearing face-to-face, the seizing of bark garments here, and the taking away of the flutes and canes. (38)
Where, moreover, is there the mutual pulling of each other’s arms out of love, and the repeated grasping of that arm smeared with sandalwood paste? (39)
In whatever place such pastimes occur, there alone does splendor reside;
where Vṛndāvana is not present, there my mind finds no happiness. (40)
Śrī Nārada said:
Then, having heard Rādhā’s words, all the great noblewomen abandoned their pride toward their own husband; they were both amazed and filled with joy. 41.
Thus, having performed the rāsa dance at Siddhāśrama, Hari, the Lord of Śrī Rādhikā,
led all the hosts of gopīs away together with Rādhā.
Accompanied by his wife, the Blessed Lord entered Dvārakā in person and caused magnificent palaces to be built for Rādhā.
Having provided all those inhabitants of Vraja with great happiness,
O King, I have thus related this account of Siddhāśrama to you.
It removes all sins, is meritorious, and bestows liberation upon everyone. || 45 ||

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Rāsa Festival," within the "Greatness of Siddhāśrama" in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva, in the Dvārakā-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā. || 18 ||
Hari Oṃ Tat Sat. May this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
The venerable Nārada said:
The region of Dvārāvatī, however, was one hundred yojanas in extent.
Its entire circumference is four hundred yojanas. ||1||
In its center was a fortress built by Kṛṣṇa, twelve yojanas in extent.
And there was a second outer fortification, ninety [yojanas] wide and difficult to cross.
O King, it was struck for a distance of one krośa by the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
And likewise, O King, the third fortress was two hundred *dvyai* (two-hundred) in measure.
O King, it was crowded for many leagues and endowed with palaces made of jewels.
Even within their innermost difficulties, [they remembered] the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Indeed, there are nine hundred thousand diverse temples. ||4||
There, at the door of Rādhā’s palace, is the Līlā-sarovara lake.
O King, this best of all holy places has come from Goloka. || 5 ||
Having bathed in which, even a sinful man, becoming observant of vows and composed in mind, [attains purity].
And on the eighth day, having given a gift of gold and having bowed according to the prescribed rite, ||6||
One is liberated from the sins committed throughout ten million births; of this there is no doubt.
At the end of his life, that great chariot shall lead that man from Goloka.
He who resembles a thousand suns is coming; of this there is no doubt.
Possessing the beauty of ten Kandarpas, he was adorned with jeweled earrings.
Wearing garlands and yellow garments, he is dark-complexioned, with a brilliance flashing like a thousand suns.
Accompanied by a thousand attendants, he was resplendent with the waving of yak-tail whisks. ||9||
Accompanied by the sound of victory, it resounded with the music of flutes and drums.
Having become thus and mounted his chariot, he goes to Goloka without a doubt.
Now, O King of great intelligence, hear of other sacred fords as well.
And there, exactly sixteen thousand one hundred [are situated]. || 11 ||
And there were likewise eight palaces for his wives.
Having circumambulated them and bowed down to each one individually.
Having bathed in the Jñānatīrtha, he who touches the Pārijātaka tree—
At that very moment, knowledge, dispassion, and devotion arise within him. || 13 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa shall always dwell in his heart with a joyful mind.
All prosperities and accomplishments naturally attend him. || 14 ||
He who beholds the temple of Hari shall be liberated and have fulfilled his purpose.
There is indeed no Vaiṣṇava equal to him, nor is there any sacred ford equal to it.
From that temple of the Blessed One, which was five yojanas in extent, [he departed].
At a distance of one hundred bows lies Kṛṣṇakuṇḍa, which originated from the splendor of Kṛṣṇa. ||16||
Having bathed there, Sāmba, the son of Jāmbavatī, was liberated from leprosy.
By the mere sight of him, one is liberated from all sins. ||17||
Therefore, O King of Mithilā, in the eastern direction at the eighteenth step, [he saw it].
The great Balabhadra lake is meritorious and the best of all sacred fords (tīrtha).
Having circumambulated the earth, the exceedingly powerful Baladeva—
Having performed a sacrifice there, he shone resplendently with the Revatī constellation;
having bathed there, a person is immediately liberated from all sins.
And the fruit of circumambulating the earth is not difficult for him to attain.
O King, [it is] a thousand bows' length in front of the temple of the Blessed One.
To the south lies the great sacred site of Gaṇanātha. ||21||
O King, when ten days had passed since the birth of his own son Pradyumna at that time, [he performed the naming ceremony].
Where Rukmiṇī performed the worship of Gaṇeśa. ||22||
O lord of kings, he who bathes there and bestows a gift of gold—
He shall obtain sons, and his lineage shall flourish.
O King, from the temple of the Blessed One, in the western quarter of the directions.
Two hundred bow-lengths further lies the most auspicious Dānatīrtha. ||24||
Wherever one constantly makes offerings to Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra.
Having bathed there, O King, a man likewise obtains two palas of gold.
Four times that amount of silver, as well as a hundred pieces of fine silk cloth.
Likewise, there were nine gems, each worth a thousand [gold pieces]. || 26 ||
Listen to the fruit of merit for that best of men who gives this gift.
Thousands of horse-sacrifices and hundreds of Rājasūya sacrifices.
They do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of the sacred ford of generosity.
Whatever fruit a man obtains on a pilgrimage to Badarikāśrama, [he attains that same fruit by bathing here]. || 28 ||
During the pilgrimage to the Saindhava forest, while the sun was situated in Aries (meṣa). || 29 ||
During the Utpalāvarta festival, when the sun is situated in Taurus.
Bathing and giving gifts here become a hundred thousandfold in merit; of this there is no doubt.
Therefore, O King of Videha, the merit at the Dānatīrtha is ten million times greater than that.
And whatever bathing and giving of gifts one performs at Dānatīrtha for one month; || 31 ||
And Citragupta does not know whatever merit has been produced by him.
Even the four-faced Brahmā is not capable of describing the greatness of that sacred ford.
And among all gifts, the gift of a horse is traditionally held to be supreme.
From the gift of a horse one gains the merit of a gift of an elephant, and from the gift of an elephant, that of a chariot. ||33||
O King, the gift of land is superior to the gift of a chariot.
The gift of food is proclaimed to be a great gift, even greater than the gift of land. || 34 ||
A gift equal to the gift of food has never existed, nor will it ever exist.
The satisfaction of the gods, sages, ancestors, and spirits arises through food. || 35 ||
For he who, being high-minded, gives food at the sacred ford of charity;
Then, liberated from the three debts, he goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
O Indra among kings, there are ten on the mother’s side and ten on the father’s side.
But on the tenth lunar day, a man should rescue ten persons belonging to his beloved.
Four-armed, of divine form, with serpents forming their crests.
Wearing garlands and yellow garments, they proceed to the abode of Hari.
O King, it has been heard that [it is] to the north of the temple of the Blessed One.
O tiger among kings, half a krośa away is the enchanting Māyātīrtha.
Where Durgā, the destroyer of misfortune, shines eternally.
Bhadrakālī, mounted upon a lion, is the destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.
He entered the cave of the king of bears in order to recover the Syamantaka jewel.
And Queen Devakī honored her son with excellent fruits. ||41||
Then the Blessed Lord Hari, together with his beloved wife and his jewel, departed.
From that cave, that well-known Māyātīrtha emerged, which bestows rewards.
And that person who, having bathed at Māyātīrtha and worshipped Māyā, shall obtain the fulfillment of all his heart's desires; of this there is no doubt. 43.

Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "The Greatness of Līlāsarovara, Harimandira, Jñānatīrtha, Kṛṣṇakuṇḍa, Balabhadrasaras, and Gaṇeśatīrtha," in the First Durga of the Śrīdvārakākhaṇḍa within the glorious Garga Saṃhitā, in the dialogue between Nārada and Bahulāśva. || 19 ||
The venerable Nārada said:
At the eastern gate of the second fortress as well was the King of Videha.
The Indratīrtha is greatly meritorious, granting desires and bestowing spiritual accomplishments.
O King, having bathed there, a man indeed proceeds to the world of Indra.
In this very world, a person attains a splendor equal to that of the moon. ||2||
Likewise, at the southern gate, the Sūryakuṇḍa is designated.
Wherein even Satrājit worshipped the Syamantaka jewel.
O lord of kings, having bathed there, whoever gives a ruby, [attains great merit].
Indeed, by means of the celestial chariot Sūryaprabha, he goes to the world of the Sun.
Likewise, at the western gate, the Brahma-tīrtha is preeminent.
Having bathed there, O King, a man [should offer] milk-rice in a golden vessel.
Listen to the fruit of merit for him who, possessing great wisdom, gives this gift.
A killer of a Brahmin, a killer of a father, a killer of a cow, and a killer of a mother or teacher are grievous sinners.
Having established his station in the world of Indra, he bore a body composed of Brahman.
And he goes to the abode of Brahmā by means of a celestial chariot with the splendor of the moon.
Likewise, at the northern gate, there should be a field that is dark blue and red.
Where Mahādeva, the blue-and-red one, shines in person. ||8||
All the deities, the sages, as well as the seven supreme ṛṣis.
O Vaideha, all the hosts of Maruts dwell there.
Having diligently worshipped the Liṅga of Nīlalohita there, however, [one attains the fruit].
Rāvaṇa, the one who makes the worlds cry out, obtained incomparable sovereignty.
O King, whatever fruit one obtains on a pilgrimage to Kailāsa, [that same fruit is obtained here].
Therefore, the merit from beholding Nīlalohita is a hundred times greater. ||11||
Indeed, the man who bathes for three days in the Nīlalohita pool, [attains his goal].
He goes to the world known as Śivaloka, even if he is burdened by tens of thousands of sins.
There shines the sacred ford named Saptasāmudraka.
Having bathed there, even a sinful man is liberated from the multitude of his sins.
And one shall quickly obtain the merit of bathing in all the oceans alike.
Viṣṇu, Viriñci, Giriśa, Indra, Vāyu, Yama, and Ravi; ||14||
Parjanya, Dhanada, Soma, Kṣiti, Agni, and the Lord of Waters.
For these always remain at his sides, O lord of men. (15)
Whatever seventy million sacred fords (tīrthas) exist within the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), [they are all here].
O King, all of them reside there in Saptasāmudraka.
Having bathed there, a person should thereafter perform the complete circumambulation.
And he obtains the full fruit of the pilgrimage to Dvārakā. || 17 ||
A journey with the nectar from the seven oceans is said to grant its fruit.
The gods know the Saptasāmudraka Tīrtha to be the form of Viṣṇu.

Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Greatness of Indratīrtha, Brahmatīrtha, Sūryakuṇḍa, Nailalohita, and the Seven Seas," within the second Durga of the Śrīdvārakākhaṇḍa in the glorious Gārgasaṃhitā, in the dialogue between Nārada and Bahulāśva. || 20 ||
The venerable Nārada said:
At the eastern gate of the third fortress also was Mahābala.
O King, Hanumān, the son of Añjanī, guards [him] day and night.
Having beheld that Hanumān, the devotee of the Blessed One and possessed of great strength, [he spoke].
A human being is born as a devotee of the Blessed One, just like Hanumān. ||2||
Likewise, O King, the Sudarśana discus named Cakra protects the southern gate day and night, its mind fixed on Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
By the mere sight of him, one becomes a supreme devotee of Hari.
Indeed, Sudarśana always provides protection even for his devotee. ||4||
Likewise, the powerful Jāmbavān, king of the bears, guarded the western gate.
O King, endowed with devotion to the Blessed One, he protects [it] day and night. ||5||
Having beheld that mighty Jambavān, a devotee of the Blessed One.
And here on earth, that human becomes a long-lived devotee of Hari.
Likewise, at the northern gate stood the mighty Viṣvaksena.
O King, the great one whose heart is fixed on Śrī Kṛṣṇa protects [them] day and night.
By the mere sight of it, a person attains the fulfillment of their purpose.
Listen, O King, to the sacred ford known as Piṇḍāraka, situated outside the fortress. ||8||
O best of kings, listen to the greatness of Piṇḍāraka.
By the mere remembrance of whom, one is liberated from great sin. ||9||
Like a gateway to the attainment of wealth for both Mount Raivata and the ocean.
In the center is the Piṇḍāraka field, the most excellent of all sacred fords (tīrthas).
The mighty King Yadu performed the Rājasūya, the sovereign of sacrifices.
O Vaideha, he performed [this] there by the command of the most perfect one.
Wherein all sacred fords from every direction have been summoned together.
O King, they took up residence with Ugrasena at that supreme sacrifice.
Therefore, it is called Piṇḍāraka, because it is the essence (piṇḍa) of all sacred fords (tīrtha).
Having bathed there, a person immediately obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice. ||13||
Having bathed for exactly three days in that very place, being observant of vows and composed in mind.
Having given a gift of gold to the Brahmins, he who becomes humble; || 14 ||
In this very life he shall become a lord of men, for he is a great-souled one; of this there is no doubt.
He himself constantly and perpetually hears his own fame proclaimed by bards.
With others who possessed faces like the beautiful moon and were adorned with gold, jewels, garments, and the like.
Constantly attended by throngs of women, he was joyful, well-nourished, and possessed of great strength.
Day and night, deep-sounding drums are beaten at the gate.
And it was accompanied by the trumpeting of elephants and the neighing of horses. ||17||
He shines forth, surveying the courtyard and the arena with throngs of kings.
It was a collection of jeweled palaces, adorned with circles of banners.
The circle of mountain peaks was struck by the two ears of the intoxicated elephant.
It adorns that gateway, decorated by the lords of the mandalas.
Without the ritual bath at Piṇḍāraka, how could sovereignty be attained here?
How indeed does a man, even though joined with sin, attain liberation? ||20||
Without bathing at Piṇḍāraka there is no peace; without bathing at Piṇḍāraka there is no success in one's rites.
Without the ritual bath at Piṇḍāraka there is no dharma; without the ritual bath at Piṇḍāraka there is no armor.
One who does not bathe at Piṇḍāraka is separated [from his beloved]; one who bathes at Piṇḍāraka is reunited with her.
One who bathes at Piṇḍāraka becomes a possessor of great enjoyments; one who bathes at Piṇḍāraka does not suffer from disease. ||22||
Having circumambulated Dvārāvatī in the middle of the month of Mādhava, one pays obeisance to it.
O Vaideha, all accomplishments, both in this world and the next, reside in the palm of that person's hand. || 23 ||
Having bathed at sacred fords, sleeping on the ground, pure, observing silence, and practicing vows while subsisting on air as food;
It is said that starting from the full moon day of Caitra, he who undertakes the pilgrimage reaching Mādhavī [is blessed]. ||24||
Even the four-faced Creator, composed of the Vedas, is unable to recount the measure of that merit.
One might at some time count the torrents of rain, but one can never count the merits of Kṛṣṇa’s city.
Just as the day of Hari is among the lunar days, and just as Śeṣa is the king of serpents among all snakes;
Just as Garuḍa is among birds in the sky, and as the Bhārata is among the Purāṇas, O Bhārata. ||26||
For just as among the gods there is the God of Gods, Śrī Vāsudeva, the God of Gods of the Yadus.
Likewise, among all the cities and sacred fields, the meritorious Dvārāvatī is most highly praised. || 27 ||
Oh, how blessed she is, for she shines upon the surface of the earth, enchanting with her circles of trees!
Kuśasthalī is presided over by the pastimes of Vaikuṇṭha, just as a row of clouds in the sky is graced by flashes of lightning. 28.
Wherein the Supreme Lord himself, having assumed the fourfold manifestation, shines forth in full splendor.
Salutations again and again to that Hari, who bestowed the status of lord of kings upon Ugrasena and [the sovereignty] upon Kṛṣṇa. ||29||
When the Blessed One shall depart for his own world, he will then submerge that [city] in the ocean.
Without the divine palace of Hari belonging to the King of Videha, the Blessed One will not make his residence there.
In that very place during the Kali age, they hear the sound of the ocean, spoken thus by Kṛṣṇa, day after day.
Whether he be ignorant or possessed of knowledge, that Brahmin is indeed my own body. || 31 ||
Then, having become a brahmin, he went from the shore of the unfathomable ocean and took hold of the image of the Supreme One.
Having performed the consecration and constructed a palace, this Arka shall carry out the installation ceremony.
Those devotees who, in the Kali age, behold the true form as the illustrious Lord of Dvārakā;
They go, O god among men, to the abode of Viṣṇu, which is difficult even for the lords of yogins to attain.
O god among men, I have thus related to you this very greatness of Kṛṣṇapura.
Whoever hears this or causes others to hear it with devotion shall obtain the fruit of residing in Śrī Dvārakā. ||34||
This most meritorious section concerning the kingdom of Śrī Dvārakā has been narrated by me before you.
The lineage of Kīrti bestows both liberation and sovereignty upon those who listen with great devotion at all times. ||35||

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Greatness of Piṇḍāraka," in the third Durga within the Śrīdvārakākhaṇḍa of the glorious Gargasamhitā, in the dialogue between Nārada and Bahulāśva. ||21||
Śrī Nārada said:
There was a certain Brāhmaṇa named Sudāmā who was a friend of Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
he lived in his own city accompanied by his wife Satyā.
Detached from the world, devoid of wealth, and a master of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences,
he maintained his livelihood by begging from a wife of similar character.
Once, as she was suffering due to poverty, he said to his beloved:
"O devoted wife, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the lord of Dvārakā, is my friend."
That lore was studied by me and by him as well in the house of Sāndīpani;
yet Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas, has not been seen again.
"The Blessed Lord, the protector of the three worlds, the destroyer of suffering, who is compassionate toward the distressed"—having heard these words of his, the devoted wife's mouth went dry. (5)
Wearing tattered clothes, distressed and hungry, she said to her husband:
"O Brahmin, if indeed Hari, the Lord of Kamalā, is your friend... (6)
"How is it that you, though hungry, wear only worn-out rags?
People go to Dvārakā and, having seen the Lord of Śrī in person, return endowed with wealth; therefore, you ought to go there. (7)
Sudāmā said:
"I am the teacher of all; you shall provide the instruction to him.
O beloved, for a learned brāhmaṇa, alms are declared to be wealth."
Priyā said:
Go to that friend of yours, the Lord of Śrī, who dwells not far away; he will destroy your suffering and poverty.
Such has become my condition as I endure this suffering and poverty;
O beloved, what fruit is there for the state of friendship with that treasure-house of compassion who gave [to us]? 10.
Sudāmā said: "Destiny written by the Creator shall come to pass exactly so.
What is the use of coming and going, O blessed lady? I am practicing meditation on Hari."
At whose gate kings, gods, gandharvas, and kinnaras do not pass without permission—what can be said of me, a wretched man? (12)
Priyā said: "The gods, gandharvas, and kinnaras will certainly not go without my command;
Hari, as the inner witness, will quickly summon you through messengers. (13)
The brāhmaṇa said: O beautiful lady, Kṛṣṇa is indeed so compassionate; however, listen:
in a time of calamity, one should not go to the excellent home of a friend. (14)
But how can I make a request after seeing my own beloved after so long?
For while joy might arise from his freedom from greed, it will surely depart because of the act of begging. (15)
Priyā said:
"Behold Śrī Hari, who removes suffering and poverty;
you must not make any request at all, for He will grant you abundant wealth."
Thus was the brahmin addressed in many ways by his beloved wife.
"Indeed, this is the supreme gain: having met my friend. But what gift shall I give? I am ashamed because of my poverty. (17)
Having spoken thus, that virtuous woman quickly went to another's house;
then, having requested four handfuls of rice, she returned to her own home. (18)
And having tied them in a piece of worn-out rag, she gave them to the Lord.
Then, taking the flattened rice and grains, wearing tattered rags, soiled and weak,
he went slowly toward the city of Kṛṣṇa while remembering in his mind the God who is the benefactor of the brāhmaṇas.
Having crossed the ocean by means of a small boat, he beheld there the glorious Dvārakā, the city of Hari, variegated with gold,
adorned with rows of assembly halls, various types of fortresses and mansions, and banners.
It was protected by exceedingly powerful Śṛṅgāṭakas and by the Yadus.
Having seen the city of Kṛṣṇa, the brāhmaṇa asked the people about Śrī Hari:
"Where indeed is the temple of Śrī? Tell me all of you now. (22)
Having heard this, the guardians of Mādhava’s palace said, "Kṛṣṇa is present in all the mansions. (23)
Having heard this and entered his dwelling, the twice-born man beheld Kṛṣṇa seated upon a couch and attained the bliss of Brahman.
Knowing that his friend had arrived, Mādhava rose up suddenly;
joining their arms together, they were overwhelmed with tears of love.
Having washed his feet with a golden vessel and having taken that water upon his head, he then seated him upon a couch.
He performed worship with perfumes, sandalwood, agallochum, and saffron,
as well as with cooked foods, incense, lamps, and honey-mixtures according to the prescribed ritual.
Afterwards, having offered betel and a cow, he spoke words of welcome to the old man,
who was dressed in tattered rags, soiled, weak, and white-haired.
Filled with smiles, Mitravindā fanned him with a whisk;
all the beloveds of Śrī Kṛṣṇa were astonished and then laughed. 29.
Seeing the brahmin thus honored by the mendicant Avadhūta, the women said to one another: "What ascetic merit has been performed by this man?"

In the meantime, while they were holding each other's hands, those two recounted stories born of their former lives in the preceptor’s family— stories of how they had been honored by the Lord of the Three Worlds like an eldest brother.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Brāhmaṇa; all branches of knowledge have been recited by you and me.
Yet, after giving the teacher his fee, you are no longer seen.
"But I, O friend, have gone to Dvārakā out of fear of Jarāsaṃdha;
tell me truly, O Lord, in what place do you dwell? (33)
Once, urged by our teacher’s wife for the sake of firewood, we all, being students of knowledge, went to that terrifying forest. (34)
There occurred a calamity there, a terrifying storm of wind and rain; the sun had set, and a great darkness arose during the night. || 35 ||
Everything has become composed of water, and no dry land is seen at all;
we have all taken one another’s lotus-hands.
Beholding everything in all directions by the light of lightning, they wandered about;
then, when sunrise had occurred, the great preceptor Sāndīpani [appeared].
Having gone to the forest, the Guru saw his disciples suffering from the cold in the water;
bringing them all out of the water onto dry land, he was overwhelmed with tears. (38)
He said: "O children, you are devoted to my command;
yet you disregard the Self, who is the dearest of all living beings, and instead take me as your supreme goal. (39)
Therefore, being well-pleased with you, I shall grant you a boon that is difficult to obtain;
may all your desires also be fulfilled in every respect. (40)
Indeed, let the Vedas, Shastras, and Puranas be committed to memory;
through the grace of my guru, may I therefore be filled with all forms of happiness. (41)
Sudāma said:
"O God of gods, you are indeed my preceptor and the leader of ten million universes;
yet for you to dwell among the preceptors of that Lord of Śrī is a supreme mockery."
Then, O King, the brahmin Sudāmā, with his face cast down, offered puffed rice grains to Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul.
The Lord, the soul of all, having understood the reason for his arrival, thought: "This brahmin does not desire wealth; he serves me for the sake of liberation. (44)
His wife, devoted to her husband, was making him despair by hoping for wealth;
therefore, how could I give wealth to those two who were not its givers? (45)
Thinking thus, and realizing again that he would take my rice and depart without giving anything out of shame, he spoke as follows. (46)
Therefore, having understood this, he spoke these words as he made his request. || 47 ||
Kṛṣṇa said:
"What gift have you brought from your home for my sake?
Even if it is offered as something minute, if it is presented with devotion, it shall become abundant. (48)
Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water— that offering made with devotion by one of purified soul, I accept.
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One took grains of rice from a piece of bark-cloth belonging to the Brahmin who would not give them; why did he take this himself? (50)
"O friend, this which you have brought to me is a source of supreme delight;
moreover, O Brahmin, these grains of rice shall satisfy the entire universe."
Such excellent puffed rice grains were enjoyed in Gokula, given by his mother Yaśodā;
yet he never saw them again.
Having swallowed one handful, he bestowed the wealth of the earth;
then he began to swallow a second, intending to bestow the wealth of the netherworld.
At that moment, Śrī quickly took Hari’s hand from his chest and said, "O Lord, why do you wish to abandon me without any offense? (54)
By this much alone, O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, a twice-born man may become equal to Indra;
yet even a poor brahmin does not know that secret. (55)
And having obtained all his wealth through the illusory power of Viṣṇu within his own home,
he stayed for one night, and after eating and drinking, he went away happily.
When morning dawned, having bowed to Kṛṣṇa, he set his mind on returning to his own home;
and he was commanded by the Blessed One, saluted, and embraced.
He did not make a request and, feeling ashamed, went to his own home;
thus was the devotion to Brahmins seen by me in the Lord of Śrī, the god of the brāhmaṇas.
"I am a pauper, yet I have been embraced by the arms of Kṛṣṇa; O twice-born one, I have been placed upon a couch enjoyed by my beloved like a brother. (59)
Even though he was fanned with a fan by Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā,
having been penniless, he would not remember the Lord of Śrī even after obtaining wealth.
"Thus Kṛṣṇa has not given me wealth out of compassion"—
reflecting thus as he walked along, he remembered the brāhmaṇī with indignation.
"Take ten million pieces of gold; having gone home, I shall say:
'I have heard that this Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the god who is kind to Brahmins and a generous giver. (62)
"Though I have seen with my own eyes that he is wretched and filled with pride despite being overflowing with wealth, how could I vainly cast a curse upon my friend out of greed for money? (63)
He will bring about for them the same kind of joy as that which was produced in me;
for in the past, his parents were cast into prison by Kaṃsa.
But Kṛṣṇa was reared in the house of Nanda, which is another's home;
how can he give away wealth, being as poor as he is even though possessed of riches? (65)
Seeing houses filled with jewels, one should not harbor desire;
for whatever is written upon the forehead, that shall not be diminished.
Thus conversing, the brahmin went to the vicinity of his own city,
which was joined with Suvarṇadurga and adorned with gates and banners.
It was filled with archways, colorful jars, and palaces, and surrounded by virtuous people;
it was rich in splendor like Dvārakā, and completely filled with all kinds of jewels.
Seeing him wandering from street to street while asking, "What is this? Whose place is this?", the women and men took him in.
Seeing that the twice-born man was not coming, the female and male servants told the mistress; upon hearing this, she was filled with wonder.
Hearing that her husband had arrived, the wife, filled with agitation, quickly emerged from her dwelling like the goddess Śrī herself in embodied form. (71)
The Brahmin woman, mounted upon a palanquin and surrounded by a multitude of male and female servants,
showed her own face and seized the wandering Brahmin.
Seeing his young wife shimmering, adorned with golden garments and rich with jewel ornaments,
like the beautiful Indirā in her celestial chariot;
Filled with joy, he considered it to be the grace of Kṛṣṇa. || 73 ||
Accompanied by her, he went to his own home, which resembled the palace of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
furnished with foods, precious objects, couches, fans, and seats.
Having seen it adorned with canopies, golden vessels, and archways, Sudāmā became young again through the grace of Kṛṣṇa. (75)
The greedy brahmin enjoyed his own unmerited prosperity, while in his mind he was renouncing it through knowledge, dispassion, and devotion, along with his wife. (76)
The Brahmin reflected: "From where have these prosperities of mine come, which are difficult even for the gods to obtain, granted by the God who is the friend of the Brahmins? (77)
Having bestowed such wealth, Hari himself did not say anything at all;
rather, he joyfully accepted even my handful of rice. (78)
May I have friendship and servitude with him in birth after birth;
by meditating upon his lotus feet, may I cross over the ocean of worldly existence. (79)
Having reflected thus in his mind, Sudāmā,
surrounded by his wife, fixed his heart upon the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and [offered] wealth to the brāhmaṇas.
Having given [it], he went to the supreme abode of Hari.
The person who hears this life-story of the divine Śrī Kṛṣṇa is quickly liberated from poverty and becomes a devotee of the Blessed Lord. (81)
O King, this most meritorious section concerning Śrī Dvārakā has been narrated by me before you;
it bestows fame, noble lineage, supreme devotion, liberation, and even sovereignty upon those who constantly listen to it. (82)

Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Narrative of the Brahmin Sudāman," in the Dvārakā-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā, within the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva.
Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
The Blessed One said: "Obeisance to you, the Blessed One, Vāsudeva, the witness."
Salutation to Pradyumna, to Aniruddha, and to Saṃkarṣaṇa. ||1||
For one blinded by the darkness of ignorance, with the collyrium-stick of knowledge...
Salutation to that glorious Guru by whom the eye was opened. ||2||
The illustrious Garga said:
O sage, thus have I narrated to you the life of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
This bestows the four goals of human life upon men; what more do you wish to hear? ||3||
Śaunaka said:
Bahulāśva, the lord of Mithilā, was beloved by Śrī Kṛṣṇa and dear to Hari.
O ascetic, tell me now what he asked of the divine sage.
Śrī Garga said:
O sage, [I shall tell you] what was done for Ugrasena, the lord of the Yādavas, by Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Having heard this, the King of Mithilā was greatly amazed and said to Nārada: ||5||
Bahulāśva said:
"Who indeed is this King Marutta, and by what merit has he come to the surface of the earth?"
The highly intelligent Ugrasena became the lord of the Yādavas.
For whom even Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra himself, Hari, became a helper.
O best of divine sages, tell me of his greatness.
Śrī Nārada said:
In the Kṛta Yuga, there was a universal monarch (cakravartin) born of the Solar dynasty.
He, who had conquered the world, performed a sacrifice according to the prescribed rites for the Maruts. ||8||
On the northern side of the Snowy Mountain, by those who have gathered the great accumulations of merit and wisdom.
Having indeed taken Saṃvarta, that tiger among sages, as his preceptor, he was initiated. ||9||
In his sacrifice, there was a sacrificial pit five yojanas in width.
A yojana is a Brahmakuṇḍa, while five kuṇḍas make a gavyūti. ||10||
Ten were constructed with girdles, moats, widths, and altars.
The great sacrificial pillar, a thousand cubits high, shone forth. ||11||
The sacrificial pavilion was made of gold and twenty yojanas in extent.
Adorned with canopies and arches, it shone, beautified by groves of plantain trees.
The gods, beginning with Brahmā and Rudra, arrived there together with their retinues.
All the ṛṣis and sages came together to his sacrifice. ||13||
There were ten million Hotṛ priests, and ten million who had been consecrated.
The Adhvaryus [recited] five hundred thousand [verses], and likewise the Udgātṛs and others.
Learned brahmins, knowers of the four Vedas, were summoned there.
Others, numbering in the tens of millions, who knew the true meaning of all the scriptures, were also fully honored. ||15||
Having consumed a stream of clarified butter equal to the trunk of an elephant, the consumer of oblations (the fire) [is satisfied].
Know this, O King of Mithilā, that it was no wonder that indigestion occurred during that sacrifice. ||16||
To those [ancestors] here, the Viśvedevas and the members of the assembly declare their share.
Or rather, those very servers gave them to each of those [guests].
Indeed, there were no living beings at all in the three worlds who remained hungry.
Indeed, all the gods fell into a state of indigestion due to the soma. ||18||
At the sacrifice, he gave the kingdom of Jambūdvīpa to Saṃvarta.
And fourteen million elephants laden with burdens of gold. ||19||
O King, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, he gave a hundred arbudas of horses as the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
To that Great-Souled One, [he offered] ten million highly precious nine-jeweled [ornaments].
Five thousand horses and one hundred elephants.
He gave a hundred bhāras of gold to each and every brahmin.
And golden vessels for water and food shine forth.
Having eaten those and quickly discarded them, the twice-born departed satisfied. ||22||
O King, with golden vessels that had been cast aside, defiled by food remnants, and abandoned.
On the slope of the Himālaya mountain, there was a mountain that even today remains a hundred yojanas in extent. ||23||
The sacrifice of Maruta is such as that of no other ever is.
Listen, O Indra among kings: in the three worlds, there has never been such a one, nor will there ever be. ||24||
Having emerged from the sacrificial fire-pit, he himself became the most perfect one.
He revealed himself to the high-souled Marutta.
Having beheld him and bowed to Hari, the king joined his palms in reverence.
Overwhelmed by love and with his hair standing on end, he was unable to speak. ||26||
Seeing him filled with love, fallen at his feet, and bowing down;
The Blessed One spoke directly with a voice as deep as a thundercloud.
The Blessed One said: "O King, I have been gratified by your humility; you have worshipped me without motive, being devoted to sacrifice."
"O Great-minded One, choose a supreme boon; I shall grant it swiftly, even one difficult for the gods to obtain in heaven. (28)
Śrī Nārada said:
Having heard this, King Marutta, with palms joined in reverence, circumambulated Hari, the Supreme Lord.
Having worshipped with devotion through pure offerings and having bowed down deeply, he spoke with a voice faltering with emotion. ||29||
Maruta said:
"O Śrī Puruṣottama, Supreme among the supreme, I do not know any boon greater than Your lotus feet."
Just as thirsty and very foolish men, having come together, dig a well [instead of going to the Ganges], so do those of evil intellect. ||30||
Nevertheless, out of respect for your words, I beg that your lotus-feet be placed within the lotus of my heart.
O Lord of Vraja, may my root never depart from You, the source of the fourfold wealth of human goals. 31.
The Blessed One said: "O King, blessed is your stainless intellect; even though you were enticed by boons, you have not been filled with desire."
Nevertheless, choose from me whatever boon you desire; for without the fruit of devotion, I have no happiness. (32)
Maruta said: "O Lord, since my desired boon is to be granted,
please establish Vaikuṇṭhaloka upon the surface of the earth."
O you who are affectionate toward your own devotees, protect me as I stay in that city together with other devoted people. 33.
The Blessed One said: "In this Manu-period, when twenty yugas have passed, the ocean of the gods' desires has reached eight [yojanas]."
Having gone to heaven and then returned to the earth,
you shall indeed leave a footprint of a cow-calf by me.
Śrī Nārada said:
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One vanished right there before their very eyes.
This very person indeed became King Ugrasena, the lord of the Maruts.
Hari himself caused that Rājasūya sacrifice to be performed.
O Lord of Maithila, what indeed is difficult to obtain for devotees within the three worlds?
