With her face filled with tears and feeling dejected, she bowed to Hari and spoke.
Madālasā said:
"O Lord, O Primordial God, you have been born on earth in the lineage of the Yadus for the purpose of removing the world's burden."
Having cast aside those things you would otherwise consume, you remain unstained by qualities; I bow to you.
Protect my son who is terrified; O Lord, place your hand upon his head.
"O Lord of Gods, O Abode of the Universe, please forgive this offense committed against you by my husband."
The venerable Nārada said:
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One placed both his hands upon his head.
The great sage bestowed the entire kingdom of Candrāvatī upon him.
Having granted a lifespan lasting until the end of the kalpa, along with devotion, knowledge, and detachment.
Kṛṣṇa gave his own auspicious garland to the young bird. ||9||
The horse Uccaiḥśravas, the jewel-cow Kāmadhenu, and the celestial tree.
Those who were formerly carried off by Śakuni from Purandara in battle.
Śrī Janārdana bestowed them with great effort upon Purandara.
He himself is the protector of cows, Brahmins, gods, the virtuous, and the Vedas. ||11||
Bahulāśva said: Who were these Daityas of great strength, such as Śakuni and the others, in former times?
O divine sage, this is a great wonder to me: why have they attained liberation? ||12||
Śrī Nārada said:
O King, in ancient times, during the Brahma-kalpa, there was a lord of the Gandharvas named Purūravas.
He had auspicious sons who were born of his own loins. ||13||
Possessing beauty equal to that of Kandarpa and adorned with divine ornaments.
Those skilled in song and instrumental music sang constantly in the world of Brahmā.
Mandāra, Mandara, Manda, Mandahāsa, and Mahābala.
Sudeva, Sudhana, Saudha, and Śrībhānu—these are their renowned names. ||15||
Once, out of delusion, the Creator beheld his daughter, the goddess of speech.

Due to the offense against Surajyeṣṭhā, she entered a dark womb.
Then, in the Vārāha [kalpa], those nine were born to the wife of Hiraṇyākṣa.
Śakuni, Śambara, Hṛṣṭa, Bhūtasaṃtāpana, and Vṛka.
Kālanābha, Mahānābha, Hariśmaśru, and likewise Utkaca. ||18||
Once, the sage Apāntaratamas was returning home.

The Daityas said:
"O Brahman, listen from your own mouth: Hari himself is the Lord of Kaivalya."

Apāntaratamas said: "Those who worship the Supreme Hari through the non-differentiation of the qualities (guṇas)..."
Those various Daityas attained the supreme, attribute-less leader of liberation.
Oneness, friendship, affection, fear, anger, and likewise pride.

Just as the Lords of Creatures [attained their status] through their connection with Pṛśnigarbha.
The sage Sutapas was devoted to his body out of friendship and affection. ||25||
Out of fear was Hiraṇyakaśipu, and out of anger was his father, the Asura Vṛtra.
And through that smile, the Śrutis attained the supreme state, which is difficult even for yogins to reach.
By whatever means possible, one should fix the mind upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
O gods, that abode which is attained by these [means] is reached through the yoga of devotion.
Śrī Nārada said:
O King, when the sage Apāntaratamas had spoken thus and vanished, [the king...]
Śakuni and others harbored enmity toward Hari, who was most perfect.
They reached Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, with a spirit of enmity.
Know it not to be strange, O Indra among kings, just as a worm [is transformed] by a silk-worm maker. ||29||

Thus ends the forty-second chapter, titled "The Account of the Previous Births of the Daityas Śakuni and Others," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Śrī Viśvajit-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā. ||42||
Śrī Nārada said:
Having thus conquered the region of Bhadrāśva, the illustrious Lord of the Yādavas—
Then he went to Ilāvṛta together with those two armies. ||1||
Therein shines the king of mountains like the pericarp of the lotus-globe of the earth.
O King of Mithilā, Sumeru, the abode of the gods, is made of gold with shimmering luster and peaks of jewels.
On all sides were Mandara, Merusundara, Supārśva, and Kumuda as the fourth.
That one Lord of Mountains shines alone among the mountains, like a single object of desire among all things that exist. ||3||
Indeed, *jāmbūnada* is that which originates from the *jambu* tree; for wherever it comes from, gold is produced by its own inherent perfection.
Where the river named Aruṇodā was born, by drinking whose water one is freed from disease on earth.
And there are five streams of honey born from the Kadamba tree, by drinking which men never again [suffer].
O King, states such as cold, heat, discoloration, exhaustion, and the like, as well as foul odors, do not occur.
From which arise wish-fulfilling cows, rivers, jewels, new garments, and beautiful ornaments.
Furthermore, they offer celestial fruits such as beds, seats, and other such things.
And thus, where the forest of Urdhva is renowned,
and where Saṃkarṣaṇa shines resplendent;
That Śiva always delights with his beloveds,
and there the people attain the state of being women.
With golden lotuses, cool spring breezes, saffron trees, and groves of clove plants;
The region of Ilāvṛta shone exceedingly, its sky filled with bees blinded by the intoxication of the fragrance of celestial trees. ||8||
He beheld the earth, enchanting and made of gold, variegated with clusters of sprouts of lapis lazuli gems.
Having conquered Ilāvṛta, which was filled with adorned gods, Hari seized it as his portion and took Bali captive. ||9||
In former times, one named Śrīśobhana became the son-in-law of King Mucukunda due to his past deeds.
He who has fasted on the Ekādaśī day in Bhārata has indeed reached Mount Mandara along with the gods. (10)
Even today, it is said, that son of the king rules his kingdom like Kubera by means of the Candrabhāgā river.
O King of Mithilā, having taken the offering before the best of gods, that supreme and beautiful youth returned. 11.
Having circumambulated Hari, the best of the Yadus,
Śobhana then fell at his lotus feet.
Having bowed down with devotion and quickly offered an oblation to the Great-Souled One, he departed for Mount Mandara, O King of Mithilā. ||12||
Bahulāśva said:
When the auspicious king had departed, the blessed Madhusūdana [remained].
O best of divine sages, tell me, what did the Lord do first? (13)
Śrī Nārada said:
On that ridge of Mount Mandara, there is a supreme and divine lake.
Beholding the golden lotus, the wearer of the crown (Arjuna) spoke to Mādhava.
Arjuna said:
It was surrounded by golden creepers and golden lotuses.
Speak to me, O son of Devakī: whose is this wonderful pool?
The Blessed Lord said:
"Pṛthu was the first king of kings, born of the lineage of Svāyambhuva."
He performed divine penance; this is his wonderful pool.
By drinking its water immediately, one is liberated from all sins.
Having bathed there, O Pārtha, even one who is not a human being goes to that supreme abode.
Śrī Nārada said: Right here, the Blessed One himself went to that land of asceticism.
There, all those eight Siddhis dance in their own forms. ||18||
Having beheld them, Uddhava spoke to the eternal Blessed One.
Uddhava said:
Whose ground of great austerity is this in the vicinity of Mount Mandara?
"O Lord, tell me, who are these women who shine forth in embodied form? (19)
The Blessed One said:
"In ancient times, penance was performed here by Svāyambhuva Manu."
This ground of his, where he performed great austerities, remains even today exceedingly auspicious.
For indeed, the eight siddhis always abide right here in the form of women.
In this case, for whomever [the fruit] has been attained, those [impurities] indeed cease to exist. ||21||
In this place, by means of a moment's austerity, a human being attains divinity.
Even the four-faced Brahmā is not capable of describing the greatness of this land of austerity.
Śrī Nārada said:
Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa, surrounded by his own army, [departed].
He went to the most formidable regions, repeatedly sounding his kettledrums.
It is there that the Daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu performed penance in ancient times.
Therein lies the golden city named Līlāvatī.
Līlāvatīśvara is the manifest Agni, the consumer of oblations.
Possessing a physical form on earth, he of noble vows constantly exercises sovereignty.
He too [offered it] to the great-souled Supreme Person, Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra.
Having offered the oblation, Dhanañjaya performed supreme and constant praise. ||26||
Beholding everything in this manner, the God of gods [ruled over] Ilāvṛta for a full year.
He went to the delightful city of Vedanagara in Jambudvīpa. ||27||
For indeed, the Veda itself is always seen there in embodied form.
In her assembly, the Goddess of Speech (Sarasvatī) was always present, holding a lute and a book.
Singing the auspicious deeds of Kṛṣṇa, which are the source of all blessings.
O King, the Apsarases, headed by Urvaśī and Pūrvacitti, perform a dance.
And they were pleasing the Lord of the Vedas with their gestures, expressions, and side-long glances.
I, Viśvāvasu, Tuṃburu, and Sudarśana. ||30||
Likewise, Citraratha indeed played these musical instruments again and again.
Flutes, lutes, drums, and instruments joined with reed-pipes; ||31||
They play them together with cymbals and drums according to the prescribed ritual.
O King, [these are] the short, long, protracted, acute, grave, and circumflex accents.
And likewise, there is the distinction between nasalized and non-nasalized [articulation].
By these eighteen divisions, the Śrutis are sung by others. ||33||
O King, they shine there in embodied form within the city of the Vedas.
There are eight *tālas*, seven notes (*svaras*), and likewise three scales (*grāmas*), O King. (34)
For they always dwell in the city of the senses in embodied form.
Bhairava, Meghamallāra, Dīpaka, and Mālakaṃsaka. ||35||
Śrīrāga and Hiṇḍola—these six rāgas are thus proclaimed.
And with five beloved ones, and with eight sons, each separately. ||36||
But they move about there in embodied form, O lord of men.
Bhairava is tawny in color, while Mālakaṃsa has the luster of a parrot. ||37||
Indeed, the Meghamallāra is endowed with the splendor of a peacock.
Dīpaka is golden-hued, and Śrīrāga bears a reddish color.
O Lord of Mithilā, the swing, resembling a divine swan, shines resplendently. 38.
Bahulāśva said:
"O best of sages, regarding the notes, the scales, and the musical modes of the tālas..."
Tell me how many varieties of dances there are, together with their names.
Śrī Nārada said:
Rūpaka, Cañcarīka, Tāla, and Paramaṭha are remembered [as the four types].
Virāṭakamaṭha, Mallaka, and Jhaṭijjuṭā; ||40||
Niṣāda, Ṛṣabha, Gāndhāra, Ṣaḍja, Madhyama, and Dhaivata.
And the fifth; these, O King, are proclaimed as the seven notes (svaras). ||41||
Sweetness, the Gāndhāra note, and stability are remembered as the three qualities of the triple scale (grāma).
And likewise, the Rāsa dance, the Tāṇḍava, dramatic performance, and the music of the Gandharvas and Kinnaras. ||42||
O King, [he taught] the Vaidyādhara, the Gāuhya, and the Nṛtyamākrūra dance.
And by means of the ten *hāva*, *bhāva*, and *anubhāva* [gestures], which possess eight varieties. ||43||
A word is traditionally defined as that which is accessible through the musical notes: sa, re, ga, ma, pa, dha, and ni.
This has been told to you, O King; what more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the forty-third chapter, titled "The Description of Vedanagara," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Śrī Viśvajit-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā. ||43||
Bahulāśva said:
O divine sage, tell me the names of those who are passionate.
Thus, indeed, you are the most knowledgeable regarding the higher and lower states among the sons of Rāga. ||1||
Śrī Nārada said: Through time, through differences of place, through ritual action, and through the blending of musical notes.
The wise have proclaimed fifty-six crores of varieties of song. ||2||
O Lord of Kings, they possess infinite internal divisions.
Know this Hari to be passion, bliss, and composed of the Brahman of sound. ||3||
Therefore, I shall declare before you the primary divisions.
Bhairavī, Piṅgalā, Śaṅkī, Līlāvatī, and likewise Agarī. ||4||
For Bhairava-rāga as well, five rāgiṇīs are proclaimed.
Maharṣi, Samṛddha, Piṅgala, and likewise Māgadha. ||5||
Bilāvala, Vaiśākha, and Lalita as the fifth; thus [are they].
The eight sons of Bhairava who are celebrated individually.
Citrā is said to be Jayā, Jayāvantī, and furthermore Vicitrā.
The descendants of Vṛjja, Lārṣya, and Andhaka are captivating, even though they are full of passion.
O Maithila, five [varieties] of the Meghamallāra rāga have been described.
Śyāmakāra, Soraṭha, Naṭa, and also Ḍāyana. ||8||
Kedāra, Vrajaraṃhasya, and likewise Jaladhāra;
And Vihāga—these eight sons were described by the ancient sages. ||9||
Kaṃcukī, Mañjarī, Ṭoḍī, Gurjarī, and likewise Śābarī. ||10||
For the lamp-like passion as well, there are five renowned impassioned ones.
Kalyāṇa, Śubhakāma, and Gauḍakalyāṇa as well. ||11||
Kāmarūpa, Kānhara, and likewise Rāmasaṃjīvana.
The King of Videha had eight sons, including one named Sukha and another named Mandahāsa.
This has been declared by those learned in passion (rāga) regarding even the illuminating [flame] of passion.
Gāndhārī, Vedagāndhārī, Dhanāśrī, and Svarmaṇi likewise. ||13||
O Lord of Mithilā, these five are passionate, yet they are exalted by their virtues.
The passion of Mālakośa is said to be within the circle of passion. ||14||
Megha, Camacala, Mārumācāra, and likewise Kauśika.
Candrahāra, Ghuṅghuṭa, Vihāra, and Nanda. ||15||
The eight sons of Mālakośa and Rāga are proclaimed.
Vairāṭī, Karṇāṭī, Gaurī, and likewise Gaurāvaṭī. ||16||
And Catuścandrakalā, as well as the five renowned Rāgiṇīs.
O King of kings, [the ragas] of Śrīrāga have also been described by the ancient masters. ||17||
Sāraṅga, Sāgara, Gaura, Marut, and Pañcaśara.
Govinda, Hamīra, and likewise Gīrbhīra. ||18||
O King of kings, Śrīrāga also had eight charming sons.
Vasanti, Airajā, Herī, Tailaṅgī, and Sundarī likewise. ||19||
For the rāga Hiṃḍola as well, five well-known rāgiṇīs are recognized.
And Maṅgala, Vasanta, Vinoda, and likewise Kumuda. ||20||
And thus is described the manifestation of the circle of vowels.
And eight sons are proclaimed, O Lord of Mithilā, by those who are wise. ||21||
Bahulāśva said:
"The Śabdabrahman is the direct manifestation of Hari, the Great-Souled One of the Nigama."
Thus, for each swing individually, there is a circle of passion (rāgamaṇḍala). ||22||
O God, tell me which limbs are there upon the surface of the earth?
Śrī Nārada said:
Grammar is declared to be the mouth, and Piṅgala is called the feet. ||23||
The Mīmāṃsā-śāstra is proclaimed as his two hands, and the Jyotiḥ-śāstra as his eyes.
Āyurveda is his back, and Dhanurveda is his chest. ||24||
Know that the Gandharva is the sense of taste, and the Vaiśeṣika is traditionally remembered as the mind (manas). ||25||
Sāṃkhya is proclaimed as intellect (buddhi) and ego-sense (ahaṃkāra), while Nyāya is proclaimed as discourse (vāda).
For his mind is indeed the Vedānta, and he is the great-souled one of the Veda itself. ||26||
O King of Mithilā, know this monastery to be the very form of passion.
This has been told to you, O King; what more do you wish to hear? ||27||
Bahulāśva said: What did Hari himself do in that beautiful city of Veda?
Tell me this, O divine sage; you possess direct divine vision.
Śrī Nārada said:
[I saw] Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the Yādavas, approaching the city of Vedanagara.
The merchant guild, too, having brought an offering, [went] along with that Sarasvatī. ||29||
Together with gandharvas and apsarases, along with musical scales, rhythms, and notes.
Accompanied by his various retinues, he prostrated with palms joined in reverence. ||30||
The Blessed One, Janārdana, the God of gods himself, was visibly pleased.
He spoke this Veda while all the virtuous Yadus were listening.
The Blessed One said: "O Nigama, choose a boon; tell me whatever dwells in your mind."
When I am delighted, what is difficult to obtain for my devotees within the three worlds?
Veda said:
"O Lord, if you are pleased, then all those who are my excellent attendants—"
O Lord, O Supreme Ruler, reveal Your own true form to them here.
Whatever form You have in Your own abode, Goloka, which is radiant with shimmering splendor;
And in Vṛndāvana, at that rāsa dance, he was longing for a vision of Him. ||34||
Śrī Nārada said:
Having heard the words of the Vedas, Kṛṣṇa himself, who is the most perfect Supreme Being, [acted accordingly].
He revealed his supreme true form together with Rādhā.
Seeing that beautiful form, they all indeed fell into a swoon.
Filled with sattvic states of being, they forgot the comfort of their own bodies. ||36||
Then all were filled with joy by musical instruments of sweet sound.
O King, they sang that before him while the virtuous looked on. 37.
Just as it was heard, so it was seen: a sweetness and a form truly marvelous.
In that very manner, Veda and the others performed a description of the conduct of the King of Mithilā.
The Veda said:
He is pure consciousness alone, both existent and non-existent, the supreme, the vast, the eternal, the ever-peaceful, the all-pervading, the equal, and the great.
I praise you, O Brahman, who are difficult for even the Vasus to attain, the supreme one who has forever transcended all deceit by means of your own self-effulgence. 39.
Sarasvatī said: "The yogis indeed know you as the Supreme Greatness, while the Sātvatas declare that there you possess a manifest form."
But that pair of feet of mine which you have seen shall become the sovereign of great blessings and well-being. (40)
The Gandharvas said:
"The dark and the fair have been made known by you through your own power; indeed, this state has been brought about by your own will."
You shine eternally and perfectly with those two, like a dark cloud accompanied by streaks of lightning. ||41||
The Apsarases said:
"Just as a tamāla tree shines with a golden creeper, or as a dark cloud gleams with a flash of lightning."
The blue king of mountains was like a touchstone-mine for Śrī Rādhā, and likewise, the primordial one was with his beloved.
The villages said:
"The dust of whose foot is [sought] by Śambhu, Ramā, and the gods."
If you desire that, O Rādhā, then worship the feet of Mādhava.
The Tālas said:
"One should take away only that strength by which Bali might enjoy a good dwelling."
Worship that foot of Hari within the cave of your heated heart.
The Gānas said:
"The virtuous cast out their suffering once they have gone for refuge to him."
We place the divine lotus feet of Rādhā and Mādhava [upon our heads]. ||45||
The Svaras said:

[We salute him] who possesses a beauty like an autumnal blossoming lotus, who is intensely hostile to the elephant of Māra, who is licked by the sage-like bees, and who is marked with the signs of the thunderbolt and the lotus.
I hold within my heart, O Lord of Rādhā, Your two feet, which possess shimmering golden anklets, which shatter the threefold torments of Your devotees, and which radiate moving luster.

Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter, titled "Description of the Praise of the Vedas and Other Scriptures," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Śrī Viśvajit-khaṇḍa of the glorious Śrī Garga Saṃhitā. ||44||
Śrī Nārada said: The hosts of musical modes (rāgas), beginning with Bhairava, arrived before the Lord Hari.
Seeing her body, whose limbs were perfectly proportioned to its form, they were filled with exceeding joy. ||1||
And wherever their gaze indeed fell upon the body of Hari, [there they were liberated].
And remaining there, she was indeed unable to depart because of her loveliness. ||2||
Oh, how wonderful is the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra, the Lord Hari!
They also each separately gave descriptions of what they had seen of him. ||3||
Bhairava said:
"Worship the two knees of Hari," thus [spoke] Lakṣmī.
He always embraces her with his two lotus-like hands. ||4||
Meghamallāra said:
O Viṣṇu, I meditate upon your two thighs, which are like segments of a plantain tree and resemble venerable golden pillars.
Both of Kṛṣṇa’s [arms] were full of vitality, endowed with beauty, and yellowed by the dust of his garments. ||5||
Dīpaka said:
[I praise Him] who brings about all happiness and bears the luster of gold.
Worship the celebrated foot of Hari upon the surface of her hip.
Mālakośa said: "The hips and hair of Hari exist there; they steal away the sight of men through their eyes."
But she, being shaken by gentle breezes, moved slowly; thus she captivated the hearts of all. ||7||
Śrīrāga said: "The abode of Nābhi is like a lotus-pool, charming with its ponds, sacrificial sessions, creepers, and waves."
I eternally worship the hairline of the Lord of Rādhikā in my heart, which has utterly abandoned the forest of desire. ||8||
Hiṇḍola said: Is it a row of syllables, or a row of offerings, or a garland of delusion upon a pipal leaf?
Is this the dark line upon the lotus? Or is it the line of hair upon the belly? ||9||
The passionate women of Bhairava said:
"That yellow garment of Kṛṣṇa-Hari is endowed with a brilliance like that of Indra’s bow."
Adorned with beautiful golden sculptures, it removes the suffering of human beings.
The sons of Bhairava said:
"Like the four oceans, they fill the universe; like the four goals of human existence, they are indeed givers of bliss."
Those arms, like the world-supporting elephants of the quarters, appear victorious like the staffs that uphold the canopy of the world. ||11||
The passionate Meghamallārīs said:
O mind, worship the sweet lower lip of Hari, adorned with the luster of a ripe bimba fruit.
The beautiful form of the lord, the beloved of King Sakalavallabha, [resembles] a fresh lotus petal. ||12||
The sons of Meghamallāra said:
"Of camphor, ketaka flowers, pearls, and diamonds; of sandalwood, the moon, lightning, nectar, and jasmine..."
Formerly, that row of stainless teeth which belonged to the Supreme One when He was remembering them caused both their delight and their humiliation.
The Dīpakarāgiṇīs said:
May that which has arisen from Your pair of eyes protect us day and night—
that [vision] which is beyond the reach of the arrows of Madana and is the initiation into all beauty.
Her sidelong glance, which has surpassed millions upon millions of celestial trees, which is protected by her own father, and which is skilled in bestowing gifts. (14)
The sons of Dīpaka said:
"Or rather, what is this pair of kuliṅga birds dwelling in the midst of a fresh lotus, like a pair of sharpened swords for the destruction of their suffering?"
Does the victorious bow of the god whose banner is the sea-monster triumph here, or is it the circle of brows on the face of this moon-like woman? 15.
The women of Mālakośa said:
"The moon-disk dances like two wives of a serpent with their dangling earrings."
Like a swarm of bees upon lotuses brimming with nectar, [they settle] upon her beautiful, rounded cheeks. 16.
The sons of Mālakośa said: "Is it the sun itself in the circle of the sky, or is it lightning amidst the clouds of the Lord of the Yadus?"
It presides over the orb of the cheeks, a fragment of radiance, like an earring of refined gold.
The Śrīrāgiṇīs said:
"Indeed, a battle took place among the women over the two Khañjana birds, who had become the offspring of Kaliṅga."
Among them, the parrot has departed for the lotus blossoming at dawn, desiring to assume the crimson hue of its reflection. ||18||
The sons of Śrīrāga said:
[We behold] Hari, who has made his yellow garment his attendant and whose neck is bowed by the crowns of peacocks.
I worship him who holds a staff and a bamboo flute, whose earrings sway, who is most skillful, and who wears a humble disguise. ||19||
The women of the Ḥiṇḍola rāga said:
"He whose splendor is comparable to the flax flower stands amidst the kadamba trees on the banks of the Yamunā."
May the one wearing a forest garland, who delights in the pastimes with the young cowherd wives, extend auspicious blessings. ||20||
The sons of Hiṇḍola said:
"O Hari, there is no sinner on earth equal to me, and likewise, there is no remover of sins equal to you."
Thus, considering you to be the Lord of the Universe, do with me as you wish. ||21||
Śrī Nārada said:
Whoever always hears or recites this meditation performed through passion, [attains the fruit].
The Blessed One, who is compassionate toward his devotees, comes within the range of his vision. ||22||
Having thus presented his own philosophical system, Hari himself [spoke] from the Vedas and other sources.
As they looked on, the four-armed wielder of the Śārṅga bow appeared.
Having beheld Viṣṇu, the Lord departed together with his attendants.
Having stationed the son of Śambarāri, the best of the Yadus, in the army.
The Supreme Being among the supreme resolved to go to his own city, Dvārakā.
With a chariot whose sweet sound was produced by the tinkling of small bells and ornaments on the anklets, and by the resonance of bronze vessels;
And he was joined by Sugrīva and his chief attendants, who were as swift as horses, along with Dāruka, O Prince of Mithilā. ||26||
Accompanied by the sound of the Vedas, possessing the splendor of the six jewels, and with the Garuda-bannered god [Viṣṇu] stirred by the winds;
Leaving that city of the Vedas, the Supreme Self went to the city adorned by the multitude of Yādavas.

Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Meditation on Śrī Kṛṣṇa," in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva within the Śrī Viśvajit-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā. ||45||
Then, when the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa had gone to the city of Dvārāvatī,
Pradyumna went to the wish-fulfilling river (Kāmadugha) together with his soldiers. ||1||
Extending for a hundred yojanas, it was enchanting to the Gandharvas.
There is a city named Vasanta-mālā, composed of gold and jewels. ||2||
With nets of *lavaṅga* creepers and with products from the regions of Elā and Kaśmīra.
With nutmeg and other spices, jāyitrī, sandalwood, and pārijātaka [flowers]. ||3||
It resounded with the humming of intoxicated bees and was made vocal by birds of variegated plumage.
It was graced by noble Gandharvas, like Bhogavatī is graced by Nāgas.
In that very place, there was a Gandharva lord of great power named Pataṅga.
The virtuous one rules his kingdom with strength and prowess like Śakra. ||5||
Having heard that Pradyumna had arrived, having set out for the conquest of the quarters, [he went forth].
Accompanied by formidable Gandharvas, he set his mind on engaging in battle.
And with ten koṭis of gandharvas, along with heroes on chariots, horses, and elephants.
Pataṅga arrived to fight in the very presence of Pradyumna.
A terrible battle indeed took place between the Gandharvas and the Yadus.
With bhallas, maces, iron clubs, mallets, javelins, and spears.
When a darkness of arrows had arisen, the powerful great chariot-warrior Pataṅga appeared.
Making his bow twang, the powerful one arrived and roared like a thundercloud.
The powerful younger brother of Baladeva, taking up his mace, [advanced].
He crushed that army as Indra crushes a mountain with his thunderbolt.
Some Gandharvas fell in battle by Gada’s mace.
All the chariots were crushed to pieces, and the elephants had their heads split open.
Certain heroes mounted on horses fell upon the front lines of the battle.
The Gandharvas were with their faces turned downward or upward, and their arms were severed.
In a mere moment, a river of blood indeed arose within that army.
In the battle, the Pramathas seized the heads for the sake of Hara’s garland.
Bhadrakālī is mounted upon a lion, surrounded by a hundred ḍākinīs.
Even with skulls, they are seen drinking blood in the battle.
Thus, during that battle caused by the mace, the Gandharvas fled.
Then the Lord of the Gandharvas arrived, accompanied by a force of one hundred thousand elephants.
O King of Mithilā, Pataṅga struck Gada in the chest with his mace.
Gada also struck him with his own mace on the chest with great force, like a moth [attacking a flame].
And between those two, there was a mace-duel for two ghaṭikās.
The two maces, emitting sparks, were reduced to powder. ||17||
Quickly taking up a heavy mace weighing a hundred thousand bhāras.
The moth, intoxicated by the battle, struck him on the head with his mace. ||18||
