Then, having performed the twilight ritual and offered milk and other substances, he should proceed.
Then, at the time of dusk, one should again perform the ritual waving of lights (ārati). ||26||
Having provided the supreme and most delicious food, one should prepare the bed for Hari.
And it is indeed rajasic, O Indra among kings; this is truly of the nature of rajas.
With his mind entirely intent upon the service of Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra.
Having delivered a hundred generations of his lineage, he goes to the ultimate state. ||28||
The Janmāṣṭamī of Kṛṣṇa and likewise the Śrī Rāmanavamī.
The Rādhāṣṭamī, the Annakūṭa, and the Vāmana-dvādaśī. ||29||
The fourteenth day [of the lunar fortnight] is for Nṛsiṃha, as is the Anantacaturdaśī.
During these times, one should perform the great worship of Kṛṣṇa. ||30||
Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Description of Royal Service," in the section on Knowledge within the Śrī Garga Saṃhitā, in the dialogue between Śrī Vyāsa and Ugrasena. ||7||
Śrī Vyāsa said:
Then, having bathed and performed the daily and occasional rites, he—
Endowed with five colors, upon a pure sacrificial ground mandala.
Endowed with thirty-two petals, it is radiant with a pericarp and filaments.
Having fashioned a lotus and established it according to the rules with Vedic hymns. ||2||
O King, one should place the auspicious lion-throne of Hari upon the pericarp.
There, having established Rādhā, Ramā, Bhūdevī, and likewise Virajā; ||3||
In the center of that, one should place Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, in person.
Likewise, in the center of the eight-petaled lotus, one should place the auspicious eight companions of Rādhikā. ||4||
Then, in the center of the eight-petaled lotus, [one should worship] Śrī Kṛṣṇa as well as his companions.
Likewise, upon the sixteen petals, there are two for each of the female friends. ||5||
And on the sides of the lotus, [he should place] a conch, a discus, and likewise a mace.
And the lotus, the Nandaka sword, the Śārṅga bow, arrows, the mace, and the plow.
The Kaustubha gem, the forest garland, the Śrīvatsa mark, and the blue garment.
Likewise, the wise one should place the yellow garment, the flute, and the staff. ||7||
Then, on the sides [of the chariot], there were likewise the marks of palm trees and the mark of Garuḍa upon the chariot.
Sumati, the charioteer Dāruka, Garuḍa, and likewise Kumuda. ||8||
Caṇḍa, Pracaṇḍa, Bala, and Mahābala.
The wise person should diligently install both Kumudākṣa and Bala.
Likewise, having installed the guardians of the directions individually in their respective quarters.
Viṣvaksena, Śiva, myself, Brahmā, Durgā, and Vināyaka. ||10||
And the nine planets, as well as Varuṇa and the sixteen Mātṛkās.
The wise one should place Vītihotra upon the sacrificial mound at the tip of that lotus.
The invocation, the seat, the water for the feet, and especially the water for the guest-offering (arghya).
And likewise, bathing, the honey-mixture offering, incense, and a lamp. ||12||
The sacred thread, a garment, an ornament, and even perfume—
Likewise, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), and a beautiful food offering (naivedya). ||13||
Water for sipping (ācamana), betel leaf, and likewise a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) should be offered.
Circumambulation, prayer, and likewise the waving of lights (nīrājana) are thus prescribed. ||14||
Then one should perform salutations, both through ritual action and individually.
For the invocation, flowers are used; for the seat, two blades of kusha grass.
For the water for washing the feet (pādya), one should likewise offer śyāmā grass, dūrvā grass, and viṣṇukrāntā.
O Yādava, *saugandhika* flowers are suitable for the water-offering (*arghya*). (16)
Mixed with sandalwood, uśīra, camphor, saffron, and agallochum.
O high-minded King, such water as this is suitable for bathing. (17)
For it is considered that the honey-mixture (madhuparka) consists of āmalaka fruit and lotus.
In the incense offering, the eight fragrances should be given, and in the lamp offering, camphor alone.
The sacred thread is yellow, and the two garments are considered to be yellow robes.
And for ornaments, gold; for fragrance, saffron and sandalwood. (19)
Tulasī blossoms should be used for flowers, and unbroken rice grains for the *akṣata* offerings.
In the food offering, however, the six tastes and various kinds of enjoyments are considered appropriate. ||20||
Among waters, the water of the Gaṅgā and the water of the Yamunā are suitable.
And nutmeg and kankola at the end of the sipping of water, O King. (21)
In betel, cardamom is the "chewing" [ingredient], while gold is the sacrificial fee for the southern direction.
In the rite of circumambulation, there is the act of walking around; in the rite of lustration with ghee, it is performed for cows.
In prayer, devotion to Hari is conjoined with the characteristic of love.
O Great King, during prostration, one's body should be bent down with its eight limbs. ||23||
Having tied his topknot with the twelve-syllable mantra, the pure man, being purified, [should proceed].
Having placed the ritual services before him, one should face the venerable mouth [of the deity]. ||24||

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Procedure for the Great Worship," in the section on Knowledge within the Śrī-Garga-Saṃhitā, in the dialogue between Śrī Vyāsa and Ugrasena. ||8||
Śrī Vyāsa said: [I shall describe] the auspicious mantras for the ritual services as declared in the Vedas.
I shall speak to you, O Indra among kings; listen with a one-pointed mind.
Now follows the invocation: O Lord of the abode of Goloka, O Consort of Ramā, Govinda, Dāmodara, you who are compassionate toward the distressed!
O Lord of Rādhā, O Mādhava, O Lord of the Sātvatas, be present before me upon this lion-throne. ||2||
Then there was a seat with a back that shone with precious rubies and lotus feet inlaid with costly lapis lazuli.
O Vaikuṇṭha, O Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, accept this yellow fragment of a jar from the city of Taḍiddhāṭaka. ||3||
Then there stood the supreme water for the feet, collected from Lake Bindu in a stainless golden vessel.
O Lord of Yoga, Lord of the Vedas, Abode of the Universe, accept this water for the feet; I bow at Your feet. ||4||
Then [he offered] the pure *arghya*, accompanied by water-born and *campaka* flowers, which remained priceless within the vessel.
Accept [this], O Lord, delighter of Ramā, Lord of the Yadus, Protector of the Yadus, Supreme among the Yadus! ||5||
Then, the bath [was performed] with water mixed with saffron and sandalwood,
along with jasmine and ushira root.
Perform your bath, O Lord of the Yadus, O God Govinda, O Protector of the cows, whose feet are the sacred ford! ||6||
Then follows the honey-mixture bath (madhuparka-snāna),
which arises from the midday moon and sun, removes all impurities, and is supremely enchanting through contact with the white-bodied [deity].
O Viṣṇu, O Lord of the Sātvatas, clad in yellow garments, look upon this and accept the madhuparka offering. (7)
Then, O Lord, there appeared a garment that shone brilliantly on all sides, beautiful with its shimmering rays, supreme, and exceedingly rare.
O Lord, take this self-created garment, the color of lotus filaments, known as the "Yellow Robe. (8)
Then [he should wear] the sacred thread (yajñopavīta),
which has the luster of gold or a yellowish hue, which has been consecrated with supreme mantras, and which was fashioned by one learned in the Vedas.
O Lord, for the sake of the five auspicious rites and on these specific occasions, please accept this sacrifice and this sacred thread. ||9||
Then there appeared an ornament made of gold and jewels, fashioned by Maya,
which destroys the pain of love and is an abode of splendors.
O Pūṣan, at dawn, accept this golden ornament, which is an ornament for all the worlds. ||10||
Then [he offered] perfumes, beautiful as the moon at twilight, highly auspicious, and blended with the paste of fragrant Kashmiri sandalwood.
O bearer of the burden of the entire circle of the earth, accept this collection of fragrances for your own adornment.
Then [he took] the unbroken grains (akṣata),
which had been sown previously by Brahmā in Brahmāvarta and sprinkled with the waters of Brahmā as well as by Viṣṇu.
O Abundant One, accept those who have been protected from the Rākṣasas by Rudra and have remained uninjured before your very eyes.
Then [he offered] flowers from the mandāra, santānaka, pārijātaka, kalpadruma, and śrīharicandana trees.
O Hari, take these flowers mixed with fresh tulasī blossoms.
Then, [he offered] incense mixed with the powders of cloves and sandalwood, which bestows happiness upon humans, gods, and asuras.
O King of Dvārāvatī, accept this incense, which instantly perfumes the palace grounds. 14.
Then [he offered] that lamp, which dispels darkness, is the embodiment of knowledge, and is beautiful with its shimmering wick and abundance of camphor and cow’s ghee.
O Lord Jagannātha, O Master, O Lamp of the Universe, accept this foremost of lamps with its shimmering light. ||15||
Then the food offering was prepared with the five flavors according to the rules for their classification,
enriched with those flavors, and made by Yaśomatī.
Accept this most delightful food offering, the nectar of cow's milk, O beautiful son of Nanda! (16)
Then, with a golden vessel, he drew up water as cool as the moon, which had been lifted from the Ganges by the force of its northern current.
O beloved of Rādhā, O you who are affectionate toward your devotees, please accept this water which is exceedingly pure and like nectar. 17.
Now, O Lord of Rādhā, O Lord of Śrī Virajā, O Master, O Lord of Śrī, O Lord of all, and O Lord of the earth! [Herein is] the ritual sipping of water (ācamana).
O ocean of compassion, please accept this supreme water for sipping, scented with *kaṅkola*, nutmeg, and flowers. (18)
Then there was betel-leaf, combined with nutmeg, cardamom, cloves, betel-vine leaves, and areca nuts.
O Lord of Ramā, accept this betel leaf, prepared with pearls, lime, and the heartwood of the khadira tree. 19.
Now, O Lord Hari, whose pair of feet is saluted by the crowns of Nākapāla and Vasupāla, [I offer] this sacrificial fee.
Accept this sacrificial fee, O Mādhava, you who are skilled in the world; for you, the bestower of boons, there is no need for a fee.
Then follows the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), a most radiant and auspicious spectacle, featuring five new wicks soaked in cow’s ghee.
Accept this lamp, O destroyer of suffering, you who have made the earth radiant with the fame of your merit! 21.
Now, the salutation:
Homage be to the Infinite One, who possesses a thousand forms,
a thousand feet, eyes, heads, thighs, and arms.
Salutation to the eternal Puruṣa of a thousand names, who sustains a thousand crores of yugas. ||22||
Now, the merit of circumambulation is equal to the fruit arising from all pilgrimages, sacrifices, gifts, and works of public utility.
He who performs a circumambulation [of this] obtains the eternal state of another. ||23||
Now, O Hari, my prayer is this: there is no sinner on earth equal to me,
and likewise, there is no remover of sins equal to you.
Thus, O Lord of the World, O God, having considered this, do with me as you wish. ||24||
Now follows the praise:
It is mere consciousness, both existent and non-existent, supreme, great, eternal, tranquil, all-pervasive, equal, and vast.
I indeed worship you, the Brahman, who are exceedingly difficult to attain, the Supreme, who eternally transcends all deceit by your own splendor. 25.
Having thus worshipped the Lord of Gods with these mantras, O great-minded one.
Having prostrated before Viṣṇu, one should diligently perform the worship of all his limbs.
Oṃ, salutations to Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person, the Great Soul.
We meditate upon the Great Swan, who abides in the intellect of pure beings. ||27||
Having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma) with this mantra,
[one should offer obeisance] to Oṃ Viṣṇu, Madhusūdana, Vāmana, Trivikrama,
Śrīdhara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha, and Dāmodara.
Salutation to Saṃkarṣaṇa, Vāsudeva, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Adhokṣaja, Puruṣottama, and Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

Thus, one should perform the worship of all the limbs, thinking: "I worship separately [the Lord] in the feet, ankles, knees, thighs, hips, belly, back, arms, neck, ears, nose, lips, eyes, and head. Likewise, [one should worship] His companions, the friends, the conch, discus, mace, lotus, sword, bow, arrows, plow, pestle, and so forth; as well as the Kaustubha gem, the forest garland, the Śrīvatsa mark, the yellow garment, the blue garment, the flute, the staff, and so forth; and likewise Tālaṅka, Garuḍāṅka, the chariot, Dāruka, Sumati, the charioteer, Garuḍa, Kumuda, Nanda, Sunanda, Caṇḍa, Mahābala, Kumudākṣa, and others.

One should worship with the names preceded by the *praṇava* (oṃ), ending in the dative case, and joined with *namaḥ*; likewise, one should worship Viṣvaksena, Śiva, Vidhi, Durgā, Vināyaka, the guardians of the directions, Varuṇa, the nine planets, the Mothers, and others with their respective mantras.
Oṃ, salutation to Vāsudeva, and salutation to Saṃkarṣaṇa.
Salutation to Pradyumna, to Aniruddha, and to the Lord of the Sātvatas. ||28||
With this mantra, one should offer a hundred oblations.
Having circumambulated the deity and having deposited great wealth, he departed.
One should prostrate like a staff upon the ground and utter this mantra: ||29||
I am the object of meditation, the eternal destroyer of humiliation, the bestower of desired objects, the abode of sacred pilgrimage sites, praised by Śiva and Viriñci, and the worthy refuge.
O dispeller of the distress of your servants, O protector of those who bow before you, I worship your lotus-feet, O Great Being, which are a boat for crossing the ocean of existence. 30.
Having thus bowed to Hari, O King, one should again perform the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) for Hari.
A devotee should cause it to be performed according to the rules, together with the people who are devotees of Hari. ||31||
With the sounding of ghaṭī-instruments, ringing bells, bronze cymbals, lutes, and flutes;
The wise person should cause kīrtana to be performed with cymbals, mṛdaṅga drums, and other such instruments. ||32||
The devotees, overwhelmed with love, indeed dance before Śrī Hari.
Accompanied by sounds of victory, they were intent upon sacred stories and song. ||33||
Having again paid homage to the Lord in the temple, which was radiant with the light of the sun;
One should properly prepare the bed of the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ||34||
Thus does he perform service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose mind is firmly attached.
And the deities born in heaven bow down to him, O King. ||35||
O Indra among kings, that person also, having secured a place in heaven, becomes a servant of Hari.
In the end, he goes to the supreme abode, Goloka, which is difficult even for yogis to attain. ||36||
Thus, the method for the service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa has been described by me.
It bestows the four goals of human life upon men; what more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "Description of the Method for Serving Śrī Kṛṣṇa," in the Vijñānakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garga Saṃhitā, within the dialogue between Śrī Vyāsa and Ugrasena. ||9||
Ugrasena said:
"I am perfected; I am graced by you who possess the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa."
The Śrīkṛṣṇapaddhati has indeed been heard by me directly according to the prescribed rules. ||1||
Alas, people are utterly deluded, possessed by greed, delusion, and pride!
For they do not attain detachment, nor do they ever worship Hari. ||2||
O Blessed One, the cause of delusion for this world is truly marvelous.
Tell me, O Lord, how it is born, and how it ceases? ||3||
Śrī Vyāsa said:
Just as one who has entered the water perceives the moon from the sky solely through its rapid movement, so too does he perceive it.
For in this way, the reflection of the Supreme proceeds through illusion, arising when the notions of "mine" and "I" have taken hold. ||4||
A person, performing forbidden actions through the qualities born of primary nature, time, disposition, and the body, becomes bound.
He perceives a child in a glass vessel, life itself in a sandy riverbed, and a serpent in a mere thread— thus he views things with his eyes.
O King, the world consists of delusion, and is composed of passion (rajas), darkness (tamas), and likewise, in some places, of goodness (sattva).
Know that this flickering mind is a playful whim, a distortion, and a delusion, like a whirling firebrand.
"I shall do this," "I am doing it," "I was," and "this is mine"— thus they speak, being possessed by ignorance.
I am happy, while my circle of friends is joined with suffering; thus is the world considered, deluded by the ego-sense. ||7||
Ugrasena said:
O Brāhmaṇa, please tell me out of compassion the characteristics of the Supreme Self.
O Kṛṣṇa, how many kinds of sages do they describe on the path of japa? ||8||
Śrī Vyāsa said: In this regard, for the Eternal One (Sanātana), there is neither birth nor death, neither grief nor delusion, nor old age, physical decay, and so forth.
Pride, disease, fear, pleasure, sorrow, hunger, desire, lack of delight, and mental anxieties—none of these exist [there]. || 9 ||
The Self is indeed effortless, formless, all-pervading, devoid of egoism, possessed of pure strength, and the locus of the qualities.
He who is himself the Supreme, fruitless, the source of his own auspiciousness, and whose nature is knowledge, is known by the lords of sages. ||10||
He who remains awake when this person has gone to sleep— he, and no other, knows what is beneficial for him.
I worship that primordial Person whom people do not see, though He sees all, and who is both pure and stainless. 11.
Just as the ether, fire, and wind are not attached to a pot, nor to wood, nor covered by dust;
Likewise, the person, pure through all qualities, becomes as radiant as a crystal by means of the colors. ||12||
Or [he perceives] the Supreme through elliptical expressions, through figurative indications, through paths of speech, through meanings, and through those devoted to the *padasphoṭa*.
Even by the highest among those possessing its qualities, that Brahman cannot be properly described; how much less so, then, by worldly people? (13)
Some say that on this earth the agent of action is the cause, while others say that time alone is the most excellent cause.
Some proclaim it to be discernment (vicāra), for those who know the Vedanta indeed declare that to be Brahman. ||14||
That which the qualities do not touch here, nor those born of time, nor illusion, the senses, mind, thought, or the intellects;
"The Great Veda speaks"—thus they all enter that Supreme [Self], like sparks from a fire. ||15||
Hiraṇyagarbha is the reality of the Supreme Self, whom the wise call Vāsudeva.
Having reflected upon that true nature of the Supreme Lord and having cast off delusion, one should wander about free from attachment. ||16||
Just as the single moon appears in a multitude of water vessels, and as the single fire is perceived in a heap of fuel;
Likewise, the Lord, the Supreme Self, who possesses manifold knowledge, exists both internally and externally within the embodied beings created by Himself. (17)
Just as at sunrise the darkness of night dissolves and objects within a house become visible to people;
Upon the arising of knowledge, the darkness of ignorance is dissolved;
likewise, the supreme Brahman is attained within the body.
Just as the objects of the senses, though appearing diverse through the distinct operations of the faculties, are in truth that supreme reality which is the locus of manifold qualities.
For that abode of the one, infinite, and supreme [Brahman] is indeed thus for the sages through the dharmas of the scriptures. 19.
He who is Hari manifest, the most excellent among the Supreme Persons, Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra, who is affectionate toward his own devotees.
The Lord of Liberation rescued that Nṛga;
I bow down to Him, the perfect, supreme Brahman Himself. 20.
The venerable Nārada said:
Having spoken thus and having taken leave of him, the blessed Bādarāyaṇa—
And even as the Yādavas were looking on, he vanished right there.
This which increases devotion to Hari has been told by me to you.
The section on consciousness is pure and is remembered as bestowing liberation upon listeners. ||22||
This work, spoken by Gargācārya, is known by the name Gargasamhitā.
It removes all defects, is meritorious, and bestows the fruits of the four aims of life. ||23||
Of Goloka and Vṛndāvana, of the sweetness of Girīśvara, and of the city of Śrī Mathurā.
There are nine separate sections concerning Dvārāvatī, Viśvajit, Halāyudha, and Vijñāna. 24.
Just as the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is [sustained] by the supreme nectars, so too is the earth abundantly supported by Bharata and the others.
For thus, O lord of men, the Saṃhitā of the sage Garga shines eternally in nine sections.
For just as a seal of refined gold shines upon the finger of a god with its nine jewels, so does she shine.
Likewise, the Saṃhitā of the sage Garga [is composed] in cantos and chapters concerning the ritual that bestows the fruits of the four aims of life. 26.
O King, those people who constantly listen with devotion to the compendium of sages are indeed purified.
Attaining supreme happiness right here, they thereafter proceed to the city of Goloka.
Then, having performed this salutation to the Yellow-Robed One (Pītāmbara), even a barren woman who is intensely longing will hear [the fruit of her desire].
For a short time, she wandered day and night about the courtyard of the house, tending the children. ||28||
A sick man is liberated from the multitude of diseases; one who is afraid is freed from fear, and one who has fallen into bondage is released from that bond.
Having heard this story, even a poor man attains prosperity, and a fool quickly becomes a wise scholar. 29.
The king who, endowed with prosperity, constantly listens to the Saṃhitā of the sage Garga during the month of Kārttika;
He will become a universal monarch, there is no doubt, with beautiful sandals held in the hands of the lord of men. ||30||
With new horses swift as thought from the ocean, and with excellent elephants born on the Vindhya mountains;
His fame was sung by bards upon the earth, and he was attended by courtesans. ||31||
A cow with golden horns, a fine copper-colored back,
adorned with ornaments, silver hooves, and accompanied by her calf.
He who gives two cows for every piece of sugar-candy shall indeed attain all his heart's desires. ||32||
The King of Videha listens without any ulterior motive to this entire Saṃhitā of the sage Garga.
In his heart-lotus dwells forever Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra, who is affectionately devoted to his own devotees. 33.
The illustrious Garga said:
Having spoken thus and having taken leave of him, Nārada, who has the vision of the gods, departed.
O Brahman, while everyone was looking on, the sage ascended into the sky.
The great king Bahulāśva had his mind fixed upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
But having heard this compendium of Hari, he became successful in every respect.
O Brahmin, this Saṃhitā has been narrated by me to you upon your inquiry.
Or if it is heard or recited by some, it bestows the fruit of ten million sacrifices. ||36||
Śrī Śaunaka said:
O great sage, I am blessed and my purpose is fulfilled through association with you.
I attain supreme devotion, which increases love for Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ||37||
In the pure hearts of the sages, he is a royal swan in their minds,
possessing a lineage of the sweetness of his voice that shines with every form of bliss.

May he who is the ornament of the lineage of heroes, who destroyed Kaṃsa with the strength of his arms, and who is praised by the virtuous, protect you—though he appears as one with a maimed limb in this world. ||38||
Having spoken thus to all those sages, the great sage Gargācārya—
Having taken leave of him with a serene mind, he prepared to depart. ||39||
The Saṃhitā of Garga, which sustains heaven and is enriched with nine creations and emanations.
Having spoken thus, Garga, who bestows the fourfold aims of life, departed for Mount Garga. ||40||
It intensely rivals the beauty of an autumnal full-blown lotus, is licked by bees, and is marked with the signs of the thunderbolt and the lotus.

I hold within my heart the two feet of the Lord of Rādhā, which possess shimmering golden anklets, which have shattered the threefold fire of the devotee's suffering, and which radiate moving luster. 41.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Supreme Brahman," within the dialogue between Śrī Vyāsa and Ugrasena, which is part of the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Bahulāśva, in the Vijñānakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garga Saṃhitā. ||10||
Having paid homage to Nārāyaṇa and to Nara, the best of men, [the author composes this work].
Then one should utter the victory of Goddess Sarasvatī and Vyāsa. ||1||
Salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra, and salutations to Saṃkarṣaṇa as well.
Homage to the god Pradyumna; homage again and again to Aniruddha. ||2||
The illustrious Garga said:
Having seen the son of Romaharṣaṇa arrived in the assembly hall...
Śaunaka, having prostrated and offered his salutations, questioned him thoroughly.
Śaunaka said:
O great-minded one, from your mouth all the scriptures and Purāṇas [have been heard].
Indeed, various pure deeds of Hari have been heard.
Long ago, the Garga-saṃhitā was recounted by Garga in my presence.
In which the greatness of Rādhā and Mādhava is described at great length. ||3||
Today I wish to hear from you once again the stories of Kṛṣṇa.
O Sauti, having reflected upon it, tell me that which removes all suffering.
The illustrious Garga said:
"And by eighty-eight thousand sages, [the son] of Romaharṣaṇa..."
Being questioned, he spoke while remembering the lotus feet of Hari-Kṛṣṇa.
Sauti said:
"O Śaunaka, you are blessed, for such is your intellect."
She yearned for the nectar of the pair of feet of Kṛṣṇacandra. ||6||
Indeed, the gods declare that the assembly of Vaiṣṇavas is the most excellent.
For the story of Śrī Kṛṣṇa brings about the destruction of evil. ||7||
Infinite is the life-story of Kṛṣṇacandra, which destroys all impurities.
Brahmā knows something, and likewise Umāpati knows something.
I am like a mere gnat in the ocean of the stories of Vāsudeva.
Even the gods, beginning with Brahmā, will not speak when they are deluded.
Śrī Garga [spoke] to Ugrasena, the lord of the Yādavas and king of the earth.
Having witnessed the horse sacrifice, the best of rituals, he once replied: ||10||
Blessed is the king, the lord of the Yadavas, who has performed this most excellent sacrifice.
By the command of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, I was filled with wonder by him in the city. ||11||
Indeed, I have described the stories of Kṛṣṇa in the Saṃhitā.

While the hero was speaking thus, by the command of the army commander, indeed—

Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Garga said: Then indeed Balvala, having joyfully placed his son upon the chariot, [proceeded].

The Yādavas are indeed heroes in every respect, and they are all bearers of weapons.

O King, among them stood the monarchs Indranīla and the others.

And among them, O Indra of kings, were the brothers of Kṛṣṇa, headed by Gada.

O King, having formed such a circular array (cakravyūha) there;

O King, a tumultuous battle took place there on the shore of the Sindhu.
Just as the Yādavas [overwhelmed] the Dānavas, and the oceans [swallowed up] other oceans.
There, chariot-warriors fought with chariot-warriors, and those mounted on elephants with elephant-riders.

With nooses, battle-axes, O King, śataghnīs, and bhuśuṇḍis, ||11||

Nyagrodha, Duḥsvabhāva, Durmada, and likewise Kavi.

O Indra among kings, all the days of the month of Kārtika have passed there.
O King, the enraged Balvala repeatedly twanged his bow.

the mighty one, lotus-eyed, and the elder brother of Kṛṣṇa.
The lord of serpents (Śeṣa), however, is the lord of the earth, appearing like blue garments. || 33 ||
The Lord of Vraja, who bestows great happiness, who brings about autumn, summer, and the rainy season, who is dark-complexioned,
Staying at Kadambe, he is the giver of bark-garments and the Lord of Sundarī. || 34 ||

He who destroys hunger, who does not touch the sacrificial wife with his hand, the creator of compassion, the performer of divine play, the Lord of the Earth; he who destroyed Indra’s sacrifice in Vraja, who eats sparingly, and who, in the form of a child, brought about the delusion of Indra (Śunāsīra). || 35 ||
The worshiper of the mountain, the son of Nanda, Agādha, the compassionate one named Govardhanoddhārin,
as well as the remover of wind and rain and the protector;
Being apprehensive of the cowherd women of Vraja, he remained [there]. || 36 ||
On the mountain of Agendra, he who is worshipped by Śakra was praised; formerly known as Mṛṣāśikṣaka, O Lord, he is named Govinda.
He is the protector of the lord of Vraja, worshipped by Varuṇa (Pāśin), and together with his younger brothers born of cowherds, he is the beholder of divine Vaikuṇṭha.

He whose flute-song is moving and charming, the lover of the beloveds in Vraja who infatuates the women of desire, who can assume any form at will, who is steeped in aesthetic rasa, the connoisseur of rasa, the performer of the rāsa dance, the Lord of Rādhikā— [I bow to Him].
He is the great deluder who steals away the pride of the proud woman. || 38 ||
The excellent dweller who steals the pride [of Rādhikā], whose limbs are like those of Rādhikā, who moves upon the earth and its islands, who wanders through the regions, who abides in the forest,
who is indeed beloved, who has eight faces, who is seen by the sages, and who is accompanied by Sārādha.
The bestower of great liberation, the remover of the lotus, he whose purpose is the beloved. || 39 ||
The Lord dwelling in the banyan tree, anointed with sandalwood paste, has indeed come to Vraja, being attached to Rādhā among those who enchant;
He is the creator of great delusion, His glory sung by the gopīs.
Seated upon his chariot, he was the lord of distressed women who long for him. || 40 ||

In the forest, He is the artisan who displays the footprints made by abandoning the cowherd girls; He is the deluder of desire, the self-controlled one dwelling in the midst of the cowherd girls, the maker of pleasing words for His beloved, the one devoted to the rāsa dance, and the Lord of the arts. || 41 ||
For His heart is filled with the essence of nectar, His true nature is infinite,
He is adorned with a garland, and He stands in the midst of the cowherd girls;
He has beautiful arms, beautiful feet, a beautiful form, and beautiful hair.
The Lord of Vraja, the friend, the Lord of the beloveds, the one of the beautiful land. || 42 ||
Adorned with anklets bearing a network of tinkling bells, rich in shimmering bracelets, wearing armlets and heavy necklaces;
crowned with a diadem and swinging earrings, his chest radiant with a sparkling Kaustubha gem, his limbs embellished with *mālatī* flowers. (43)

He is the stage for a great dance, rich in arts, adorned with shimmering necklaces, and joined by the dancing of beautiful women; he is the beauty of saffron from the playful frolics on the Yamunā, and is sung of by the gods as both hero and heroine. (44)
The Lord of Rādhā is rich in bliss, possessed of perfect awakening, with sidelong glances and smiles, and the playful movement of his dancing eyebrows;
he is most beautiful, with locks of hair as dark as bees and curling locks that sway.
His attire was beautiful with a garland of shimmering peacock feathers and jasmine flowers. || 45 ||
The one whose feet are supreme for the protection of Nanda from the great serpent,
who eternally bestows liberation, who destroyed Śaṅkhacūḍa,
the protector of his subjects, and he who is sung of by the cowherd girls.
The preceptor of the gods [Jupiter] is the exertion for the destruction of the humped bull. || 46 ||

Kali, who incites anger, the instructor of Kaṃsa’s mantra, and likewise the instructor of Akrūra’s mantra for the sake of the gods; the powerful slayer of Keśin, possessed of stainless splendor and showering flowers; and the destroyer of the sky-demon, who was revealed by Nārada.
Likewise, devoted to the service of Akrūra, the all-seeing Kūlavartī appeared in Vraja to enchant the cowherd women;
he was the awakener of the virtuous Rādhikā and the creator of dreams.
The playful one, the destroyer of great delusion, is self-awareness. || 48 ||
In Vraja, the husband [Nanda] was abandoned by Rādhā due to a curse; the protector [Akrūra] was consumed by the forest fire of great delusion;
Akrūra was bewildered by the bonds of his friends; and the guards of Akrūra were struck nearby by the bracelets of the friends.
Seated upon a chariot in Vraja, Kṛṣṇacandra, accompanied by Rādhā and well-guarded by the cowherds, moves with beautiful grace;
his divine form is revealed in the water to Akrūra.
Desirous of seeing [her], he who deludes the minds of women enchanting the city [approached].
Likewise, he is the destroyer of dyers, yet possesses fine garments;
he is fond of garlands and honors garland-makers;
he bestows great fame and delights in the company of hunchbacked women.
He who has subdued the fierce [demons] with his throbbing, formidable bow. || 51 ||
Bestowing distress upon the soldiers, causing bad dreams for Kaṃsa, wearing the guise of a great wrestler, striking down the lordly elephant,
slaying the chief minister, he entered the arena.
One who possesses abundant flavors, seeks fame, is powerful, eloquent in speech, and endowed with prosperity. || 52 ||
The great wrestler, the performer of all battles, the seeker of the word's true meaning,
the leader of the earth, the slayer of Kaṃsa, the foremost of the Yadus—
ever honored and renowned through Ugrasena.
Bestowing the kingdom of Dharā, his body was adorned by the Yādavas. || 53 ||
The son of the Guru, a knower of Brahman, a reciter of the Vedas,
the bearer of the great conch, the wielder of the staff— he is indeed worthy of worship; for he was sent by Uddhava to Vraja as the deluder of the cowherds.
Yaśodā was compassionate, a cowherd woman, and one who possessed knowledge. || 54 ||
Always showing affection, his body honored by Kubjā, he went to the house of Akrūra as a knower of mantras;
thus sent by the Pāṇḍavas, Akrūra himself was happy, all-seeing, and a bringer of joy to the king. 55.
The king who brought a great akṣauhiṇī army [to Jarāsaṃdha], the builder of Dvārakā, the liberator,
the warrior praised by universal emperors, and the bestower of knowledge.
He whose feet are the refuge for those who act according to the resolve of Jarāsaṃdha.
He who emerged from the mountain, who dwells in the midst of the gateway, who is adorned by Revatī and has the palm tree as his emblem;
he who is the abductor of Rukmiṇī among the Yadus, who is known by the Caidya, who destroyed the form of Rukmin, and who is the enjoyer of bliss.
Ananta, Māra, Kārṣṇi, Kāma, Manojas, Śambarāri, Ratīśa,
Rathin, Manmatha, Mīnaketu, and Śara.
Smara, Darpaka, Mānahā, and Pañcabāṇa. || 58 ||

The beloved husband of Satyabhāmā, the lord of the Yādavas, and the one who overflowed with love for Satrājit; the one who laughed (Prahāsa), the possessor of great jewels, the one who fought with Jāmbavat, the wielder of the great discus, the wielder of the sword, and the one who joined the villages (Grāmasandhi). || 59 ||
Dwelling in the forest hermitage, he was the one who showed affection for the Pāṇḍavas, the charmer of the daughter of Kalinda (Yamunā), the seeker of the Khāṇḍava forest,
the friend who brought joy to Phālguna (Arjuna), and the burner of the forest.
Likewise, the husband of Mitravindā was desirous of sport. || 60 ||
He who bestows love upon kings, who is enriched by cattle, who possesses seven forms, and who is the Lord of Truth;

he who is accompanied by dowries as desired, who is surrounded by kings, who is the husband of Bhadrā, who is playful, who is the Lord of Spring (Madhu), and the Sovereign of the proud women among men. 61.
Murāri, who is accompanied by Śunāsīra and his wife, who is endowed with Tārkṣya, who shatters the multitude of cities,
who is a great hero, the severer of heads, and the destroyer of the Daityas.
And Śarabhauma was a great hero of fierce speed. || 62 ||
Praised by the earth, the taker of the earrings and the parasol, delightful to the great jewel-like princesses,
honored by Śacī, the conqueror of Śakra, and the destroyer of pride.
Likewise, the Lord of Ramā was the one who carried away the Pārijāta tree. || 63 ||
The householder, adorned with yak-tail fans, the husband of Bhīṣma’s daughter, the creator of laughter, the one who humbles the pride of the haughty;
likewise, he is eloquent in speech to Rukmiṇī, the abode of love, the deluder of virtuous women, possessing a splendor like that of another God of Love. (64)
Sudeṣṇa, Sucāru, and likewise Cārudeṣṇa; another was Cārudeha, as well as the powerful Cārugupta;
Sutī, Bhadracāru, and likewise Cārucandra, Vicāru, and Cāru, who was a chariot-warrior possessing the form of a son.
Subhānu, Prabhānu, Candrabhānu, Bṛhadbhānu, Aṣṭabhānu, Sāmba, Sumitra, Kratu, the heroic Citraketu, Aśvasena, Vṛṣa, Citragu, and Candrabimba. || 66 ||
Viśaṅku, Vasu, Śruta, Bhadra, Eka,
Subāhu, Vṛṣa, Pūrṇamāsa, Soma,
Vara, Śānti, Praghoṣa, and Siṃha.
For the fool is indeed one whose speech rises as high as Mount Govardhana. || 67 ||
Mahāśo, Vṛka, Pāvana, Vahnimitra, Kṣudhi, Harṣaka, Anila, Amitrajit, Subhadra, Jaya, Satyaka, Vāma, Āyu, Yadu, and Koṭiśa—renowned for their sons and grandsons in the hundreds of millions. || 68 ||
Halī, Daṇḍadhṛk, Rukmihā, and likewise Aniruddha; he who is accompanied by kings, the gambler, Madhu, Brahmasū, the husband of Bāṇaputrī, Mahāsundara, Kāmaputra, and Balīśa. || 69 ||
The lord of the Yādavas, who waged great battles against the Daityas,
the destroyer of cities, the one who causes terror among living beings, the conqueror in combat, the vanquisher of Rudra, the deluder of Rudra, and the seeker of victory.
Likewise, Skandajit, Kūpakarṇa, and Praharin. || 70 ||
The breaker of bows, the striker who humbles Bāṇa’s pride, the one praised by Jvara for causing the onset of fever,
the severer of arms, and the creator of terror for Bāṇa.
The lord of the earth, having commenced the battle with Mṛḍa, engaged in combat. || 71 ||
Bestower of liberation upon Nṛga, giver of knowledge, standing in the chariot of the Yādavas, the beloved of Vraja, the chief of cowherds,
sporting with the great beauties, and wearing a garland of flowers.
The splitter of the Kalinda-born [Yamunā], the wielder of the plow. || 72 ||
The destroyer of great deceivers, the slayer of Pauṇḍraka Māna, the cutter-off of heads, the annihilator of the King of Kāśī,
the destroyer of vast akṣauhiṇī armies, who holds the discus in his hand.
The illuminator of the city and the destroyer of the rākṣasīs. || 73 ||
The infinite mountain, the serpent, the enemy of monkeys, the one of shimmering fair complexion, the one with eyes like great lotuses,
the one who has gone beyond the village of the Kurus, and the one whose purpose is weightiness.
Praised by the Kauravas, he set out with his retinue and Samba.
The Lord of Dvārakā possesses great majesty; indeed, Nārada wanders in manifold ways as one who reveals the splendor of Śrī.
Praised by the great sages, he is the ancient god Brahmā, who eternally dwells with sixteen thousand women.
The householder, devoted to protecting the world, follows worldly custom; indeed, the Lord is surrounded by Ugrasena and provided with a fortress.
Likewise, the royal messenger is then the breaker of bonds.
He remained there, introduced by Nārada, seeking the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas.
Filled with affection for the king who composed the mantras, surrounded by his sons and grandsons, he was one who went to the village of the Kurus;
compassionate, praised by Dharmarāja, and accompanied by Bhīma.
He bestows supreme bliss; he is the creator of mantras through that which is born of Dharma.
He is the conqueror of all directions, the powerful performer of the Rājasūya sacrifice, the slayer of Jarāsaṃdha, and the very form of Bhīmasena;
likewise, he is in the form of a brahmin and the performer of mace-combat.
Compassionate, he is the one who severs the great bonds. || 78 ||
Praised by kings, he arrived at the hall of dharma surrounded by brahmins; as the preparer of sacrificial materials,
he was honored by the people and endured the wicked speech of the King of Cedi.
He is the one who effects the severing of the head of the enemy, Great Delusion. || 79 ||
He who brings splendor to the great sacrifice, the universal monarch who causes joy to kings, the wanderer who is the enemy of the gods, and who,
surrounded by his assembly, humbles the pride of the Kaurava.
Likewise, he is the destroyer of Śālva and the slayer of Yāna.
And Sabhoja, Vṛṣṇi, Madhu, Śūrasena, Daśārha, Yadu, Andhaka, Lokajit,
Dyuman, Mānahā, Varmadhṛk, and Divyaśastrin.
One's own awakening is the eternal protector and the slayer of the demons. || 81 ||
Likewise, he was the destroyer of Dantavaktra, the wielder of the mace, the one who performed pilgrimages throughout the world, the wearer of a lotus garland,
the wielder of the *kuśa* grass, the slayer of Sūta, the compassionate lord of memory, the stainless one, and the one who shattered the splendor of Balvala’s limbs.
Likewise, he is the supreme bestower of wisdom upon the formidable Duryodhana, the giver of happiness to Rohiṇī, and the lord of Revatī;
he performs great acts of charity, destroys the poverty of the Brahmins, and is always filled with love as the companion of Śrī Sudāmā.

Likewise, having heard of the solar eclipse, the all-seeing [king], accompanied by Rāma and his great army, set out for the field of Bhārgava; intent on performing ablutions and making great gifts, he proceeded seeking a meeting with Mitra. (84)
Likewise, He who brings joy to the Pāṇḍavas, who was the suitor for Kuntī, who bestowed infatuation upon Viśālākṣa, and who grants peace;
and who performed the worship of Rādhikā at the banyan tree along with the cowherd girls.
The Lord of Rādhikā’s life was surrounded by millions of her friends. || 85 ||
The Lord of Vaibhava, who extinguishes the forest fire of his friends' delusion,
who possesses the distinctive charm of ten million radiant Kandarapas,
and who is the playful dispeller of Rādhikā’s sorrow— [to him I bow].
Surrounded by his companions, the Lord of Mādhavī removes all curses.

The Lord of Vraja, who for a hundred years removed the distress of Nanda’s son, who rested upon Nanda’s chest with his limbs cool to the touch, who washed away Yaśodā’s grief and destroyed her sorrow, remains forever fixed in the eyes of the gopīs.
Praised by Devakī and Rohiṇī, the lord of gods, who bestows secret knowledge and honor upon the cowherd women;
likewise praised by the principal queens, he is indeed the eternal worshipful lord of Lakṣmaṇā’s life.
Śuka, Vyāsadeva, Sumantu, and Śitikaṇṭha, whose limbs were praised by thirty-two thousand women;
Bharadvāja, Gautama, Āsuri, along with Vasiṣṭha, Śatānanda, and the foremost Rāma—[these are the sages]. (89)
The sage Parvata, Nārada, Dhaumya, Indra, Asita, Atri, Vibhāṇḍaka, Pracetas, and Kṛpa; Kumāra, Sananda, as well as Yājñavalkya, Ṛbhu, Aṅgiras, Devala, and the illustrious Mṛkaṇḍu. || 90 ||
Marīci, Kratu, Aurvaka, Lomaśa,
Pulastya, Bhṛgu, Brahmarāta, Vasiṣṭha, as well as Nara, Nārāyaṇa, and Datta.
Likewise [there were] Pāṇini, Piṅgala, and the author of the Bhāṣya. || 91 ||
Then there were Kātyāyana, the brahmin Patañjali, Garga, Guru, Gīṣpati, Gautamīśa, the sage Jājali, Kaśyapa, Gālava, the twice-born Saubhari, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, and Kaṇva. || 92 ||
Dvita, Ekata, Jātūdbhava, and Ghana; Kardama’s son was Kardama; likewise Bhārgava, Kautsaka, and Aruṇa.
The pure Pippalāda was the son of Mṛkaṇḍu. || 93 ||

Sapaila, as well as Jaimini, the excellent Satsumantu, Gāṅgala, Sphoṭageha, and Phalāda—the Brahmin who was always honored, the lord of sages who possesses all forms, the immortal destroyer of great delusion—were there from of old. (94)
Praised by the Lord of Sages, the bestower of knowledge to Śauri, the performer of great sacrifices, worthy of worship with the bath of clarified butter,
always giving sacrificial fees, and possessing royal gifts from kings.
He is the giver of joy to Vraja and the one who showed him the house in Dvārakā. || 95 ||

The bestower of great knowledge and the giver of sons to Devakī, he was worshipped by the Asuras and honored by the army of the lord of serpents; always bringing joy to Phālguna (Arjuna), he presided over the marriage of Subhadrā and bestowed elephants and horses while showing honor to his vehicles.
Bhūmānanda, employed by the King of Mithilā,
the twice-born, and supported by the Brahmins, quickly stood ready;
he was a master of action, an instructor in both the world and the Vedas for the people of Mithilā.
He who always lies upon Śeṣa is praised by the words of the Vedas.
Surrounded by Brahmins during his examination, he was entreated by Bhṛgu while holding the chowries; he is the slayer of Daityas, the protector of Īśa,
and the friend of Arjuna who strikes down pride.
Likewise, he who grants a son to a Brahmin shall go to the divine abode. || 98 ||

Residing in the monastery, his body adorned with mādhavī vines, he was as delightful as a great forest fire that has consumed the delusions of others; he was indeed King Ugrasena and Akrūra of the Yadu clan.
Likewise, Uddhava, Śūrasena, and Śūra [were born]. (99)
Hṛdīka, Satrājit, the immeasurable Gada, Sāraṇa, Sātyaki, Devabhāga,
as well as Mānasa, Sañjaya, and Śyāmaka.
Vṛka, Vatsaka, Devaka, and Bhadrasena. || 100 ||
King Ajātaśatru, Jaya, the sons of Mādrī, Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, and Pāṇḍu whose eye was wisdom;
likewise Śaṃtanu, Devavrata (Bāhlīka), Bhūriśravas, Citravīrya, and Vicitravīrya. || 101 ||
Śala, Duryodhana, Karṇa,
and the son of Subhadrā, the celebrated Viṣṇurāta—
he is Janamejaya, the Pāṇḍava and Kaurava.
Likewise, Hari possesses all splendor and is the embodiment of all forms.
For Pūrṇadeva, the supreme bridegroom devoted to the rāsa-līlā and possessing a divine form, has come to Vraja with Rādhā;
seated upon his chariot, he reveals the various regions of Navadvīpa.
Mahāmānada, Gopaja, and Viśvarūpa. || 103 ||
Sananda, Nanda, Vṛṣa, Vallabheśa, Sudāman, Arjuna, Saubala,
Toka, Kṛṣṇāṃśuka, and he who is known as Sadviśālarṣabha.
Sutejasvika, Kṛṣṇamitra, and Varūtha. || 104 ||

The Lord of Kuśa, the Lord of the Forest, likewise the Lord of Vṛndāvana, the Sovereign Lord of Māthura, the Lord of Gokula; He who is always with the herds of cows, the Lord of Cows, the Lord of the Gopīs, then Govardhana, the Lord of the Cowherds, and the Lord of Kanyaka. || 105 ||
Hari, the Supreme Person, is indeed beginningless; he is devoid of qualities, of the nature of light, and free from effort.
He is eternally changeless and transcends the phenomenal world.
He is Truth, He is Full, He is the Supreme Lord, and He is Subtle. || 106 ||
Likewise, in Dvārakā, he was the performer of the horse sacrifice by the king who was his grandson— the remover of the earth's burden—
and again in Śrī Vraja, he was the performer of the Rāsa dance.
Hari is the husband of Rādhā and of the gopīs. || 107 ||
He is eternally one yet manifold, his limbs filled with radiance, the creator of *yogamāyā*, and the conqueror of time.
He is the clear-sighted one whose form is the *mahat-tattva*; born as the progenitor, he is the immutable foundation, the primordial sprout in the form of a tree.
Indeed, that very ego (ahaṅkāra), abiding in its modified state, is the agent, being both taijasa and tāmasa.
Salutations to the quarters, the wind, the sun, Varuṇa, the Aśvins, Agni, Śakra, Upendra, and Mitra.
The ear, skin, sight, nose, tongue, speech, the hands, the genitals, the anus, and the feet, together with their functions;
as well as earth, ether, water, air, and fire; and likewise form, taste, smell, sound, and touch. (110)
He is the conscious mind, the intellect, the Virāṭ, and likewise Kāla in the form of Time; he is Vāsudeva, the creator of the universe, whose limbs are the elements.
Likewise, lying within the cosmic egg with Śeṣa, he is the primordial incarnation, the Lord of Ramā, possessing a thousand forms. || 111 ||
The lotus-born creator of the world, the performer of actions,
likewise born from the navel-lotus, of divine complexion,
the poet, the maker of the worlds, the maker of time, and the one whose form is the sun.
A blink of an eye, a birth, and the end of a year—these are [the durations of] the greater [kalpas]. || 112 ||

The lunar day, the weekday, the asterism, the yoga, the ascendant, the month, the ghaṭī, the kṣaṇa, the kāṣṭhikā, the muhūrta, the watch (yāma), the planets, the night, the day, and the son of a god situated in the garland of asterisms; || 113 ||
The Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali ages constitute one thousand [years]; therein lies a Manvantara. Dissolution, preservation, and creation [occur] within that, as does a Parārdha.
The two-syllabled one, whose form is Brahman, brings about constant origination. || 114 ||
Likewise, there is the creation of Rudra, the creation of Kumāra,
the creation of the Sage, the creation of the Devas, and the primordial (prākṛta) creation;
as well as the Śruti, the Smṛti, the hymn of praise, and thus the Purāṇa.
The science of archery, sacrifice, and the science of music. || 115 ||
Vidhātṛ, Nārāyaṇa, Sat-kumāra, Varāha, as well as Nārada, Dharmaputra, and the sage Datta, the son of Kardama; [these are the forms].
That sacrifice was Amara, Nābhija, and Śrīpṛthu. || 116 ||
And Sumatsya, Kūrma, Dhanvantari, as well as Mohinī, the majestic Nārasiṃha,
the twice-born Vāmana, and the form of Reṇukā’s son.
The sage Vyāsadeva is the author of the Śruti-stotra. || 117 ||
The incarnation of the moon from the ocean of the science of archery,
the lord of Sītā, the remover of the world’s burden, the enemy of Rāvaṇa, the king who built the bridge, and the striker of the lord of monkeys.
The lord of the Raghavas is a performer of great sacrifices and is fierce. || 118 ||
Balarāma, Kṛṣṇacandra, Kalki, the destroyer of the Kali age, the renowned Buddha, Haṃsa, and likewise Aśva;
the lord of sages, Ajita, the Lord Vaikuṇṭhanātha, Amūrti, and the Avatāra of the Manvantara. (119)
The illustrious Manu Gajoddhāraṇa was the son of Brahmā; Nṛpendra, born of Duṣyanta, was of a generous disposition.
Thus have been seen, heard of, or become [the kings], as well as those yet to be—those who are stationary and those who move, the small and the great. (120)
Thus has been declared the thousand names of Hari, the Lord of Rādhikā, in the *Bhujaṅgaprayāta* meter; indeed,
a twice-born man should always recite them with devotion.
One shall become one who has accomplished the goal, possessing the very nature of Kṛṣṇacandra.
That which is always dear to the Vaiṣṇavas and auspicious indeed shatters the great heap of sins—
namely, this [festival] occurring on the day of Rāsa-rākā in the month of Āśvina, and likewise specifically during the Kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī.

Likewise, having worshipped it in four ways on the full moon day of the month of Caitra, or on the auspicious eighth day of Rādhā in the month of Bhādra, one who recites this with devotion becomes excellent and bestows perfect liberation. || 123 ||
One should recite it in Kṛṣṇapura, or in Vṛndāvana, or in Vraja, or in Gokula, or at Vaṃśīvaṭa,
or at a banyan tree, or in Kṣaya, or on the bank of the Yamunā.
That devotee then goes to the abode of Goloka. || 124 ||
With a spirit of devotion, one should worship Hari everywhere on this earth— whether in a house or in a forest; for Hari never leaves such a devotee for even a moment.
Mādhava Kṛṣṇacandra will become easily submissive. || 125 ||
It must always be kept secret, always kept secret, always kept secret with great effort by the devotees;
the thousand names of Hari must not be disclosed.
In this manner, one must never give to a lecherous person. || 126 ||
In whatever house this book may reside, there the primordial Lord of Rādhikā shall dwell;
likewise, the six supernatural powers (ṣaḍguṇas), the twelve perfections (siddhis), and the thirty characteristics (lakṣaṇas) shall all come forth.
Thus ends the fifty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Thousand Names of Śrī Kṛṣṇa," in the Aśvamedha-khaṇḍa of the illustrious Garga-saṃhitā.
Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
The illustrious Garga said: Having heard this thousand names of Kṛṣṇa from the mouth of Vyāsa,
that lord of the Yādavas worshipped him with devotion and fixed his mind upon Kṛṣṇa.
Then, having granted his audience to Bahulāśva and Śrutadeva in Mithilā, Kṛṣṇa returned to the city of Dvārakā.
Thereupon, all the Pāṇḍavas, together with their wife Draupadī,
departed from Dvārakā and wandered from forest to forest.
O King, having completed their forest exile as well as their period of living incognito,
they all remained in the city of Virāṭa together with their armies.
Then all the Kauravas, though entreated even by Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
did not grant them half of the kingdom, nor even half of that half.
Having learned of the battle between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kauravas, Janārdana became disarmed during his journey; meanwhile, Bala slew Sūta and Balvala.
Then, having entered Kurukṣetra, the field of dharma,
all the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas waged war against one another.
Through the grace of Kṛṣṇa, victory indeed belonged to the Pāṇḍavas;
and all the Kauravas, having committed sins, perished in the Bhārata war.
Thereafter, Dharma reigned for nine years;
he performed three horse-sacrifices, by which the king became purified.
Then, O King, by the will of Kṛṣṇa, it is said that once in Dvārakā,
a great curse from the Brahmins befell all the Yādavas.
Then the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa recounted the supreme Śrīmad Bhāgavatam to Uddhava, who had sought refuge in him, while they were at the holy fig tree (Aśvattha).
Then a mutual conflict arose among the Yādavas;
they were indeed slain at Prabhāsa by means of various kinds of weapons.
Balarāma, having abandoned his human body, went to his divine abode;
seeing that the gods had arrived there, Hari vanished from sight.
Having gone to Vraja, Hari, the lover, met Nanda, Yaśodā, and Rādhikā,
as well as the cowherds and cowherd-maids, and spoke with affection to his own beloveds.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
"Go, Nanda and Yaśodā, casting aside the notion that he is your son, [go] to Goloka, the supreme abode, together with the inhabitants of Gokula. (15)
First, the terrible Kali age will arrive, which brings suffering;
in that age, mortals will undoubtedly become sinners. (16)
There is no restriction regarding male or female, nor likewise for the social classes;
therefore, go quickly to my supreme abode, which removes old age and death.
While Śrī Kṛṣṇa was speaking thus, there appeared a most wonderful chariot,
five yojanas in width and five yojanas in height.
Resembling a diamond in its stainless purity, adorned with pearls and jewels,
it was joined by nine hundred thousand palaces and lamps made of gems.
It had two thousand wheels and two thousand horses;
it was covered with fine cloth and surrounded by ten million female companions.
The cowherds, filled with joy, beheld him who had come from Goloka;
in that interval, he emerged from the body of Kṛṣṇa.
O King, the four-armed Lord, resembling ten million Cupids, the glorious Master of the Universe, held the conch and discus, together with Lakṣmī. || 22 ||
Mounting his beautiful chariot, the Blessed Lord Hari, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, in the form of Viṣṇu, quickly proceeded toward the Ocean of Milk.
O King, having mounted Garuḍa with Lakṣmī, he departed for Vaikuṇṭha;
thereafter, Hari became the two sages Kṛṣṇa and Nara-Nārāyaṇa.
For the welfare of men, Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself, the most perfect one, accompanied by Rādhā, set out for Badrikāśrama.
The Lord of the Universe ascended the vehicle that had come from Goloka,
as did all the cowherds headed by Nanda, and the women of Vraja headed by Yaśodā.
Having cast off their bodies there, they became possessed of divine forms;
and the Blessed Lord Hari, having placed Nanda and the others upon his divine chariot, [departed].
Accompanied by Gokula, the cowherd quickly departed for Goloka;
having gone beyond the cosmic eggs, he beheld the river Virajā.
Having seen Mahāloka, which bestows happiness and destroys suffering, upon the lap of Śeṣa,
he descended from his chariot together with the inhabitants of Gokula.
Accompanied by Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa entered while beholding the imperishable banyan tree,
the excellent mountain Śataśṛṅga, and likewise the glorious circle of the rāsa dance.
Then he went some distance to the glorious forest of Vṛndāvana,
which is endowed with twelve groves and surrounded by trees that grant all desires.
It was joined by the Yamunā river, adorned with the spring breeze,
filled with clusters of flowering groves and thickets, and surrounded by cowherds and cowherdesses.
Then, when the abode had previously become empty and Śrī Kṛṣṇa had arrived, a great roar of "Victory! Victory! arose in Śrī Goloka.
Then, having ascended the funeral pyre out of grief,
all the women, including Devakī and the others, went to the world of their husband along with the Yadu wives.
Having pacified himself from his grief through the knowledge of the Gītā, he performed the funeral rites for his kinsmen whose lineages had been lost. (35)
Arjuna, having returned to his own city, spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira;
that king, together with his brothers and his wife, went to heaven.
O tiger among kings, leaving behind the home of the Lord of Śrī Rukmiṇī, the ocean flooded Dvārakā along with Raivata.
Even today, the cry is heard at the gate of Dvāravatī regarding Hari:
"Whether ignorant or learned, a Brāhmaṇa is my own body. (38)
Viṣṇusvāmī, an incarnation of the sun-god, will go to the great ocean at the beginning of the Kali age,
and having brought forth the image of Hari, he will establish it in Dvāravatī.
O lord of kings, those men who behold that Lord of Dvārakā in the Kali age all attain their purpose upon going there.
Whoever hears this account of Hari’s ascent to Goloka and the liberation of the Yadus and the cowherds is released from all sins.
Thus ends the sixtieth chapter, titled "The Ascent of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa to Goloka," in the Aśvamedha-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā.
Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Vajranābhi said:
O Brahmin, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, is beyond primordial nature (prakṛti);
you should explain to me how his form is dark blue. || 1 ||
O Brahmin, sages such as you understand the deeds of Hari;
likewise, we do not [understand those] of the god Kṛṣṇa, for we are deluded by karma.
Sūta said:
O sage, having heard these words and being thus praised by him,
that compassionate knower of reality spoke in reply for the sake of [attaining] the knowledge of reality.
Garga said:
O lord of sages, the gods have described Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa as dark-complexioned, for He is the very embodiment of the erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra-rasa);
indeed, due to His mass of loveliness and His brilliance, the form of Hari is truly dark and beautiful.
Just as the dark form of a jar is seen from afar, so too is this [darkness] in the pit of the river;
or it is like the great, dark-blue form of the sky.
And the water and the sky are neither brilliant nor black. || 5 ||
Just as a dark hue appears upon a washed cloth due to the nature of another object,
so too do the virtuous describe the dark form of Hari because of His disposition toward the playful amorous sports of ten million Cupids.
Vajranābhi said:
"O best of sages, by your word my doubt has vanished;
O Brahmin, the terrible Kali age will soon come upon the earth."
O Sage, tell me what kind of mortals will exist in that [age];
for you know the future, therefore I bow down to you. (8)
The Lord of the World remains for ten thousand years of the Kali age;
half of that time is occupied by the waters of the Ganges, and half of that by the village deities.
Then all men will become sinners, deluded by the Kali age;
they shall all go to hell and be short-lived.
The Brahmins will give their own daughters to other Brahmins for a price,
and the greedy Kshatriyas will even kill their own daughters.
Vaiśyas, intent on the property of Brahmins, will engage in fraudulent trade;
and Śūdras, through association with Mlecchas, will defile the Brāhmaṇas.
Brahmins devoid of sacred learning, Kṣatriyas deprived of their kingdom, Vaiśyas lacking wealth, and Śūdras—these indeed cause suffering to their protector. (13)
During the day, women were intent on sexual intercourse and ceased from righteous deeds; they acted according to their own whims, while men were lustful for women’s wombs.
Likewise, the worship of the ancestors, as well as of the Vedas, the officiating priests, Viṣṇu, the Vaiṣṇavas, Tulasī, and the cows. || 15 ||
Deluded by the Kali age, men will for the most part not act rightly;
they will be infatuated with courtesans, the wives of others, and the wealth of others.
It is said that all people will become of a single caste, equal to great Śūdras;
the earth will be devoid of crops due to the incessant rain of stones. 17.
A tree devoid of fruit, a river devoid of water, a king struck by his subjects, and subjects struck by their king—[all these are alike]. (18)
The king said:
"O best of Brahmins, you who are the most knowledgeable in all things high and low, tell me by what means will the liberation of living beings come to pass in the Kali age? (19)
Garga said:
Yudhiṣṭhira, Vikrama, as well as Śālivāhana,
Vijayābhinandana, and likewise King Nāgārjuna— 20.
Likewise, the Lord Kalki— these indeed are the Śakabandhis— who will establish righteousness as kings during the Kali age.
Yudhiṣṭhira became king, and those kings shall also become;
having indeed become universal monarchs (cakravartins), they will destroy unrighteousness.
Vāmana, Vidhi, Śeṣa, and Sanaka—these shall become twice-born brāhmaṇas in the Kali age for the sake of dharma and artha, according to the word of Viṣṇu. (23)
Viṣṇusvāmī is a portion of Vāmana; likewise, Mādhva is a portion of Brahmā;
Rāmānuja is a portion of Śeṣa; and Nimbārka is a portion of Sanaka. (24)
In the Kali age, these four purifiers of the earth shall appear as the propagators of the tradition in the year of Vikrama. (25)
Those mantras that are devoid of the traditional lineage (saṃpradāya) are remembered as being fruitless;
therefore, there must indeed be recourse to the traditional lineage even by men.
Wherever the story of Śrī Kṛṣṇa occurs, it brings about the destruction of evil;
[there,] by Vaiṣṇavas, eminent Brahmins, and those devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa.
In the Kṛta age, the region is defiled; in the Tretā, the village itself;
in the Dvāpara, the family is said to be defiled; but in the Kali age, the doer alone is defiled.
What one attains by meditating in the Kṛta age, by performing sacrifices in the Tretā, and by worshipping in the Dvāpara,
that one attains in the Kali age simply by chanting the name of Keśava.
That which is accomplished in ten years during the Kṛta age, and in a single year during the Tretā,
and in one month during the Dvāpara, is accomplished in a single day and night during the Kali age.
When the terrible Kali age has arrived, which is devoid of all righteousness, those mortals who are devoted to Vāsudeva have achieved their purpose; of this there is no doubt.
O King, those who indeed remember the names of Hari or cause others to remember them during the Kali age are certainly fortunate among men and have achieved their life's purpose.
The syllable *kṛṣi* signifies "all," and the letter *ṇa* signifies the "Self";
since the Supreme Brahman is the Self of all, He is therefore celebrated as Kṛṣṇa. (33)
Having recited the supreme Brahman, the essence of the Vedas, which is higher than the highest—
the two syllables "Kṛṣṇa," [meaning] "there is nothing higher, there is nothing higher"— 34.

A person full of desire shall dwell in the womb for as long as that, and undergo the torments of Yama for that long; likewise, a householder seeking enjoyment remains so only as long as he does not serve Kṛṣṇa.
Wealth, enjoyments, and kinsmen on this earth are truly transitory and unstable;
when renounced by oneself, they lead to happiness, but when made to be abandoned by others, they lead only to suffering. (36)
Having heard by chance this great censure, the wise man is liberated from all sins through the remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; otherwise, he shall go to the Raurava hell.
The Lord is not found in wood, nor in stone, nor in gold;
where there is devotion, there is Hari. Therefore, one should indeed cultivate devotion.
By whomsoever the two syllables "Kṛṣṇa" are uttered even once,
he has girded his loins for the journey toward liberation.
Disease among virtuous people, enmity, causing suffering to others, reviling the Vedas of the twice-born,
extreme anger, and bitter speech.
This is the sign of a man who has gone to hell. || 40 ||
For those who have come from heaven to this world of living beings, four signs always abide:
a devotion to giving and sweet speech.
Worship of the gods and honoring of Brahmins. || 41 ||
The king said:
"O Brahmin, among vows, what is the best? Among holy places, what is the greatest?
Among deities worthy of worship, who is the foremost? Tell us. (42)
Garga said:
"O delighter of the Yadus, Ekādaśī is indeed the most excellent among vows;
the Bhāgīrathī is the best among sacred fords; and the Vaiṣṇava is the foremost among devotees of the gods. (43)
Among the gods, Viṣṇu is the Lord; among those worthy of worship, the Śrī Guru.
Those who do not accept this truth fall into the Kumbhipāka hell.
The King said:
O Sage, O God who is my Guru, salutations to you! Out of your grace, please tell me the greatness of the Ekādaśī as well as that of other [days]. (45)
Garga said:
O delighter of the Yadus, I shall tell you everything; listen.
On the eleventh day (Ekādaśī), one must not eat food, nor likewise fruit.
O best of kings, if a man joyfully observes the Ekādaśī according to the prescribed rule,
then it shall yield its fruit for him.
Vrajanābhi said:
"O Lord, tell us in detail what the destiny becomes for those men who subsist on fruit alone on the day of Hari. (48)
The sage said:
One obtains the entire fruit as described through fasting;
by subsisting on fruits, the fruit would be half, and by water, it would be slightly less.
O Lord of Kings, having avoided all grains except for wheat and the like,
a man should joyfully subsist on fruit alone on the eleventh day.
O King, that lowest of men who eats food on the eleventh day becomes a Cāṇḍāla in this world, and after death, he attains a miserable state.
Curd, milk, as well as sweet [sweets], kūṭa, and karkaṭikā;
vāstūka, the root of the lotus, rasāla, and the jānakī fruit. (52)
The fruit of the Gaṅgā, the leaves of the nimba, and especially the pomegranate;
the śṛṅgāṭaka, the nāgaraṅga, rock salt, and the plantain fruit.
Āmrātaka, ginger, cotton, the fruit of the jujube tree, the rose-apple fruit, the myrobalan, the bitter gourd, and likewise the three types of kuśa grass. || 54 ||
Ratālū, sugar-cane, sugarcane stalks, as well as grapes and other such fruits that are pure; || 55 ||
O Indra among kings, one should eat only once on the day of Hari (Ekādaśī),
after the third watch has passed, and [only] a measure of a prastha or a pala.
Half [of the food] should be given to a twice-born man, and half should be for one's own meal;
one should consume water twice, and likewise fruit once.
Having worshipped Janārdana, that man who observes a vigil two or three times on the day of Hari [Ekādaśī] should do so. (58)
He subsisted on fruit, yet not even a single fruit was his;
for the sin that arises from eating grain over fifteen days—[that he incurred]. (59)
By fasting on the eleventh day (Ekādaśī), all that [sin] shall be dissolved;
indeed, one should observe the fast after giving food to a Brāhmaṇa.
Having heard her greatness, one is liberated from all sins; indeed,
by the vow of Ekādaśī, one seeking wealth obtains wealth, one seeking a son obtains a son, and one seeking liberation obtains liberation.
Thus ends the sixty-first chapter, titled "The Greatness of Ekādaśī," in the Aśvamedha-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga Saṃhitā.
Hari Om Tat Sat; may this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Garga said:
"He by whom difficult-to-digest austerity was performed in a previous birth quickly develops devotion to the Guru in this world. (1)
He who does not serve his guru, he who does not respect his own teacher, and he who, though capable, fails to do so, falls eternally into the Kumbhīpāka hell.
Seeing one who has gone forth [as a renunciant] but is devoid of devotion to the Guru, a man becomes a killer of a cow;
however, by bathing in both the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, he then becomes pure.
Wherever the disciple may obtain wealth, a tenth part of that household property must indeed be given to the guru; such is our tradition.
If a disciple eats that [food] by force and does not give it separately to his teacher, he goes to the Mahāraurava hell, deprived here of all pleasures. || 5 ||
O King, those who constantly perform the ninefold devotion toward Hari indeed cross the ocean of worldly existence with ease.
Relatives, learning, high status, physical beauty, and youth—
one should diligently avoid these five, for they are thorns to devotion.
O king of kings, those who with devotion receive the grace of Kṛṣṇa’s water from his feet shall become protectors of the earth; of this there is no doubt.
The Gaṅgā removes sin, the moon removes heat, and the wish-fulfilling tree removes wretchedness;
likewise, the company of the virtuous instantly removes sin, heat, and wretchedness.
The ancestors, intent on receiving the funeral rice-balls (piṇḍa), continue to wander in saṃsāra as long as no son devoted to Kṛṣṇa is born in their lineage.
Is he a guru? Is he a father? Is he a son? Is he a friend? Is he a king? Is he a kinsman? He who does not direct his mind toward Hari is none of these.

Those who take pride in their learning, wealth, homes, and arts; those whose minds are constantly fixed on beauty, wives, and children; and those who, desiring rewards, behold other deities—[all these are deluded].
Though living, they are as good as dead; they do not worship Keśava.
O best of kings, I have related before you the account of the horse-sacrifice of Sumeru and the deeds of Kṛṣṇa as told by Vyāsa.
O tiger among kings, by the mere hearing of which devotion to Kṛṣṇa will arise in men, removing their sorrow, delusion, and fear.
By this practice as well, a man obtains his desired fruit:
wealth, grain, a son, devotion, and likewise the destruction of enemies. (15)
Therefore, O Indra among kings, quickly worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the universe,
with devotion— whether at home or in the forest— having realized that the entire world is composed of mind.
O hero among men, may your life increase evermore like the nights of winter;
may you always be pleasant to behold for the worlds like the sun in winter;
may you always be exceedingly difficult for enemies to withstand like the waters of winter.
May your enemies also go to their destruction, like an autumnal lotus.
Sūta said:
Having heard this, Vajranābha was delighted and overwhelmed with love;
remembering the majesty of Kṛṣṇa, he bowed to his guru and then spoke.
I am blessed and my purpose is fulfilled by you, whose very soul is compassion;
having heard the majesty of Kṛṣṇa, our minds have become fixed upon Kṛṣṇa.
Sūta said:
Having spoken thus, the best of kings honored Garga Ācārya with perfumes, unbroken grains, flowers, garlands, and likewise with a lattice-work necklace.
With elephants, chariots, horses, palanquins, and mansions, as well as with loads of silver and loads of gold, O Śaunaka. (21)
Likewise, filled with joy, he honored him with jewels, villages, and his own self, as well as with circumambulations, prostrations, and the waving of lights (nīrājana) and other rites. || 22 ||
Then Garga, having risen and bestowed his blessing upon Vajra,
was honored by the king and departed accompanied by a sacrificial fee.
Having gone to the sacred ford named Viśrānti on the bank of the Yamunā,
the sage gave all his wealth to the Brahmins from Mathurā.
Then, following the words of Garga, Vajra performed the horse sacrifice at Mathurā with the lords of sages, just as the lord of Nāgapura had done.
Then he [worshipped] Dīrghaviṣṇu and Keśava in Mathurā,
Govinda in Vṛndāvana, and Harideva on Girīśvara.
Vajra established Gokuleśa in every Gokula and Bala at a distance of one yojana from Gokula; he also installed six images of Hari.
Furthermore, five other images of Bala were established within the circle of Vraja for the welfare of men; the joyful Vajra installed them. (28)
When four thousand and five hundred years have passed in the Kali age,
Śrīnātha will indeed manifest on the excellent mountain.
Viṣṇusvāmī, the embodiment of the Sun, will worship him in Vraja;
as will his disciples, beginning with Vallabha, and others who are masters of Gokula.
Having seen liberation through the Śrīmad Bhāgavata, Vajra Parīkṣit,
as well as the sages, set their minds on renouncing the kingdom out of dispassion.
Then the Vaiṣṇava Aupagavi arrived from the hermitage of Nara-Nārāyaṇa,
bearing upon his head the sandal of Kṛṣṇacandra.
Honored by the king with rising from his seat, offering a seat, and other marks of respect,
he joyfully recited the Śrīmad Bhāgavata at the tip of the diamond-throne.
Having heard the Bhāgavata from Uddhava, Vajra spoke with joy:
"O dear one, I previously heard it from Parīkṣit in an excellent assembly."
The discourse on Samādhi spoken by Vyāsa was described by Śukadeva, and it has been recounted by you as well; thus, I have indeed become one who has attained his purpose. (35)
Having spoken thus, Vajranābhi gave his own kingdom to Pratibāhu, and Uddhava departed for Goloka by means of a celestial chariot.
He ruled the kingdom righteously in Mathurā and in the south;
his son was Pratibāhu, and in the north was Janamejaya.
O Brahmin, the terrible Kali Yuga will arrive;
however, one means of sustenance is seen that destroys sin. (38)
As long as the Bhāgavata scripture exists, as long as the Lord of Gokula remains,
as long as Govardhana and the Gaṅgā endure, so long indeed shall the Kali Yuga not prevail.
O Sage, just as among the regions of the Bhāratas in Jambūdvīpa,
Mount Meru shines resplendent in the center, golden like a lotus flower.
Likewise, O great sage, in the Saṃhitā of the Goloka-khaṇḍa,
Mount Meru shines resplendent in the midst of the narrative of the horse-sacrifice.
By merely hearing this, even a Brahmin who has violated the preceptor’s bed, a woman, a king, or a father, or a killer of a cow, is liberated from all sins. (42)
A Brahmin obtains knowledge, and a Kshatriya likewise obtains a kingdom;
by listening [to this], a Vaishya obtains wealth, and a Shudra likewise obtains merit.
Just as the Gaṅgā is among rivers, as the Blessed One is among gods,
and as the King of Holy Places is among sacred sites, so indeed is this [Saṃhitā] among all Saṃhitās.
O Sage, by merely hearing this, the best of men attains satisfaction; he would not cling to other scriptures as he does to the Bhāgavata.
Therefore, O sages, for the sake of your own welfare, worship the lotus feet of the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who removes the suffering of his devotees. 46.
Śrī Garga said: Having heard this account of Hari’s deeds, the sages headed by Śaunaka,
with delighted minds, offered praise to the son of the Sūta.
O Viṣṇu, ocean of compassion, protect me, who am wretched and submerged in the ocean of saṃsāra, my limbs seized by the grasp of Time; salutations be unto you! 48.
O virtuous one, show us favor, for you are the beloved protector of those who are helpless;
act as our master does by granting fearlessness to the three worlds. (49)
Indeed, by the grace of the venerable Guru and through the service of the illustrious Madanamohana, my speech has been awakened; thus, the life-story of that Hari has been narrated.
May Vālmīki, Vyāsa, and others behold this brief poem of mine;
having seen it, you ought to forgive any offense. (51)
The glorious Mādhava, the Lord of Vraja, whose body is like a fresh cloud,
the husband of Rādhā, the Lord of the gods, the holder of the flute,
the destroyer of the afflictions of His devotees, the Supreme Reality, the infinite God.
I bow my head and mind with devotion to Kṛṣṇa. || 52 ||
There are two hundred and sixty-six verses concerning the beloved wives of the high-souled Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Meru of deeds, and eighty-three concerning those who are very dear to him. (53)
Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, titled "The Completion of Mount Sumeru," in the Aśvamedha-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garga-saṃhitā.
The Aśvamedha-khaṇḍa is completed; this work is finished. Hariḥ Oṃ Tat Sat. May it be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
